reviewText: La Madeleine has certainly become a beloved spot of mine since first moving to Albuquerque a couple of years ago. It features good food, quaint atmosphere, and friendly staff. I might actually be so bold as to say that I have never had a bad experience while dining in at La Madeleine. Though I often get the mouth-watering Chicken Pesto Pasta; my most recent visit saw me indulge on the Croque Monsieur sandwich. As is the case for most things on the menu, it was delicious and filling. Not to mention that the complimentary bread table near the fountain machine is a big plus. The restaurant is also consistently clean, which is always reassuring. Pastries are well presented and the restaurant does well to include calorie content information for all items. La Madeleine doesn’t get much human traffic despite being located in the busy uptown area; which is a shame as it has a lot to offer. With that said, I always look forward to my next visit and hope that if in the vicinity; you’ll choose to give it a chance as well.

reviewText: La Madeleine charged me 38$ to gatekeep and gaslight me. It was one of the worst experiences, period. I've been to this location before years ago, and this time I saw they had this "Croffle" and I thought I'd give it a try. My partner had the American Breakfast, and we had two drinks. I was charged $38.05, which I didn't think much of at the time. The drink dispenser was out of syrup on both Starry and Bubly Lime, but you couldn't tell till you drank it. The melon in fruit salad my order came with had been cut too near the rind but you couldn't tell till you ate it. They used to have fresh bread out as an appetizer, but that was gone too, though the butter and jam were still out. Unpleasant so far, but a pleasant meal could cover a lot of failures. Then my order was delivered. It was a single Croffle, no powdered sugar, with a 2oz plastic cup of syrup, and a strawberry cut in half that was an unhealthy shade of overripe. I took it back to the counter to ask if this was the right order, and the manager confirmed it was. I asked where the other Croffle was, and the lady looked me in the eyes and said it was two. I looked at her, then at the round Belgian waffle iron behind the counter. "Where's the powdered sugar and preserves?" She said I could pump my own from the condiment bar. That's the gaslighting. When King Solomon has handed a baby, he didn't cut it in half and say, "There, it's two babies." But La Madeleine seems to think that's how it works. The gatekeeping came into play when the manager returned with my sugared Croffle. She'd walked past a tub if sliced bread in plastic baggies. I asked her how much for the bread, since my meal was half the size the menu said. She said the bread was free and passed me some. Apparently, I had not met their complimentary loaf standards until I complained. The strawberry jam came from a ketchup pump and was mostly corn syrup with the consistency of catsup. The bread was not fresh and had some of that school lunch plastic bag smell and a stale, waxy texture. I can't figure out how my order came to 38$ and I wasn't given a receipt to check. If I hadn't been so pissed off by the point I tired it, I might have actually enjoyed the Croffle because it was tasty.

reviewText: We were shopping at Perkins Rowe and wanted to stop by for an early dinner. We've eaten here many times before and this, by far, was the worst experience ever. The restaurant was not very crowded so easy to find a table for the 3 of us. My wife and son ordered and I was last. My son is a growing teenager and has a huge appetite. Even though he's a kid, he has a man-sized appetite! All he wanted was pasta and butter. Easy enough, right? When it was my turn to order, I told the employee taking orders I have a gluten allergy. He then proceeded to scream throughout the kitchen: GLUTEN ALLERGY! I turned around and saw people standing behind me. I thought: could he not be a bit more discrete? It is no one else's business. I ordered a salad and he proceeded to scream to the kitchen staff: GLUTEN ALLERGY! While I appreciated his attention, I thought there could be a better way of handling this. I walked to the register to pay and found a table. When my son's food arrived, it was a kid's size serving of pasta. I think we counted how many pieces of penne were in the bowl. After he cleaned the bowl, he filled up on sourdough bread. After we ate, we went to the dessert section. No one there. I counted 4 employees standing approximately 4 feet away from me, I made eye contact with at least 2 of them. And no one acknowledged my presence or offered to help. I could have easily interrupted but thought, no, I wanted to see how long it would take before someone stopped the conversation long enough to see what I needed. Six minutes! A lady broke away from the group and she took my dessert order. She started to put my dessert in a box and I said, we're eating here. She proceeded to put my dessert in a "to go" box and I said, we're eating here. She handed me the "to go" box with my desserts. I had to ask her for 2 plates because we were eating here. I really hated giving her my cc to pay for these two desserts. It will be a very long time before we return here.

I think a lot of businesses forget how important and unforgettable an experience can be when customer service is impeccable. You never know what others are dealing with when they enter your establishment, and sometimes just being treated with a little kindness can make a world of difference to someone. Kudos to everyone here who worked yesterday between 11:45-3:45; they were some of the most pleasant people I've ever had the pleasure of interacting with, and as a PhD student who just needed a change of scenery and some food in order to focus on studying for an exam, they really did make my life a little bit less stressful.

reviewText: Great food and patient staff. I thought I was an average / semi intelligent person until I tried to figure out how to place an order/walk through their "buffet" line. So when you walk in there is a paper menu to grab to figure out what you want/create a line behind you. Then you get greeted by a staff member who isn't there to take your order. Then you walk down a buffet line of food clearly displayed that you don't order. Then you reach a cashier that will take your order. If you haven't forgotten your order at this point you are more clever than I. You place your order and get a wooden spoon with a number carved into it that...wait for it...a waiter brings your order to your table. Why not just be seated and be given a menu and order with waiter/waitress? The credit card receipt has a place for a tip... who gets that? the greeter? the cashier? The dude who brought my food? I'm telling ya, join the restaurant club of waiters and make this process much more efficient. 3 jobs wrapped into 1. When the place is crowded, this is a nightmare convoluted process. If this is how you order food in France I just saved a 1,000 plane ticket. No thank you. Viva la'Merica baby. Also the food is decent. 🇺🇸♾🥂😎

reviewText: I would like to say that, being from San Antonio, I have gone to LM locations quite often and been totally impressed. I took my friend to this location on a trip to Katy expecting a good time, and my friend and I left agreeing that it was the worst form of service we have ever experienced in our lives. First off, we went there in the evening ordering breakfast, something that is served all day. When explaining to the lady at the register what our orders were, she had to take the menu from us and look at it more clearly because she did not seem to know what we were ordering or have any real experience with the menu at all (my friend ordered an iced latte and a breakfast crepe, I ordered a yogurt parfait). Everything seemed very much like the whole staff had just started working at this location, and was falling apart at the seams. When my friend got her drink, they didn’t even bother to give her a straw. I had to go and get this for her. The man who we just saw sweeping And mopping with dirty water in the back was the one to give my friend her meal, something that immediately was a red flag for both of us. My meal did not come out for 30 minutes. During that time, I went to the bathroom, and instead of hearing any sort of music I just heard some sort of Rosetta Stone English to French translation segment over the speakers, some thing that was scary and left me feeling like I was in the twilight zone or something. After waiting much too long for my yogurt parfait, we summoned the guy who is sweeping over to our table, showed him the receipt, and explained that I was still waiting on my yogurt parfait. He apologized and left, returning with a parfait that was not what I ordered. Instead of being my seven dollar yogurt parfait, it was one of the tiny two dollar dessert parfaits that was displayed in a box in front of the cash register. By that point, my friend and I were stunned. I thought of going up and complaining, but didn’t think it be worth the effort. We left. My first thought was that the worker was deliberately trying to scam me out of 4-5 dollars, but then my friend and I came to the agreement that he just genuinely did not know the menu whatsoever. This happened on January 31, just a few days ago. My friend and I are able to laugh about it the best we can, but it’s still very surprising and concerning. Very disappointed.

reviewText: My how things have changed, not for the better. We've been eating at La Madeline for 20 years. My wife and I nearly always get the same thing regardless of which location we're at, the baked chicken and the bow tie pasta. Saturday we changed things up. We noticed they no longer sold the bow tie pasta - which was GREAT, so we chose items on their list of "New" entrees. My wife got Chicken Cordon Bleu Baked Pasta and I got the Ham and Swiss Crepe. We also got a "Gillette". I asked the server what it was and he said it's a hashbrown, to which I asked, so it's kind of like a hashbrown and he said, no, IT'S A HASHBROWN! We really love the place. I don't usually don't review a restaurant at less than a 3, if ever. Unless something very, very bad happened. Something very, very bad is happening to La Madeline. We were disappointed and sad. But let me first say this, service was fast, clean and the employees were polite and nice. I'll start with the Gillette. With tax and tip it's almost $4.00. Almost anywhere a hashbrown is half that price, but I wasn't so concerned about the price, I knew I was getting a hashbrown when I ordered it. I didn't expect it to be crunchy, as in almost chip a tooth crunchy on the outside, and almost creamy on the inside. Very weird, very awful That's not why they get the bad review though, maybe that's just the way French hash browns are supposed to be, I'm totally serious. The review is because of the entrees. My dish, in the photo, looked like it would be filling. When it arrived I realized it was served on a normal sized plate but the photo of the entree must've been taken on a plate just the next size larger than a saucer for a coffee cup because you could've quadrupled the order and it would have easily fit on my plate. Before I even had a bite I was disappointed with the small serving size but hoping that it would taste good. So much for wishful thinking. I was grateful that there was ONLY 2 small crepes because if there'd been 4 I wouldn't even have eaten the last 2. I don't know why I even ate 2., When I say they were bad, I don't mean spoiled bad, or cooked badly. I'm saying they were so salty it was ridiculous. The cheese did not have a good taste, the ham was about paper thin and allegedly there was chicken in there too, somewhere. I don't know if the cheese was the culprit, the ham or both. When I was leaving I spoke to an employee who will remain anonymous and mentioned the salt problem.. They said "everyone says the same thing. I personally think it's the ham so when I order it I tell the Chef no ham, use turkey". I would never order it again, ever, and we may never go back either. If the Gillette and crepe were the only problem I'd rate the meal as a 2, if I was generous. My wife's entree was very good sized, probably 15 times the volume of my entree. It was so big that I even remarked before we took a bite that we may have to share some of that because my meal is so small and we could take it home and get 3 more meals out of it. We ate about 20% of it and agreed, no doggy bad. It was awful with a capital A. If we'd taken it home it would have gone straight to the trash. Nothing spoiled, nothing cooked wrong, just way too salty and the cheese was not very good tasting cheese. The "diced ham" wasn't even diced, it was the same shredded paper thin salty ham that I had in my crepe. If we'd never been to La Madeline before and had this meal, I'm 100% positive we'd never, ever eat there again. The 2 entrees were really that awful. The current menu is a game changer. There is no way they do not know how bad those items are, they only need to try them. On top of that, when multiple employees remarked, when I politely expressed my concerns about those 2 entrees, "we know, I'm so sorry, everyone says the same thing". Such a shame, place isn't the same. Never eating there again.

reviewText: American Perspective: The food was wonderful, offering authentic European dishes like baguettes and croissants. The setting seemed authentic, but the "cappuccino" was not up to standard. The orange juice wasn't fresh as promised, and the croissant tasted store-bought. My girlfriend's egg was bland. The owner should visit France to understand authentic breakfast. Calling this place "French" feels inaccurate.

reviewText: Este fue un vuelo desde Veracruz a Cleveland con conexión en Aeropuerto de Dallas Forthworth. Vuelo casi con salida al medio día y llegada a Cleveland 11 pm, teniendo en cuenta dos horas adelante en Cleveland respecto del Puerto. Casi aterrizando en Dallas se presenta una caída del sistema de planeación de vuelos y hasta tal vez de sistema de gestión de la Torre de Control. La espera en plataforma fue grande, solo teníamos 3 horas para el siguiente vuelo, que reprogramado para las 9 pm. Existe un área de gestión social del aeropuerto que atiende a afectados por los vuelos. El vuelo se canceló y se programo para el siguiente día . Sin embargo a pesar de haber más de 2000 afectados , algunos alcanzamos a obtener por parte de la aerolínea una habitación de hotel con los traslados incluidos. No fue suficiente. El Taxista acabo con el tiempo disponible y después de un mega paseo en Dallas, en el finalmente acepto el error en su definición de ubicación del hotel, ya que algunos malandros se ocultan en el idioma. El aprendizaje es : 1) Evitar vuelos con conexión ya un poco tarde, y si no lo puedes evitar, entonces contrata una reserva en un hotel cercano al aeropuerto pero incluye en ese contrato la recogida en el aeropuerto de un vehículo del hotel. 2) Busca al área Social y lo más pronto posible al responsable de las operaciones de vuelo, a fin de asegurar la continuidad de tu vuelo. 3) Si no pudiste realizar la reserva de habitación y el taxi, mejor quedate en el aeropuerto y presiona todo el tiempo para tu vuelo.4) Vital tener un contrato de servicios de viajes al extranjero para el apoyo logístico de todo tu viaje. Importante no pierdas la calma y evita salir del aeropuerto a buscar el hotel que la aerolínea te ofrece, no es culpa de ellos , los del hotel abusan también. Es un poco más caro asegurar tu tranquilidad. Excelente trabajos de Manager de operaciones Santosh, desgraciadamente el resto del personal de piso no tiene el mismo compromiso que el con los usuarios de la aerolínea.

reviewText: I have officially reached the seventh level of hell (aka DFW). I haven't flown American in years so, I have managed to avoid DFW, but due to where my parents recently moved, I was "forced" to try American again. I was mid flight heading to a layover at DFW when we are told that DFW has lost radio communication. Apparently a sign that we are truly becoming a third world country. We ended up arriving at DFW and waited on the tarmac for over half an hour, and the temperatures reached at least the 1st level of hell. We eventually deplane and god forbid you have to go to the bathroom at DFW. At most modern airports the bathrooms are within easy sight of a gate when you land. Not at DFW. After a long walk, I finally found one and the sign outside says the next restroom is 4 minutes away. Inside, 2 of the urinals are broken and everything looks like it hasn't been updated in 30 years. The flooring in the terminal is tiles, and there are cracks plus metal plates in spots to cover some gaps in the tile or something. The food? It sucks as well, and is expensive. I could deal with the price if it was at least decent food. The bread on my sandwich was so stale, it crumbled when you bit into it. The design of this airport is ridiculous. A kindergartener could have come up with a more logical design. Everything is just mashed together. On top of that the HVAC kinda sucks and there are parts that are warm and others that are cool. At one point, I was by a window that had a brown film that you couldn't even see clearly through anymore. Felt like everything was old and dumpy. Customer service: American has a 3-4 agents to handle thousands of angry and stranded travellers. Talked to one woman in the line and she was there for 2 hours and still hadn't gotten to the front of the line. You'd think American would want their home base to be a shining example of a modern airport, but instead it just reminds me of why I don't want to fly American if I don't have to. P.S. The Uber pickup was also somewhat confusing compared to most other airports. Most other airports it is much clearer where you have to go exactly for the pick-up.

My favorite item to order is the chicken friand. It's usually my go-to entree. Last night (8/8/25), we decided to do a dinner and a movie at home. Since La Madeleine is just down the street from us (like less than a mile), we decided to treat ourselves. We placed the order from home, waited until about 15 minutes for the order to be prepared and then got there, picked it up and brought it home. I opened my chicken friand container and thought "Wow, this looks a little dark." As soon as I sank my knife into it, the pastry basically exploded, crumbled and fell apart. I could not draw my knife through the bottom of the pastry. It was hard and clearly burned. I thought maybe the sauce would make it edible. I just could not eat it. The pastry is what makes L.M. so notable for and this was far, far from that. It was INCREDIBLY disappointing, especially when the item was not cheap. On the plus side, the ham and cheese pastry we picked up for breakfast was edible. But my most favorite dish was burned and quite old. Big time fail, La Madeleine.

I stood there at the soup counter staring at my tomato bisque, already prepared and sitting in a ramekin waiting for my sandwich so I didn't ask for my soup even though I saw it there, a woman behind me who looked like she might have been a manager or something was in a meeting with an older gentleman and asked me if there was anything I needed, I politely told her that I was still waiting on my soup and sandwich, she went back to her conversation and I stood there for another 5 minutes and then she prompted me again and asked me what I was standing there waiting on and I reminded her my soup and sandwich and she asked the girl who was heavy on the attitude to give me my soup and then told me my sandwich would be a few more minutes, I was confused because normally the half sandwich and soup are serve together, as for me personally I really like dipping my sandwich in my soup so I couldn't eat the two separately, and by the time my sandwich had been delivered my soup was lukewarm/ room temp... It wasn't my most favorite experience with la Madeleine but I know them to be an exceptional company with exceptional food so I'm just counting this as a one-off. As for the atmosphere in my opinion the location on Cherry Street had the atmosphere nailed, and the service of an all day French cafe, but as we all have to sever now without that location, the one in Tulsa hills is the only one we have access to, and I feel like they still have a lot of work to do on the atmosphere and the vibe that the people who work their give off.

reviewText: This is I think my favorite La Madeleine of all the ones I’ve been to. Here I find friendly and very hardworking people. Lorena brings out our meals with a smile. And she takes good care of the dining room, along with Rosita. The managers are friendly and they help out to make sure everything is working smoothly and everyone is taken care of. I always enjoy the meals and they are priced affordably. There are so many options in the menu to try so food is never boring. Add to that the fact that they change it up a bit to offer special seasonal meals that are delicious. They offer a Cafe Sampler where you get to choose a combination of 3 items (salad, soup, fruits, etc.). They also have amazing salads and sandwiches that you can order whole or in combination with a side of your choice. They have a huge dining area, including an outside seating. Beverage & bread counters are in the dining area so you can freely serve yourself and go for seconds, if you wish. And they’re great at serving fresh coffee. The bakery offers tempting desserts. Make sure to get their La Madeleine app and sign up for their rewards - that way you make every visit count towards free items or special offers.

reviewText: I hadn't been to this kind of restaurant in a long time, so I didn't remember how it worked. No one asked if we had been there before or explained how it all worked. The first person who took our order was nice. The second person who rang us up didn't speak to us. By the time I put my card back in my wallet, she had left to go back to the front register. I didn't know that I would have to get my own drinks, silverware, and the potato galette. We didn't see her put the galette on the counter, so we weren't sure if it was ours. I was waiting to ask her for clarification, but she never came back. We figured it out after we'll sat down like a bunch of confused little goobers. The food was okay. The potato galette was cold and was a little too strong on the onion flavor for me, so I didn't eat more than a few bites. The omelet (bacon, bell peppers, cheddar) and croissant were good. My husband got the croissant sandwich with sausage, which he said was okay. The lady who brought us our food was sweet. She was chatting with a regular customer next to us and having a really pleasant interaction, but one of the managers interrupted their conversation mid-sentence and told her to get back to work. It was awkward. I don't know if it was all worth the cost, so we probably won't be coming back.

I wasn't asked if I even wanted a replacement item or a refund, instead they just grabbed whatever they felt was fine and tossed it into my order instead. I was missing a 4-pc mini baguette and the sauce for my chicken friand(!! Kind of part of the dish??). If you order takeout, please be aware and double check your orders before you leave the building because you'll likely end up like I did. What we got definitely wasn't worth the $60 we paid.

reviewText: L'Aeroporto Internazionale di Dallas è indubbiamente enorme, con una notevole quantità di terminal. Tuttavia, la connessione tra di essi è ben organizzata, rendendo gli spostamenti relativamente agevoli. Già all'arrivo, le procedure per l'uscita verso l'esterno sono state veloci, e abbiamo trovato comodissimi i frequenti autobus che in pochi minuti collegano l'aeroporto ai centri di noleggio auto. Un punto decisamente positivo per chi, come noi, aveva bisogno di ritirare un veicolo. All'interno, l'ambiente è molto pulito e tecnologicamente avanzato, con un'ampia varietà di negozi e ristoranti capaci di soddisfare tutti i gusti. Abbiamo apprezzato la presenza dei totem informativi digitali, utili per orientarsi e trovare ciò che si cerca. Tuttavia, proprio questi totem sono stati la nota leggermente stonata della nostra esperienza. Abbiamo riscontrato due informazioni errate che hanno un po' condizionato la nostra permanenza. In un caso, un ristorante veniva indicato come chiuso, mentre in realtà era aperto. In un altro, i prezzi visualizzati nel menu digitale erano sensibilmente inferiori a quelli che abbiamo poi effettivamente pagato al ristorante. Consiglio vivamente di aggiornare le informazioni presenti sui totem interattivi, in quanto queste imprecisioni possono causare confusione e una percezione negativa, seppur minima, dell'efficienza dell'aeroporto. Nonostante questo piccolo neo, l'Aeroporto Internazionale di Dallas rimane una struttura efficiente, ben organizzata e dotata di numerosi servizi. Con una maggiore attenzione all'accuratezza delle informazioni digitali, potrebbe facilmente raggiungere le cinque stelle.

Each bite was a true delight, particularly the muffins and croissants. And, of course, no breakfast would be complete without a steaming cup of coffee. reviewText: We had a pretty bad experience there today. We ordered our food and were told it would be around 15 minutes. 35 minutes later we got a third of our order. We finally get our soups 10 minutes later and they were cold, as was my husband's au jux. Add 10 more minutes and my mom hadn't gotten her main dish yet. Waiter came around to say it would be another 5 minutes until it was ready. My mom waited almost an hour when she had been told her food would be ready in 12 to 14 minutes. It was all together really bad service but I'll give it 3 stars because the manager was very sorry and gave us $30 in gift cards to apologize. I've been to other La Madeleines before and had never experience bad service. I'll give this one the benefit of the doubt and try again another time. Hopefully they just had a rough evening or were maybe understaffed, so we'll see. I'll update my review the next time I come.

reviewText: Today I renewed my vow to never return to this la Madeleine. I was there at about 10:30 this morning, hoping to take a couple of chocolate croissants home. There are two cash registers there, one for the café, the other for the bakery. One customer was at the café register paying for his meal. I was the only customer at the bakery register. There were 5 workers milling around (in addition to the one for the café). They walked by me, glanced, and continued ignoring me. I'm 6' 3", 225 pounds, but apparently invisible. After several minutes of being ignored, I waved my arms above my head and shouted for all to hear, that I was there. One worker ambled over and asked what I wanted. I said, "how about 'good morning', or 'how can I help you', or 'Happy Thanksgiving'". I got the equivalent of a 'whatever'. I then ordered the overpriced croissants. I paid cash, but she forgot to give me change, then could not open the register without a manager. The manager must be a mute, because she didn't say anything either. I bought a package of 16 pan au chocolate at the neighboring Costco for less than the two from la Madeleine, took them home and popped two in the air fryer. They were as flakey and chocolatey as the ones from la Madeleine. Several of the 'workers' looked like they were in training, although customer service does not appear to be part of the syllabus. Maybe the manager is training them to ignore the customers that pay their salaries.

reviewText: We are regular customers at this Location on Sam Houston Parkway around the Memorial Area. This restaurant chain is unfortunately on the downfall. Here are the reasons why. They no longer put the chicken in the foil wrap, the chicken that is used for the chicken Caesar salad was cold, and not warm/hot like they used to do it when they wrapped it around in tin foil and had it in the warmer section. The Dressing portion that they provided with the salad was half-filled, how in the world is that enough dressing for the whole chicken Caesar salad? They are being selfish on the salad dressing, so its pretty much obvious they are trying to cut down costs, but these cut downs impact the user experience. Third, The Chicken Friand was really dry, even with the mushroom sauce added on. The Chicken Friand itself is super dry and the chicken isn't as tender and soft as it usually is. I have been a customer at La Madeline since I was in my high school years, I am 38 and now and this will be my first negative review for the restaurant. I hope its not going to be a Snowball effect and hope it was just a bad experience on a bad day.

reviewText: My wife and I went to La Madeleine for breakfast because we had been given a gift card. I ordered an omelette and asked if they had gluten free bread option and they said no. I then asked if I could substitute something like fruit for the croissant and they said no. If you go to Denny's they have both gluten free muffins (which are very nice) and they will substitute fruit in place of bread. My wife also asked for a substitute in her order and they said no. Apparently there are no substitutions at all! When we went to pay we were told their gift card reader was not working. There was no sign out saying that the card reader was not working. You think the manager might have apologized and offered some sort of compensation, but La Madeleine does not do anything like this apparently. The food was OK but nothing special. For the same money you can have a lot better omelette at Denny's or IHOP, with much better service. There are admittedly some distinct lunch/dinner options like the caesar salad and the tomato basil soup which are worth going to La Madeleine for. My wife and I really like the ambiance at La Madeleine, like we always have. But the food is not all that special and the service stinks. We will use up our gift cards (assuming they get their card reader working) but we probably won't go back after that. Or if we do it definitely won't be for breakfast.

reviewText: ⭐☆☆☆☆ I had a very frustrating experience at DFW Airport on March 25, 2025, around 3:30 PM at Gate E30. Only after I insisted did she call, and the rep walked her through finding the reservation. She then blamed us for “splitting” the tickets due to a name correction we never made ourselves. After harshly handing me the boarding passes, she told us to leave. When I asked if she could seat them together, she refused to assist, said there was a fee, and told me to use the app—even though no one else was waiting. Completely unacceptable customer service. If this is how passengers are treated when it’s not busy, I worry about how they’re treated during peak times.

reviewText: From the moment you step into this warm and inviting cafe, you're transported to a quaint French bistro that's both cozy and elegant. The tomato basil soup is a must-try, with its rich, velvety texture and perfectly balanced flavors. While the Caesar salad was just okay, it's still a refreshing and light complement to any meal. Moving on to the entrees, the creamy pesto pasta with shrimp is a standout dish that's both creamy and flavorful, with perfectly cooked shrimp adding a touch of sweetness to the dish. The chicken la Madeleine is another highlight, cooked to perfection and served with a delectable side of creamy mashed potatoes. And let's not forget about dessert! The creme brulee is an indulgent treat that's both creamy and satisfying, with the perfect amount of caramelized sugar on top. And of course, no trip to La Madeleine is complete without trying their signature Madeline cookies, which are the perfect sweet ending to any meal. Overall, La Madeleine in Mockingbird, Dallas is a must-visit destination for those seeking a taste of France in the heart of Texas. I would definitely return to this location. Food 4/5 Service 4/5 Atmosphere 5/5 Parking 5/5 Cleanliness 4/5

reviewText: I would like to give this place a one star review, but because I was partially at fault here I feel like have to give them a two. I was on my way to my appointment when I realized that I was going to be late (my fault). I called four minutes after my appointment time to let them know that I was a few minutes away, they put me on hold for two minutes, at which point I had pulled into the parking lot. When the woman came back to the phone she notified me that the doctor had left for the day 'just two seconds ago'. Seriously, I called FOUR minutes after my appointment time, and you're telling me the doctor had already LEFT!? Now I know late is late, and it's rude and annoying. However, I have spent many years in an industry that required me to schedule appointments and deal with late and on time clients alike. I never dared to consider a client a 'no show' any sooner than 10 minutes after their appointment time, often 15 minutes was required. I was so disappointed and upset. I've had a miserable eye twitch for the last 4 weeks, and the thought of having to deal with it for another week or more while I try to find another doctor and make an appointment just makes me want to cry. Like I said, I shouldn't have been late, hence the two star. I'd like to give them a one star rating.

reviewText: I am a very frequent customer of this restaurant for a pretty good while for about a year. I always order through Uber eats to save time and I have always enjoyed their food especially the sandwiches. However recently starting about a month ago, they decided to switch the bread of the sandwiches to a much smaller size. Mind you that they have always had decent proportions in terms of the bread size since you can choose half or whole in size when you are ordering the sandwich. It always was about a good 9 to 10 inch sandwich for the whole portion to which you can even save the other half for later. Now it is literally just a 6 inch sub cut in half with another type of bread. Absolutely ridiculous. I’m not sure what made them to do this decision, whether it’s for financial reasons but it’s a poor excuse knowing that this is a chain restaurant throughout the United States. I’m not sure if it’s other restaurants also doing the same thing so I’m going to test out the one up in Dallas when I go there this weekend for the Fourth of July to see if they are doing the same thing. Or if it’s just the location of the Huebner Oaks shopping Center. Big disappointment! Especially being that the restaurant is close to me and other business areas nearby.

reviewText: As much as I would like to give this place 5 stars I rather share in hopes of management improving to keep La Madeleine as a well loved restaurant with great service, atmosphere and food. I think the location on champion forest is much better, except I live closer to this one. I can only hope new things are in-store for this location on 290 frwy and 1960. Update to my last review: Today is Oct 30, 2018 I can't say it was my review that made a difference, but all that matters is that La Madeleine at the NW frwy did make great changes to the restroom issue. Today I walked in the ladies room, no sticky mopped floor, no bad smell, I think they added this furniture piece as well and hung a few frames on the wall. It looks better and smells better, makes me happy to see this and that maybe "my review " made a difference. Thanks La Madeleine!! *Also, a few weeks ago we came in on a cooler morning and asked to have the fireplace turned on and thankfully the manager took care of that! :-)

reviewText: Breakfast Experience Last Saturday, my husband and I decided to have breakfast at this location, a spot we used to enjoy. My husband ordered the French Dip Sandwich, and I went for the breakfast quiche. We both had coffee and decided to indulge in a chocolate croissant to start the day. While the wait for our order wasn’t an issue, the rest of the experience left much to be desired. When my quiche arrived, it came in an aluminum foil tray sitting on a plate that was too large for its contents, making it look quite unappetizing—almost like it was an afterthought. Honestly, it was an eye sore. Is it too much to ask to have it served in a more appealing way, maybe without the foil tray and with a garnish to make it look a bit more inviting? The coffee was another letdown. It tasted old and was cold, which was a bit surprising for a place that usually serves decent brews. I even had to remind someone behind the counter about our chocolate croissant. When it finally arrived, it too was a disappointment. It was cold and definitely didn’t taste fresh, which is the last thing you want in a pastry. I haven’t visited this location in a while, but I don’t remember the quality being this poor. It's unfortunate because I used to enjoy their breakfasts, but after this experience, I don’t think I'll be returning anytime soon

reviewText: I ate here on 3/28/21 at the location in Webster TX. Essentially what you are getting is the "French" version of Jason's Deli (not that there is anything wrong with that). The portions at this restaurant are small and frankly overpriced. The soup was lukewarm at best. Their coffee was of about Starbucks caliber. My order was taken incorrectly. I was given a small salad when I ordered a large salad. The cashier took 5 minutes to figure out how to ring up our order and had to be assisted by the manager. Upon getting our food and eating our food, the manager comes to our table, She stated that she had to wring up the order again as it "didn't go through". We showed her our receipt but she still insisted upon ringing it up again. How did it not "go through" if we had a receipt showing the order had gone through? Essentially, we were charged twice for the same meal. I asked her what the plan was since we shouldn't have to pay for the same food twice. I was told the double charge "would be removed at the end of the day". That isn't a solution and said so. The manager told me that she had a new cashier and he had made the same mistake on three tables. That isn't my problem. I shouldn't have to pay twice due to their inability to train their staff. The manager gave a half hearted "apology" and then turned on the tears as a sympathy ploy but offered no other solution. Bottom line: If you like small portions, poorly trained staff, and management that has no clue how to handle employee mistakes, La Madeleine is the restaurant for you.

reviewText: My wife and I love La Madeline’s. And we especially love the chicken Caesar salad and the potato soup. We have frequented the Perkins Rowe and Old Hammond/Jefferson location for years. We first went to La Madeline’s in 1984 at the N.O. Worlds Fair. Recently (a month or so ago), my husband had a busn lunch there and got both of the above items. The potato soup was terrible. No definable character but closer to watery dishwater than potato soup. And the salad was every bit as disappointing as the soup. The chicken seemed like just white breast that had not come out of a rotisserie as in the past. No detectable seasoning on it at all. Plus, the croutons were seriously lacking in a distinctive flavor. (We used to buy the croutons by the bag in the past…that is how much we loved them.). Finally, the salad dressing lacked flavor. Overall, the salad was just BLAH. I so hoped it was a 1-time occurrence and excusable due to Covid. But surely by now, the products should be better. Nope! Today my wife went in and placed an order at the counter for 3 salads. Same exact concerns as expressed above. Three fans of La Madeline’s were all surprised by the distinctive lack of character in the salads. Please, please get this store straight! We love La Madeline’s but need our beloved chicken salad restored.

reviewText: I love la Madeleine, I usually go to the restaurants in Dallas but since I was in the area I decided to try this location. I've never been disappointed with this place in general until today. I got the chicken parisien sandwich, side ceaser salad and 2 BOWLS of potato soup. Idk if it was bc I had it delivered (which shouldn't have made a difference bc I get their food delivered often and it's always great) but the sandwich was dry and it's usually very juicy. They gave me 2 CUPS instead of 2 BOWLS of potato soup, the soup tasted like it was left on the stove too long or something and was too runny not thick and creamy like the other places make it. The salad was kinda soggy very clear it wasnt fresh greens. I would call and ask for a refund or something but I'd rather just not visit this location again.

reviewText: The employee didn't seem to know the menu. I had checked the menu on line so I would know what I wanted to order. They didn't have it. The young lady brought our food to the table with it held right under her mouth and nose with no mask on. Then asked what else we ordered and had already paid for. I had heard so many good things about this place. It was nothing like was described as far as service was concerned. I did speak with the manager about our food and how it was delivered. The same young lady walked by doing the same thing. The manager had her put a mask on and hold the tray lower. Then she delivered the food. They did not replace our food. With COVID concerns it seem like that would have been the first offer. Food replacement was definitely not going to happen and neither was a refund. I vote with my feet. I will never go back. I'll advise people not to go. I hope anyone who reads this doesn't go even if you have gone and liked it. At a minimum see how the food is delivered to you.

name: la Madeleine

reviewText: Amazing food and the ambience is just as stellar. Went in for a birthday treat spread. Got one of everything in the pastry case. The Creme brulee was our favorite! Velvety, but with more caramel undertones and depth than I've had elsewhere. The tarts, cakes slices, Danish, etc were all very fresh. Typically slices go "off" shortly after being cut, but that was far from the case. I have also gone in for breakfast and lunch on a few occasions. The food is always excellent! It's hard to find places in the city that serve good, clean food. You can eat an entire meal without feeling lethargic. Great for a stop in on your lunch break. Their coffee is good as well, but not really sweetened enough if you're not eating a pastry with it. Staff is always polite and knowledgeable. Overall, HIGHLY recommend.

reviewText: La Madeleine has been one of my favorite lunch spots since I was a teenager. I used to visit with friends and my mom and now I take my adult daughter. I like how it is consistent no matter which restaurant I visit in any city. That was not the case with our first visit to the Forum location. The restaurant was not well kept, the whole place smelled like dirty dish rags and most tables were covered with crumbs and sticky stuff. The food was awful. I ordered the Chicken Friand with a Caesar salad and it was room temperature. It tasted like it had been sitting out for a couple of days and the mushroom sauce was cold. The salad was a soggy plate of greens and soggy croutons. It was as if it had been tossed in the dressing hours before but you couldn't taste it the dressing.. My daughter ordered the chicken Madeleine and it was NASTY. The rice was weird and tasted metallic. The chicken was bland and bone dry and the broccoli was unseasoned mush. The only redeeming items were the the Turkey Bistro sandwich and tomato soup. They were tasty as always. It is frustrating when you spend almost $50 on lunch and it is inedible. I waited in line for 5 minutes to try and speak to the manager but I was never acknowledged. We left our full plates behind and went home and ate. I honestly would have a better meal rooting around in the dumpster behind Panera.

reviewText: Cute atmosphere chain cafe. Loved the fireplace in the middle as it set the ambiance. Service was friendly. Food was flavorful but nothing mind-blowing. The flavor of the French Onion Soup was good, however the croutons were not as pictured on their site and were already super mushy before I even took my first bite, and it definitely could have used more cheese. The Chicken Friand's mushroom sauce and puff pastry were wonderful! The Chicken inside of the chicken Friand was lackluster and could have been left out. My husband enjoyed his salad and sandwich. As for the creme brulees... The gingerbread one was flavorful but tasted more like an eggnog pudding. The standard caramel creme brulee definitely had more of the eggy custard flavor I was looking for, but there was no crunchy brulee top as it was all soggy. It's a good quick french food fix, but won't be a constant go-to for me.

reviewText: If I could say one thing is that the food is good. The staff and cooks have much to be desired. The staff is ok. He said and I quote “something on this sandwich is choking me” as he coughs while eating his sandwich. Not a very pleasant sandwich if u ask me. My mother said hers was fine. I actually quite enjoyed mine. But will I ever bring friends or family here again, that’s a FAT NO! The employees seem quite oblivious to the customers needs or questions. And the chefs can’t even get a simple sandwich order correct. Also just to add an employee was sitting with a man who looked absolutely homeless, I don’t know if that was her father or a relative but she was talking and gossip so loud that everyone could here. I guess she wants people to know her business. 🤷🏼‍♀️ The atmosphere was quite different and customers just seemed annoyed and standoffish. It wasn’t the worst restaurant experience, and it certainly wasn’t the best experience either. In conclusion, I will not be returning to la madeleine’s anytime soon unless they get new management and stop hiring incompetent staff.

reviewText: This is not my first experience at La Madeline’s in Lafayette, LA, but I wanted to share my gratitude to them for going above and beyond in making right a customer service mess-up. I was with a very small, intimate bridal party gathering and we each ordered separately. It was quite a while that I had waited for my food before I went to the counter to make sure nothing had gone wrong with my order. One of the servers apologized and told me she would look into my order right away. I went back to sit down, and the manager came out shortly after to deliver my food, apologized that my food was delivered to the wrong table, and gave me a full refund for my entree plus a coupon for a free entree next time I came to their restaurant. I want to really commend the manager and La Madeline’s for going above and beyond to fix this mistake. I almost never, nowadays, find any restaurants doing either of these acts in order to fix a service mistake. I wanted to write this review to show my appreciation for their efforts and service recovery. The food and atmosphere is of course always very good at this restaurant as well.

reviewText: I really hate to leave bad reviews for restaurants but on occasion I will, and particularly as consumers are being raked over the coals on prices I am more and more willing to do so. We have ordered from this location for YEARS and previously a different one before we moved here. My wife and I almost always get the same dish. We have seen the quality go from variable and occasionally good, to terrible on occasion, to really terrible recently on more than a few occasions. I ordered on the late side, but 25 minutes before close was when my order was placed. I try not to be that guy who orders three minutes before close because that is just not right for obvious reasons. It would appear, without knowing the details of what is going on in their kitchen, that they are either not busy enough to make fresh food on the late side, or cutting corners for some other reason. Bread quality has been declining and this time they sent a croissant which is unusual, and I am assuming they are trying to use leftovers rather than make something fresh. Quality of pasta dish was terrible too. I will not order again from this location and this is enough to make me reconsider going to any La Madeleine location in the future. Might be location specific but how can I know that for sure? Gradual decline and I decided to try it one more time, but today was worst experience amongst several bad ones in the past several months. I don't mind paying a premium for delivery and good quality food but I am growing weary of experiences like this. Spent close to $60 for dinner for two and I could have bought a frozen dish from the grocery store for $20 or less and it would have been better.

reviewText: Not being able to split checks for a party of five—especially in a small restaurant using Toast—is surprising. name: CASA DE JULIA RESTAURANT BAR
fullAddress: Luhrs Tower, 45 W Jefferson St, Phoenix, AZ 85003, United States
reviewText: Me and my spouse went to Casa de Julia for dinner, and unfortunately our experience was not what we expected. We made a reservation in advance because of all the hype, but it didn’t live up to it for us. When we arrived, there was nowhere to park and we ended up paying $40 for parking for no reason. We ordered a steak, and after about 45 minutes we still hadn’t received our food. When we asked our waitress what was going on, she said there was a large order ahead of us, even though there were only three tables seated and all were small parties. At the end, we had to leave because our order was never fulfilled. It was disappointing, and it felt like management didn’t care, because no one came to check on us. This is definitely not the way to build long-term success. Update: I received a call from the restaurant manager, Aaron, and I have to say I was impressed by how he handled the situation. He genuinely cared and acknowledged what happened, which means a lot. The restaurant is less than a year old, and I hope they continue growing into the hype. Because of his professionalism, I’m changing my review and will be giving Casa de Julia another try.

name: CASA DE JULIA RESTAURANT BAR
fullAddress: Luhrs Tower, 45 W Jefferson St, Phoenix, AZ 85003, United States
reviewText: I understand that when new restaurants open there are a lot of strains on the business. However, there is a saying in entrepreneurship that it is harder to retain existing customers than acquiring new ones. Which is why I have to post this review. I will start that the decor is very nice. However, what was supposed to be an exciting outing with friends turned into a sour experience. Never was there indication that seating was limited to a time (neither on their social media, on OpenTable, or by the staff). Yet, as food was coming out (approximately an hour into having sat down) we are told that we had 15 minutes left before they had to move us (table of 6) to the bar. They then proceeded to move many people who had reservations to the bar (with apparent upset faces). The restaurant seems to have issues with the sewage system because there was a foul odor. The food was decent but lacking in ingredients. I hope they take the criticism from other patrons into consideration because the restaurant does have potential.

reviewText: I came to this restaurant when it first opened in 2017, and had a bad experience with not being acknowledged after standing at the counter for quite some time and I never even got a chance to try any of the food. I searched for gluten free desserts in Albuquerque on Monday for my daughter’s Birthday, and decided to give it another shot. When I walked in, I could see a young man and a young woman standing in front of the back wall in front of the kitchen window, and a chef in the kitchen. I walked up to the counter in front of the desserts and all three of the employees looked at me, but then looked away and continued with their conversation. I stayed in front of the glass and then looked around the area there at the front to see if there was a sign or something that showed where I should go for help since the employee weren’t coming to me. Finally after a couple of minutes the girl came over to the counter and asked if I needed help.I told her that I was wanting to know which deserts were gluten free. She said she had “no idea” and then just stood there. I said that the search had lead me there so that was why I was asking. She didn’t say anything again and I just looked at her and she said “I guess I can ask”. I was already frustrated and said “uh, that would be helpful” she walked away and came back to say they didn’t have anything gluten free. I then walked out the door. I was NOT upset about no gluten free options, I was upset about receiving such bad service again two years later. It takes a lot for me to give a bad review, but this one was worth the one star I gave it. I was hoping for better service and to actually get to try the food. I guess I never will because I won’t be coming back. Great service is key in any successful business.

Why not mention that when Ive tried 3 times to pay the bill in line? La Madeline has the potential to be really great and maybe even be like it used to, but this is not the first time Ive encountered people that don't care, don't listen, and are TOTALLY unhelpful. reviewText: Food was delicious!! And great service too!! We had entrees: pappardelle and gnocchi. Foccacia bread snd shred a chocolate mousse. The pasta was definitely homemade AND fresh! reviewText: We loved Cedro’s! We were in Austin visiting our son and wanted Italian food. We were so lucky to find Cedro’s. We didn’t want to go to a chain restaurant, and found this amazing place! The pasta, the bread and sauces are all made from scratch! It was soo delicious! Also, the portions are big. Our son took home lunch for the next day. Our waitress was the sweetest, I wish I could remember her name, but she was awesome ! We had a wonderful experience!

name: Cedro Scratch Italian & Wine Bar

reviewText: I had really high hopes for this place. I have had the pizza on 2 occasions for take out and it was great. I would say it's more of a flatbread though to be clear but still good. This time I went in for dine in dinner and tried the pasta as it was made from scratch I had heard. Speaking of my dish in particular which was the pork chop parm. The meat was very tough over cooked and about as thick as a paper plate, for the price I expected to get more substance. The pasta itself was cooked well enough but the sauce tasted like it came out of a can. Almost chef boyardee esque. Good service though but for the price I can't say I've be back for anything other than the flat bread.

reviewText: We planned a trip from over 2 hours away to DFW for my partner to travel to a family funeral this weekend all the way in Illinois. Well, the airport is currently under construction with conflicting signs for exits, and poor lighting and visibility for drivers. Keep in mind, this is not enough for me to leave a bad review like this; it gets 1,000,000 times worse. My partner tapped his phone to a card reader to debit him for a toll. I remember two decades ago when I had to pick up and drop off family, we usually received a pass - so I inquired if he had a slip. He stated he did not receive one from the machine and continued on to the terminal, where I had woken up to drive the return trip. Upon entering the exit toll, I reached out to a couple of construction workers nearby and told them of my situation. These construction workers were very kind and helpful, they advised that I press a call button on a intercom. Please keep in mind the environment when trying to talk to someone on this intercom, there are vehicles behind you, there is road noise and construction around you, and the speaker works poorly and is intermittent. I reach out and a woman picks up, at least I assume it is a woman. I let her know the situation where I didn't have a ticket, as I inquire with her I notice my license plate somehow being scanned by one of their readers on the screen. Her response to my inquiry is "take this discount for $2". I responded with my boyfriend stated he already paid upon entry, why would I need to pay again. Her response was "he didn't pay". I inquired with how is that possible if we had to scan a debit card upon entry and did not receive any receipt. She stated you never pay upon entry, which is odd... So because I had no payment method on me at all, only a driver's license and other identification cards, if she could possibly charge the Wells Fargo card that we use. Her response was very crass and ugly stating "if I have to pay you have to pay and I work here". I tried explaining again I didn't have a payment method and out of frustration I stated I probably never want to come here again to utilize DFW services because of your attitude and the insane pricing of merely trying to drop off someone at the airport or pick someone up - there was a chart in front of me that says 0-8 minutes was $9 and then additional time after that was $2 either every half hour or hour I can't remember. I felt like it was highway robbery truly, especially with the state of the airport and the lack of effective service. I then requested to speak to her supervisor, who, admittedly was much more reasonable. Unfortunately because they're on an intercom and they don't have a full view the circumstance was still very frustrating. A gentleman then came on the line after a warm handoff from the original employee who suddenly developed customer service skills; and try to assist in troubleshoot. I advise on my frustration because of the reason for travel, the attitude of the associate, and the lack of payment I had on me to be able to pay the toll. Because it was a toll, being mailed the bill is an option. The supervisor requested my license plate number, because the dunce of an associate cleared whatever was in the system when I pulled up. The supervisor asked that I get out of my giant SUV where I was boxed by vehicles behind me and a gate in front of me to try and get my license plate number. I am unable to open my car door, so I asked if there is any way he could kind of lift the gate so I can pull forward and be able to get out of the car or something, and he paused... Which I have no qualms about and then I reiterated the only things I had with me was my driver's license and military ID. At that moment the supervisor immediately lifted the gate and said have a nice day. Why the hell should that alone make all the difference in treating people well. That is the reason for this one-star review. I am still extremely grateful to the construction workers and the supervisor for their assistance. But the single associate made this unbearable.

reviewText: DFW is a city disguised as an airport — sprawling, high-tech, and filled with more restaurants, lounges, and shopping than you could ever need. When it’s running smoothly, it’s one of the best big airports in the country: clean, organized, and surprisingly quick to get through considering its size. The Skylink train system is genius and makes terminal hopping painless. That said, it’s so huge it can feel like its own time zone — miss your connection, and you might as well pack a lunch. reviewText: Following a flawless flight from GSP, and landing early, there was a shortage of wheelchairs available. After a few extra minutes, “Hakim” showed up. Hakim is outstanding! So again, he offered to bring me to the new gate! There is no way to express my gratitude! It’s Christmas time. It’s busy. reviewText: Our experience was extremely disappointing. On the morning of 10/5, we decided to have a breakfast date before my wife headed to work. We placed our order at 9:17 AM and walked over to the coffee area, only to find it was out of both creamer and forks. We notified the staff and grabbed what we could to seat ourselves. The bench seating area was visibly dirty. My wife actually had to fill a cup with water to wipe down the booth herself—when I asked what she was doing, she said the seat was too dirty to sit on. We ended up moving to a standard table instead. About 10 minutes later, I checked again—still no creamer or forks. Another customer also asked, and eventually forks were restocked about five minutes after that. However, the creamer was still empty until I walked it up to the counter myself to request a refill. Despite all this, 45 minutes passed and we still hadn’t received our food. When my wife went to ask about it, she was told they were short-staffed and that we were never given a wait time. But if the delays were known, why wasn’t this communicated before we placed our order? Instead, we wasted nearly an hour of our morning waiting for food that never came. We ultimately requested a refund. This required staff to call the associate manager from the back to handle it. When the manager finally came out, there was no apology, no acknowledgment of our experience—just a refund, and that was it. What bothered me most wasn’t just the long wait or the missing items—it was the complete disregard from the associate manager, who stayed hidden in the back while her team struggled up front. If they were truly short-staffed, why wasn’t she helping? Between the lack of customer service, poor communication, and the dirty, poorly maintained environment, we left completely disgusted. No guest should have to deal with this. Period. Update: I contacted la madeleine customer service. A franchise business consultant reached out to apologize and mentioned training would happen for employees. Nothing was offered other than a thank you and appreciation for letting them know of the issues. This is truly when I believed they lost touch with customer service. An invite on the house next time would have been appropriate or a free meal or discount. Nothing. We will never be back.

name: la Madeleine

reviewText: I was hesitant to write this because I’ve truly loved this place. I’ve been a loyal customer for almost four years, but lately, I’ve noticed a decline in food wait times and overall service. During my most recent visit about two weeks ago, we went for lunch on a Saturday morning. It was busy, as usual, and we ordered to dine in. I got the pumpkin praline French toast, which I’ve had before and loved. Normally, our food comes out within 10–15 minutes, but this time we waited 30–40 minutes and started to grow impatient. When my boyfriend went to check on our order, we were told it had been marked as “to-go” and had been sitting on the pickup bench getting cold. He asked them to remake it, and after another 10 minutes, the food finally came out—but they gave me the regular French toast instead of the pumpkin praline. When I mentioned it, the server didn’t take the plate back but said he’d bring the toppings on the side. He returned about five minutes later with the pralines, pumpkin cream, whipped cream, and syrup. At that point, I was too upset to eat. They offered us free desserts to make up for it, but the line at the counter was long, so we decided to leave. Sadly, this was one of the worst dining experiences we’ve had here, and I don’t think we’ll be returning. It’s just not the same as it used to be.

reviewText: It’s a restaurant with a French-inspired theme, though it didn’t quite live up to our expectations of authentic French cuisine. We tried the Turkey Holiday Feast Sampler, which reminded us more of Thanksgiving leftovers than a signature dish. The Strawberry Spinach Bacon Salad with salmon had an interesting combination of ingredients, but the cold salmon and its strong fishy taste made it difficult to enjoy. The Country French Breakfast was highlighted by a nicely fried potato galette, but the other elements of the dish were fairly average. For dessert, we tried the Classic Napoleon and Café Au Lait Crème Brûlée, which were pleasant but not particularly memorable. The restaurant was clean and had a nice atmosphere, but unfortunately, the food didn’t quite meet our expectations. While it was an overall decent experience, it’s unlikely we’ll return.

reviewText: This was my first time at La Madeleine & I gotta say, pretty dang good! The only reason for a four star overall review was the cleanliness of the establishment. Don't worry, no roaches or anything like that, just overall sweeping, moping, & dusting. Dust bunnies everywhere! The food gets five stars easily! My gosh, the bread...*chef's kiss*...damn good! I had the Chicken Caesar Sandwich, which, side note, I was told is not a regular menu item. I was confused by the cafeteria style grab-a-tray-&-slide-it-down counter. After ordering my sandwhich I was handed my order number on a wooden spoon (kinda cool) I was told that's for folks who are ordering from the "cold menu". So I get to stroll to the end of the long counter to the register where I pay for my meal & drink. Y'all, this sandwhich, just de-friggen-licious! The bread, I want delivered to my home every morning for breakfast & lunch. Service was great. I'm sure the "I've never been here before" look on my face screamed "please help me". Like an idiot I didn't take pictures of my meal, I really should have, it was that good. Highly recommend.

reviewText: I've been to this location quite a few times now, and I have to say that I appreciate the customer service and how kind they are about teaching us how to use their systems they have in place. I like that the station for the jam, jelly butter and bread are always stocked and the women who cleaned up after us are fantastic as well because they get the job done very quickly. But I have to say it is pretty annoying to carry the trays and the things if you are sitting far away . I know that's the way that the restaurant is designed, but it is just not ideal. They do get busy quite fast and so it's better to try to find a place close the refill station so that you don't have to Be the one who is constantly having to go up and get things from the station. I do not care for the potato that they have at breakfast time or even the omelet really because it is not anything to write home about. The croissants were good and so is the satcher torte which is the favorite thing of mine that had from here so far. Overall it is a great place to grab a bite to eat but it is just a trusty place because there is nothing very different or unique about it. It does feel very cozy with the fireplace so there's that!

name: la Madeleine
fullAddress: 8825 N Fwy Suite 109, Fort Worth, TX 76131
reviewText: I am a long-time fan of La Madeleine. This restaurant has deliciously prepared food. Also, they play classical music. In an age when so many restaurants, waiting rooms, etc. have TVs blaring, THANK GOODNESS someone still values music with a meal. Now to the food...My very favorite thing is the Tomato Basil Soup. I love the tomatoey rich flavor. Next favorite is a Croque Monseiur, a sandwich made with ham and a topping of rich bechamel and cheese and broiled. Half of one is perfect for breakfast! The coffee is always delicious and they have plenty of real half-and-half. A very attractive feature of this restaurant is the bread bar, which includes a selection of breads, real butter and homemade jams and honey. Another thing worth mentioning...the roast chicken. If you go at lunch, the wonderful smell permeates the whole place. Roast chicken and Caesar Salad are perfect together. Oh, and the icing on the cake is their pastries!! I cannot choose a favorite one, but the fruit tart, the Sacher torte and the almond croissant are wonderful. And the lemon tart. And the strawberries Romanoff are also just delicious. I love everything I have ever eaten here. It really is wonderful.

reviewText: Tonight was my second time and the service was the same at the TO GO area as it was the first visit (a month ago). The service was lousy. The poor girl at the register was asking for such and such and this girl that I assume was supposed to be helping her with orders was literally just turning in circles and flitting from one thing to another, but not helping on to go orders. There were 3 other employees that worked the line standing around doing nothing but talking because there was no one in line. Didn't seem to care the to go girl was drowning with no help. The to go girl finally had to tell that she needed a chicken caesar salad now. Finally, girl that was turning circles finally made my salad. I love eating at laMadeleine's, but it won't be at this location. I'll drive to 114 in Grapevine like I did before this location opened. So sad.

reviewText: I'm not too certain people on Google reviews know how to honestly rate an establishment without sounding like a bunch of whiners. Apparently the only thing that impresses Texans is impeccable service not the quality or taste of the food. Of course they might not have all of their ducks in a row yet. Give them the slightest break especially if they are busy and have new hires. I'm not making excuses for restaurants however Im sure that if you walked over to the manager like a grown up and presented your issue in a calm way that they will accommodate and make things right. Don't jump on a review and bash them if you didn't take the time to square it away first. That said I've been here 4 times over the past month and it has been busy to an extent, yet they have always been spot on with orders and quick about things. I feel their Keesh was a little overrated, unless I got a bad batch...otherwise, not too bad. Everything else on the menu is very tasty. So far I've started to order the oatmeal which could use a little honey drizzled on top or something to sweeten it. Perhaps I'll ask next time. I love the seasoned hash brown, I forget what it's called on the menu. It was tasty. The simple things they just make better. That's important.

reviewText: I have mixed thoughts about this location. On the one hand, food is good, service is friendly and fast, but the place is always, and I mean ALWAYS filthy! It just gets worse every time. I used to come in a few times a week between 7 and 8 AM, but now I go less often because there is never even a clean table first thing in the morning. Doesn't anyone ever clean? At the very least you'd expect someone to clean at closing time so the place opens nice and pretty. The window sills look like they've never been wiped clean. Crumbs on every table and chair. Look under the bakery case near the counters at the registers, piles of debris and trash underneath. The coffee and condiments area is somewhat cleared off in front of everything, but it's obvious no one moves a single bottle or container to the side when 'cleaning' because there is dirt and coffee grinds all over the back and around everything. The trash receptacle is filthy, everything is dirty, dirty, dirty. The most upsetting thing is the fact that these observations are only where the public can see. It makes you wonder what the kitchen must look like! If you aren't going to clean what the guest can see, you certainly aren't going to clean where they don't! reviewText: La Madeline has been my go-to for decades anytime I traveled to TX. The chain never disappoints & the French Country Breakfast is my usual. Until this time… First, we and several folks behind us waited at the register for over 10 minutes while staff flittered around us without saying one word to acknowledge that we were there. A woman in a beanie finally strolled; dragging her feet from the back. Took our order and we sat down. After 8 minutes, we decided to ask about our mimosa’s where we were told they didn’t know. Ok, weird as it was rang up in the POS but not a biggie, it happens sometimes. Few minutes later, they brought out the OJ, glasses & champagne for us to make ourselves. Keep in mind, it took 10 minutes to order, 8 min for our kit to make mimosas and then another 14 for our breakfast. I kept looking at my plate trying to figure out what was missing. Once I realized the part that made it “French” potato galette was missing, I went up to ask. She quickly brushed me off and said I have them in the oven. I decided to put a timer on it bc by now I’m just irritated— who wants to eat a dry hash brown alone? It took 21 minutes & 24 seconds for it to come out ALMOST COOKED. We almost gave up on it because our meal was eaten so far in advance. Lastly, while I was waiting, I went to refill my coffee only to find out the coffee was totally removed from its location. Listen, I understand businesses are dealing with finding good help resulting in running lean. But from what I could see, I counted 5 staff members minus the cooks in the back. With this store being a much smaller restaurant (& the restaurant only being half full) in comparison to most, I don’t understand the inconsistency this store represented today. Sigh, bummed 😑

name: la Madeleine French Bakery & Cafe Montfort

reviewText: I was upset with the service I received here on today. I brought my son here and when we pulled up to the drive through window I asked a question and I’m guessing she didn’t understand it and sort of just blew it off. We ordered a Turkey Bistro and potato soup. We sat at the window about 5 mins before anyone came. Then when she did come she just told me my total took my card handed it back and we waited an additional 13 mins for one sandwich and one soup. There was no one inside and one person that was in the drive through behind me. May I add that that person hopped out of line went inside and left with their order before me. Then I finally blew the horn and the girl came to the window dumbfounded when asked why was the wait so long. I will NOT be returning here, and after reading the reviews I see I’m not the only one.

reviewText: Cedro is owned by the folks who own Bartletts and The Rotten Bunch (they used to have the best mozzarella appetizer, but closed a few years ago). We have been wanting to try Cedro for a while now. I'm so happy we finally made it! Our waitress was Emily and she was great, and friendly! There was a lot to choose from! My husband had the PEI mussel appetizer and thoroughly enjoyed it, although he wished it came with a little fork (but he made do with fingers!). Everything is made in house - so we also ordered the focaccia bread. It comes toasted and with parm on top. They usually give you olive oil and balsamic for it, but because of my restricted diet, I couldn't have. Bread was good! I skipped the appetizer so I had more room for dinner! I ordered the branzino and gnocchi (potato) in a cream sauce with mushrooms and butternut squash. It was VERY good - a bit rich, so be hungry if you go! I couldn't finish it! The fish was perfectly cooked. My husband had the lamb shank over polenta - and savored every bite. It was tender and the polenta was well cooked. I skipped dessert - I was stuffed - but we got the Tiramisu to go. One minor note - all of their red sauces, including the marinara, have wine in them, which I can't have. I wish the marinara was like most places - alcohol free. Overall a lovely meal! We will be back!!!

name: Cedro Scratch Italian & Wine Bar
fullAddress: 14028 US-183 Suite 210, Austin, TX 78717, United States
reviewText: Cedro es un restaurante que realmente supera las expectativas. La comida es simplemente excelente, preparada con ingredientes frescos y con un sabor que demuestra la dedicación del chef en cada plato. Desde el primer bocado se nota la calidad y el cuidado en cada detalle. El servicio es impecable: el personal es amable, atento y siempre dispuesto a hacer que la experiencia sea perfecta. Se toman el tiempo de explicar los platillos, recomendar opciones y asegurarse de que todo esté a tu gusto. El ambiente es cálido, elegante y muy agradable, ideal tanto para una cena especial como para disfrutar con amigos o familia. La decoración, la música y el estilo del lugar crean un entorno acogedor que invita a quedarse. En resumen, Cedro ofrece una experiencia gastronómica completa: comida deliciosa, servicio de primera y un ambiente encantador. Un lugar totalmente recomendado y al que sin duda volveré.

reviewText: Cedro Scratch Italian and Wine Bar has become one of our favorite spots for authentic Italian food just outside of Austin. After ordering takeout several times through Uber Eats and always being impressed with the consistency and quality, my wife and I finally visited the restaurant in person—and we’re so glad we did. The food here is outstanding. They make their pasta from scratch, and it truly makes a difference. The pappardelle with sausage is one of our favorites—rich, flavorful, and perfectly balanced. The Bolognese is equally excellent, and we also highly recommend the pork parmesan and salmon dishes. Portions are generous, and every bite tastes like it was made with care. Our recent dinner visit was just as enjoyable. The atmosphere is warm and casual, with both indoor and outdoor seating available. We started with the arugula salad, followed by the pappardelle with sausage once again. We ordered a bottle of wine that paired beautifully with the meal, and our evening was made even better by a friendly conversation with the manager. He let us know about their Wednesday night special—50% off all bottles of wine—which we’re already planning to come back for. There’s a nice Amarone on the list we can’t wait to try. If you’re looking for authentic Italian food with homemade pasta, a laid-back yet refined vibe, and consistently delicious meals, Cedro is an absolute gem. Highly recommended!

name: Cedro Scratch Italian & Wine Bar
fullAddress: 14028 US-183 Suite 210, Austin, TX 78717, United States
reviewText: I was hoping for a solid meal, but unfortunately, the experience fell flat in multiple ways. To start, the atmosphere was uninspiring—plain décor, dim lighting that felt more dull than cozy, and an overall lack of character. It didn’t feel inviting or lively, just… there. Service was friendly enough, but nothing particularly notable. The biggest disappointment, however, was the food. I ordered the fries and Brussels sprouts as sides, expecting something flavorful, crispy, or at least well-seasoned. Instead, the fries were bland, lacking salt or any real crispiness. The Brussels sprouts were equally underwhelming—soft, almost mushy, and missing the charred, caramelized edges that make them great. Even adding condiments didn’t save them. To their credit, when I mentioned the lackluster fries, they did offer a replacement free of charge, which I appreciated. Unfortunately, i didn’t get a second batch. The prices, on the other hand, were steep for what we got. I don’t mind paying more for quality food, but when the meal is this mediocre, it’s hard to justify. Even with the comped fries, I left feeling like I overpaid for a forgettable meal. Overall, this Italian wine bar simply isn’t worth returning to. There are too many great places offering flavorful food and a better atmosphere to settle for something this boring. If you’re looking for a memorable meal, I’d recommend looking elsewhere.
