name: Cedro Scratch Italian & Wine Bar
fullAddress: 14028 US-183 Suite 210, Austin, TX 78717, United States
reviewText:
UPDATE:
Thanks Tyler for the recommendation on the mimosa with cranberries and the Pinot grigio. It was perfect! A special thanks to Kirsten as well. You overheard me mention it was my partners birthday and brought out our tiramisu (top notch btw) with a candle which made the night even more special.

---------------------------------

Highly recommend!!!

The Pinot Griogio & Noir were absolutely delicious. Served at perfect temperatures, each.

We started with the Arancini Rissoto balls which had a red sauce with depth that I could keep eating the entire meal if I had the choice! It was a perfect pairing with the grilled bread to finish the sauce at the bottom of the Arancini dish! 😋

Following the meal we chose the fettuccine carbonara for our entree with grilled chicken. The poached egg topped the flavorful dish and added a little something extra to it with the yolk that I can't say I've had anywhere else before. The noodles were rich and perfect thickness. Definitely made in house! It was also Tuesday so they had BOGO flatbread style pizza. We went with the margarheta pizza and a pesto chicken pizza to go which were also both great options!

Before heading out we wanted the tiramisu (sadly sold out), but I'm so glad it was, because we went with the crembrule and a side of strawberries. Wow! So rich and delicious with miraculously perfect caramelization. We finished every bite.

Thanks Alicia for the recommendation. You and the host were fantastic. Compliments to the chef! 🤌

Manga Manga!

reviewText: I have been a loyal La Madeleine fan for years, and this location lives up to what I have come to expect from La Madeleine. The staff is efficient & quick while still being very friendly & helpful. Personally, I am a fan of their french onion soup, caesar salads (dressing can be purchased in bulk) & many breakfast offerings. Really, no matter what you order, I don't think you will be disappointed-I have never had a bad meal at any of their many locations. The highlight of any trip to La Madeleine, however, is their large assortment of freshly made breads & desserts. Their baked goods are available for purchase at the 'To-Go' area, where they display their many delicous dessert offerings. It would be a wasted trip to at least not take a look, if not to enjoy, their bounty of delicous confections. I always seem to find some excuse to grab something (ok, usually somethings...) from their display to enjoy at home-or to enjoy on the way home.

reviewText: Yes, I know it's a chain restaurant. But I really feel welcomed and at home when I come here. Maybe it's the food...I LOVE their mushroom soup! Maybe it's the cozy fireplace. reviewText: No exaggeration: this place has changed my life! I couldn't recommend it more to anyone needing vision care & most especially anyone with kc. I have worn contacts most of my life. Having keratoconus (kc), it's been years of frustration trying to find the best fit + best vision. I was miserable and had so many issues -- until finding this oasis of eye care at Lakeline. I am so happy with the personal service, client commitment, and lovely kindness from everyone at Lakeline. They have the latest technology, the best doctors, and an awesome staff. In ONE visit I had better and more comprehensive eye care than I've experienced in YRS from my previous dr in Austin. Honestly, with kc and not receiving much hope or help from my (former) dr, I was at the point where I thought I'd just have to struggle with dry eyes, poor vision, and things like not driving much at night. Then I came to Lakeline and everything changed. After seeing Dr. Esmali, I now have the clearest vision I've had in years, maybe ever since kc, and my eyes feel so comfortable. I am forever grateful. To make it even better, this just took 2 visits. My sclerals fit perfectly right off thanks to Dr. Esmali's meticulous care, knowledge, and dedication to her patients. In fact, everyone I've interacted with has really listened to me, taken time to answer my questions, and shown great kindness. Lakeline has given me a new outlook--literally! Thank you from the bottom of my heart. (ps. I don't write reviews unless I receive such excellent service that I must share (or if the opposite, to warn others). I have been telling everyone about this place bc it is honestly that good. (And if, like me, it's not the closest to home for you -- trust me, it's totally worth the drive.)

name: Lakeline Vision Source

reviewText: I’ve worn glasses of some sort (reading, distance, progressive lens) for about 30 years. As a former military dependent, I’ve been to vision centers all over the world and all across the country. I’ve had my share of bad experiences, poor quality eye exams, incorrect prescriptions and repeat visits, but the amount of great experiences have been extremely limited...until my last two annual exams at Lakeline Vision Source. I found this location, two years ago, through my healthcare providers website and was just hoping for “better than the other place” type of service. What I found was that from the appointment setup, to picking up my new glasses, and all of the excellent customer service in between, I could not have been happier. The staff is friendly and not “fake friendly to get your money”. They take their time, don’t make you feel rushed, do an exceptional job and my favorite...they are patient with you. There was no feeling of pushing you into a purchase of a new pair of frames, but instead comments like “I really like your current frames, would you like to put new lenses in them?” Not what I’ve been accustomed to and huge in winning me over. Two years in a row, I’ve been back and seen the same eye doctor, and have had the same experience...exceptional. Now that I’m settled down and no longer moving from place to place, I think I know where I’ll keep coming back to...year after year. Thank you Lakeline Vision Source for being an honest business with patience for your patients!

reviewText: Made an appointment to get new glasses. Was greeted promptly at arrival, temperature taken, and their protocols for trying on frames explained. I began searching for a frame(s) was later joined by my wife. We narrowed it down to 2 frames as well as potentially putting the new lenses in my spare frame. From the moment we sat down at one of the tables, Michelle took charge. First calling our insurance company to determine who was the vision plan provider (it wasn’t spelled out on out insurance card). She examined my current glasses, as well as my prescription sunglasses ( the ones we decided to have new lenses put in) to check for the type of lenses I had, the coatings, and indicated putting the new lenses in my existing sunglasses frame was the best option. She measured the old glasses, then used a couple of devices to measure my eyes, double checked everything, made some suggestions about the lens material, potential coatings, and the various levels of lens darkness. Periodically she would look up and greet new customers, immediately resuming to completing our order. Her approach and professionalism put us at ease and we felt quite comfortable with the entire process. The ultimate cost was much less than we had expected. Michelle gave us some instructions on what to expect going from there. She wrote several notes on the envelope the receipts went in case we had any questions later. While unnecessary she apologized for how long it took for her to help us. We understood that good things take time and we were appreciative of her having taken the time to do such a thorough job. If you go to the San Tan Visionworks we suggest that you ask the Michelle.

reviewText: My rating is a 3 because of the poor customer service we experienced there on Saturday. We walked in and the young woman at the register was just rude. I was going to order an item off of the line. I haven’t been here in a good while, but every time before when I’ve been here, I’ve had to walk down the line and tell the person behind the counter that I want the prepared item sitting there and they plate it and hand it right to me. However, this time, I told the lady at the first register that I wanted something already on the line and she just said “you order here”. Okay, no big deal. I then tried to explain I wanted something already over there and I’ve always just had to walk down and ask for it. Again she just responded “you order here”. She could see I was confused and just repeated again “you order here”. No explanation as to why it was different. No smile, no care that I was confused. Just a blank stare and the same words repeated three times. I don’t mind if policies have changed and I have to do it different than before, no biggie. However, I do mind when the person who is there to provide customer service is just rude about it and doesn’t give two cents about being kind or communicating. It’s a shame because the food here is amazing and if the customer service were even just okay I would give this place five stars. Maybe some retraining is in order to teach this young lady how to effectively communicate and maybe even smile or use a bit of kindness when speaking to customers.

reviewText: Soon to be a casualty -- Reply to owner...going to the La Madeleine website won't solve the real problem with your restaurant. If you are the manager, I suggest you take better care of the place. Clean it! Improve the quality of the food! It's not a corporate issue. It's a local manager issue! We went to the La Madeleine in Downtown Crown for dinner this week and will not be back. The place was dirty - tables had not been cleared or wiped down, the bathroom hadn't been cleaned for quite some time. The food was mediocre at best. I order the Croque Monsieur and French onion soup. Neither were hot, the sandwich only had a few slices of meat and no cheese; the soup was extremely thick and didn't taste good at all. Soda fountain Pepsi was flat. My husband ordered the tomato soup which was very thick and cold. His French dip was bready and barely had any meat or cheese on it. This place used to be reliably good, but the past few times it has been disappointing. I could understand the dirty tables if they didn't have staff available, but the employees were standing clustered around the register talking with little regard for the condition of the place. Trust me, it's not worth the money spent to eat here.

reviewText: We have been to the Cedar Park location, and it's usually really good (which is why I gave them 2 stars rather than one). Today though we were EXTREMELY disappointed by our experience. I took my two teenage daughters into town (we live about 30 minutes drive north of this location) as they wanted to have lunch at Ramen Tatsuya and then do some shopping. We arrived around 1pm and got in line. When we got up to the counter to order, we were told that the kitchen wasn't taking anymore orders. We were given no explanation for the inconvenience. Just a "sorry, we aren't taking any more orders and won't be for quite a while". The restaurant was NOT full, and it was in the middle of a lunch shift on a Saturday. It was very disappointing after making the long drive down. We got back in our car and went to Chick-fil-a for lunch. CFA is not as tasty, but always happy to serve. Will think twice about driving to Ramen Tatsuya in the future. :(

name: Ramen Tatsu-Ya
fullAddress: 14028 US-183 Bldg G, Suite 310, Austin, TX 78717
reviewText: Absolutely love the service at this location! My husband and I have only ever been to the Research Blvd. location, but it was closed due to a power outage, so we decided to check out another one—and I’m so glad it worked out that way! We were immediately greeted by Becca as soon as we walked in. She asked if we’d been in before and let us know she was available for any questions or help with the menu. Becca checked in on us after we received our meal and again before we left, which made the experience feel really welcoming and personal. I didn’t catch the names of the other team members, but the service overall was impeccable. The space here feels more open with plenty of seating, which made for a super comfortable dining experience. The food was amazing as always—Ramen Tatsuya is hands down my favorite place to get ramen in ATX. We ordered the MI-SO-NOT, TSUKEMEN, Gyoza, and Karaage, and everything was absolutely delicious. We’ll definitely be coming to this location from now on!

reviewText: Austin is known for many things, but a true local knows that one of its greatest culinary treasures is Ramen Tatsu-ya. This is not just a restaurant; it's a destination, and for good reason. From the moment you step inside, the atmosphere is a vibrant mix of fun and energy, with an edgy, urban feel that perfectly complements the incredible food.​The ramen is simply in a league of its own. The broths are a work of art—rich, deeply flavorful, and simmered for hours to perfection. Whether you go for the classic or one of their unique, spicy concoctions, every bowl is a revelation. The noodles are perfectly cooked, and the toppings are thoughtfully chosen, from the melt-in-your-mouth chashu pork to the perfectly marinated soft-boiled egg.​The service is always fast, friendly, and efficient, even during the busiest times. The staff is knowledgeable and passionate about their food, making the experience even better. Ramen Tatsu-ya has truly set the standard for ramen in Austin and beyond. If you're craving a bowl of pure, savory comfort, this is the place to be. It's an unforgettable meal that will leave you planning your next visit before you've even finished your first.

reviewText: This could just be my own perspective, but idk about Ramen Tatsu-Ya anymore. I usually never leave hungry, so this could be a sign of shrinkflation/the portions getting smaller? Curry Nu School & Nu School are still solid veg options, but the menu hasn't expanded on its veg offerings since the seasonal Pumpkin ramen from like... 2020/21?? That was the best they had to offer veg-wise, and since then... Just kinda the same thing with nothing new to offer returning veg heads. If Ramen Tatsu-Ya was able to offer more meat and dairy-free options, I'd come a lot more often. But sadly, missing out. Also this one time they had us wait for food that never ended up coming and thankfully we got refunded for it. But we didn't get offered any other compensation for wasting like 30 to 45 minutes of our time waiting. I believe it was simply because of the fact they didn't want to make more vegan Ramen that day and they were pushing out other people's orders so. If you don't like eating me, this isn't really the restaurant for you. Cool vibe though, good music. The front of house staff is very welcoming and a good vibe.

reviewText: Having been to this Ramen Tatsu-Ya a few times since 2023, we've never been disappointed, and we typically leave very fully satisfied (albeit maybe craving a Krispy Kreme)! All the ramen entrees have been outstanding, full of flavor and filling (whether you consume the soup base or not). But this time, I just had to try "The Crawmen" - an amazing ramen full of crawfish tails, Andouille sausage, corn kernels and more in a totally authentic soup base full of Cajun crawfish flavor! I am definitely coming back for this Crawmen again, and every year! For anyone who loves Crawfish, Cajun and Ramen, this fusion dish is outstanding!

reviewText: Dallas Fort Worth International Airport is one of the busiest airports in the country, but despite the heavy traffic, my experience there was smooth and surprisingly stress-free. Getting to the terminal was easy, and the layout is well-organized, which made the entire arrival process straightforward. One of the highlights of DFW is the Skylink service, which is excellent. The automated train system is fast, efficient, and makes traveling between terminals a breeze. Even though the airport is massive, Skylink takes away the stress of navigating long distances. The airport itself is clean, modern, and very well maintained. There are plenty of places to eat and shop, offering everything from quick bites and coffee shops to sit-down restaurants and well-known retail brands. It makes layovers or waiting times much more enjoyable with so many options to choose from. Despite being such a large and very busy airport, it never felt chaotic. The signage is clear, the staff is helpful, and the overall organization makes it easy to find your way around. Pros: - Smooth and stress-free terminal access - Excellent Skylink train service between terminals - Clean, organized, and modern facilities - Wide variety of food and shopping options - Clear signage and helpful staff Things to note: - It’s a major hub, so it can get crowded at peak times Overall: DFW Airport offers a great travel experience. Even with its size and busy atmosphere, the efficiency, cleanliness, and amenities make it stand out as one of the better large airports in the U.S.

reviewText: More diabolical experiences at DFW Yet another delay/ cancellation visit. Poor amenities. Ignorant ground staff. Flying in from YVR to DFW we got diverted to Oklahoma City and sat on the runway for 4 hours. Our pilot deemed this unnecessary . On arriving at DFW close to midnight ,having missed my connection my airline put me on an early morning flight . The overpriced airport hotel was sold out and the time involved in getting to and back from another hotel made that option futile . So I looked for a lounge.ALL CLOSED. After much searching I found a tiny hovel of a resting area with a few comfortable chairs to rest for my flight. Contrast this with a recent experience through Doha Qatar. The lounges were open 24 hours a day with comfort and available food and drink all night. Given the vast number of evening flight cancellations at DFW it is absurd that the overnight facilities are so poor!!! My return trip was equally unpleasant. Having executive status with my airline I got ready to board my flight to Vancouver. As on all previous U.S.A./Canada flights I have made I had my nexus card ready for I’.D.and immigration. The ground staff told me I had to have a passport and proceeded to insult me in front of the other passengers . Eventually at my insistence they called their supervisor . The supervisor naturally told them I was perfectly entitled to use nexus. So, EXTREMELY STRESSED I got on the plane in zone 9 .No apology of course . PURE IGNORANCE! Arriving in Vancouver was extremely efficient and quick, just as the departure had been even with clearing TSA and US immigration in YVR before we left. AVOID DFW LIKE THE PLAGUE!!!

reviewText: Dallas fort Worth is the third largest of all airport in passenger traffic, and it is still under heavy development. This comes with a toll both literally and metaphorically. Yes every car going out the airport need to pay the $2 fee! This is by far the only airport I recall that takes the fee. The plane landed on the run way. Then it took another 30minutes or forever long taxiing inside the airport and wait here and there to reach the gate. Then to get to a different gate inside the terminal it took another 1mile walking here and there with additional Skylink train. Even inside one terminal C you would have to take a Skylink to get from 27 to c2... So altogether budget something like a hour minimal if you are connecting there!!! It became a journey and experience for me. I will not transfer here unless it is international flight. Then it is the messy construction of the airport which makes even our professional van driver complain none stop. It is not an airport you can navigate easily. Inside the terminal multiple restroom fixture need to be fixed immediately. It certainly feels third world quality. Due to the slowness and some delay my connection was missed. But this gives me the whole understanding of how crappy to be number 2 in the world could mean in reality :)

reviewText: First time at Dallas Fort Worth International Airport (DFW) and it was a great experience. After landing, luggage pickup was smooth and fast. Taxis were readily available right outside the exit, and Uber and other ride-share pickup areas were clearly marked with designated spots. Free Wi-Fi is available with unlimited access, which was very helpful since I was traveling internationally without a data connection. Check-in was quick and hassle-free as I was flying with Air Canada. Staff were polite and efficient. I boarded from Terminal E, and the security check was smooth and fast. Terminal E has a few good restaurants and convenience stores. I had breakfast at IHOP around 5 a.m., and the service was quick. Overall, DFW is a well-organized airport and offers a hassle-free travel experience. Would definitely recommend.

reviewText: Reisekaos am Flughafen Dallas (DFW) 📅 6. Januar 2026 Am 6.01.2026 herrschte am Flughafen Dallas (DFW) absolutes Chaos. Um 10:00 Uhr erhielt ich meine Bordkarten (Dallas–Atlanta–Amsterdam–Düsseldorf, Delta) und zahlte 166 USD extra für Gepäck. Um 11:15 Uhr wurde der Flug komplett gestrichen. Delta buchte mich auf Lufthansa um und versicherte, dass die Koffer nach Düsseldorf geliefert werden. Am Lufthansa-Schalter warteten wir stundenlang, der Flug war voll, meine Kinder durften nicht mitfliegen (nur ein Ticket war gebucht). Zurück bei Delta: erneute Umbuchung über London, keine Bestätigung, keine E-Mail, keine Hilfe. Bis 20:00 Uhr liefen wir mit Kindern und Übersetzer zwischen Schaltern – ohne Unterstützung durch Personal oder Flughafenpolizei. Neben enormem Stress entstanden finanzielle und berufliche Schäden. Nach 48 Stunden erreichte ich endlich meine Heimat – ohne Koffer und ohne jegliche Auskunft. Dieses Maß an Fehlmanagement und mangelnder Koordination ist inakzeptabel. ⭐ Nicht empfehlenswert.

name: Dallas Fort Worth International Airport
fullAddress: 2400 Aviation Dr, DFW Airport, TX 75261, United States
reviewText: Within the vast tablelands of North Texas, Dallas Fort Worth International Airport rises like a choreographed exercise in concrete brutalism gradually softened by time and ambition—a 17,000-acre testament to how infrastructure evolves from pure function toward human experience. This sprawling complex, larger than Manhattan island, serves as both operational colossus and inadvertent architectural museum chronicling five decades of aviation design philosophy. The airport emerged from a fractious municipal rivalry, with Dallas and Fort Worth abandoning separate airport ambitions only after federal intervention in the 1960s forced their collaboration. From this tense partnership came a revolutionary concept by Japanese-American architect Gyo Obata of Hellmuth, Obata & Kassabaum (HOK), whose semi-circular terminal modules—designed explicitly to minimize walking distances and maximize parking—inadvertently created one of aviation's most distinctive formal signatures. "The humanizing thing about airports is not that they are pretty but that they are easy to use—to hell with monuments!" Obata insisted. Yet his utilitarian modules, when seen from above, coalesced into what critics later termed a "Stonehenge of the American prairie"—a rigorously geometric counterpoint to the surrounding landscape when the facility opened in 1974. The airport's most significant architectural addition is Terminal D, completed in 2005 as DFW's international gateway. This 2.1-million-square-foot, $1.2 billion structure represents a collaboration between three Dallas firms: HKS Inc. (managing architect), HNTB (lead design architect), and Corgan Associates (architect of record). The terminal received Buildings magazine's New Construction Grand Prize (2006), recognizing its delicate balance of security requirements with passenger experience. Terminal D's structurally expressive roof, featuring 11 acres of stainless steel in an Inverted Seam system by Zahner, exemplifies architecture as environmental response—reducing cooling costs by 90 percent during peak hours while creating distinctive spatial character beneath its continuous form. The recent groundbreaking for Terminal F, designed by PGAL, Gensler, and Muller2, signals a departure from Obata's horseshoe concept. This $1.6 billion structure, opening in 2027, will employ modular construction techniques pioneered in the High-C Gates project by Corgan, recipient of a Texas Society of Architects Design Award. What elevates DFW beyond mere infrastructure is its integration of art within the passenger experience. Dennis Oppenheim's "Crystal Mountain," a 45-foot aluminum sculpture in Terminal D, creates an unexpected moment of wonder, while the exterior sculpture garden curated with the Nasher Sculpture Center introduces travelers to one of the world's premier collections. The High-C Gates interior fit-out by Corgan introduces biophilic elements reminiscent of park settings—a stark departure from the original terminals' pragmatism. These "outdoor-inspired" spaces with premium materials signal recognition that reducing passenger stress requires more than operational efficiency. In the trajectory of airport design, DFW represents the pivotal moment when aviation architecture shifted from utilitarian infrastructure to experiential environment—a compelling document of how monumental scale can gradually adapt to accommodate both technological imperatives and human needs.

reviewText: Expectations have to be managed when walking into a la Madeleine, but in general this is one of the better locations. There's a nice fireplace in the dining area and it's reasonably big in comparison to the one in the River Oaks area (for example). If you're not familiar, you order at a counter, pay, and bring back a marker - then they bring your food out to you. They have complimentary jam and bread; neither is anything great the bread is hard and the jam is prepackaged. Drinks are also self-serve and includes tea, soda and water. There's also wine but that you have to order. As part of my search for good food with calorie counts listed, I came here several times in a row trying different combinations of soups and sandwiches. Here are the sad results: the soup is best. Tomato basil: ridiculously salty. I can't believe they sell jars of these; do people water them down when they get home? Country Potato: actually pretty nice; but be careful if you're calorie counting they will add cheese and bacon etc. to the top; ask for the soup without the toppings if you want to save on calories. Otherwise it's a nice filling, thick soup. Jambon-Buerre: I tried the ham and the swiss separately to figure out which of them was providing that almost chemical taste to my sandwich. I concluded that it was both. I'm scared to try the croque-monsieur because I assume it's made with the exact same ham and swiss. There was an exorbitant amount of butter on this. The baguette is actually really lovely. You might consider just getting a baguette. Chicken Salade Croissant: Oh so sad. The croissant isn't buttery or flaky at all; rather something waxy like the ones they have a Walmart. The chicken salad is also pretty sad; flavorless and drenched in mayo to mask the lack of quality of the chicken. French Dip: Horrendous roast beef quality. The best thing about this sandwich was also the baguette. The stale taste of the poor quality roast beef is doubled by the fact that it is served hot. They accept contactless payment.

reviewText: Definitely one of the better managed La Madeleine bistros. Light crowd on a cold day was not the reason for the delightful experience. It is as French as faux Cajun is for those who haven't tasted the real stuff but we don't mind it at all (having had the genuine stuff in France). reviewText: I never, ever write negative reviews. It's just not something I do. I love writing positive reviews, but this time I cannot hold back. I feel so nostalgic about La Madeleine. I remember a time with the food was incredible. Fresh, beautiful, wholesome. But they have clearly sold their soul and cut every possible corner but kept prices high. My business partner and I had breakfast for $45 for two French Country Breakfasts, French toast and two cups of tea. The eggs were ordered over-medium and came out looking like shoe leather all tough and brown. They were entirely inedible. I was raving about the potato galette but ours had sat on the warming plate so long (this is still only 9 am) and were tough and chewy. La Madeleine used to have the most marvelous strawberry and blackberry jams - made with real fruit. Now you get served a plastic thimble filled with a liquidy sugar that has some strawberry or blackberry juice. Overly sweet with no taste of the fruit. They used to have rotisserie chickens but corporate gutted the soul of freshness and realness and now they use factory-made, frozen chicken in the salads. I used to love the lemon tarts - but now for $4+ dollars they give you the tiniest of tarts that is mostly sugar cookie shell. Just not worth it. It's the classic sweetened condensed milk + egg+ lemon tart. I can make a whole pie of that for less. It is just so sad to see this once shining star of the "fast casual" dining experiences just go down the drain. I never minded paying their premium for the food because it used to be good. We seriously would have gotten better hash browns at Ihop or McDonald's. Just don't disappoint yourself and unload your wallet at the same time. You don't need to add insult to injury.

reviewText: I'm a BVD patient and drove from San Antonio for my first ever Neurovisual exam. From the first contact before they ever met me, they listened and were very compassionate and helpful in doing the steps to schedule the exam. Costs were laid out for me, and somehow they got my insurance to cover this - no one else has been able to do that. I've been messing with this for over a year, and my current optometrist was just at the point of "OK we'll try this" and when it didn't work and made my symptoms worse, it was "Sorry no refund". I'm sorry what? Turned out just as I suspected. My previous doctor wasn't bad, but he doesn't have the knowledge at all to handle real, true, BVD/convergence insufficiency. Dr. Kevin does. I told him we were banning 3 words from our visit: vision therapy, progressives, and Neurolense. He was just like "OK fam, bet, if you don't want it you don't want it". I'm paraphrasing but not by much. I was AGHAST. Through every step of this elsewhere, I've had people pushing brands at me. Both Bruce, my tech, and Dr. Kevin were laid back and fun yet very professional to work with. I'm in healthcare myself and they both respected that, as I respect that I came to THEIR specialty for help. Mutual professional respect is sadly rare. I deferred to their expertise because it's not my field, and they respected my professional knowledge and didn't talk to me like a 5 year old. It doesn't seem that difficult, and yet it often seems to be. They were very hospitable and considerate. It was raining heavily at the end of my appointment, and when I said "OK this is awkward, but yanno..... problems of the convergence insufficient..... I can't drive in heavy rain" they were happy to let me sit by the fish tank with coffee until it let up. Before my appointment I dragged my dizzy miserable self in having all but given up hope that ANYONE knows what to do with this, and left with a glimmer of it, feeling heard as an individual and not just an MRN and a potential sale.

reviewText: I wish I could provide two separate reviews, one for the doctor’s office and reception, and another for the frames section. Doctor’s Office and Reception: 5 Stars Dr. Eric is exceptionally knowledgeable, kind, and takes the time to thoroughly explain everything. The technicians are also very nice. Frames Section: 1 Star (or negative 5 Stars if I could) Unfortunately, my experience with the frames section was extremely disappointing, and here’s why: After my consultation with Dr. Eric, during which he prescribed changes to my current reading glasses, a technician escorted me to the frames section. Upon arrival, she handed my folder to an individual (I believe his name was Marcus) sitting behind a desk in the back of the store to order my new prescription glasses. Immediately, I was asked -for the third time that day- if I intended to purchase new frames. When I explained that I preferred to use my existing frames (which I love), it seemed to put him in a sour mood already. Subsequently, he began rattling off various add-ons such as progressive lenses, etc, etc. When I asked for clarification, his gave me this attitude, as if I was expected to understand the jargon. Even after I explained that I was relatively new to glasses and apologizing (stupid me omg!), he continued with an impatient and very rude attitude, questioning if this was my first time buying glasses. Then came the question, "How do you want your glasses?" When I asked what he meant, he repeated the question in a condescending manner: “how - do - you - want- you - glasses?” 😳. Despite my explanation that the glasses were for reading, his impatience persisted and abruptly pointed out that I had two prescriptions and demanded to know how I wanted them, as if I should have known this information without it being explicitly communicated by the doctor. Feeling increasingly uncomfortable and totally unwelcome, I decided to stand up, paid for my visit, and left. From the moment I entered the store, it felt as though their primary concern was whether I would purchase frames from them. In summary, while the doctor and the office staff were great, but I wouldn’t recommend buying frames there.

reviewText: I moved to Austin almost a year ago, but I put off finding a new eye-care professional until a freak situation led me to needing a new contact prescription as soon as possible, so I did some urgent searching online for offices near me and found Lakeline Vision Source. What stood apart from the other offices I saw in the results was their hours of 9-6pm, I recently started working a job that might have allowed for a late afternoon appointment, but then I saw they even offered Saturday appointments and immediately decided that the convenience was worth the shot. They have the option to schedule an appointment online even as a new patient and I was able to be seen the very next Saturday when looking for an appointment on that Wednesday. They sent me a link to fill out forms online before my appointment which I always appreciate for streamlining the actual new patient appointment process. I have worn glasses/contacts for over 13 years, so it’s all a very routine for me, and the process at this office was super seamless. They even let you text them information like your insurance card. When I arrived for my actual appointment, front desk staff were super nice, very welcoming, and there was very little wait before I was seen by a technician. He was very cordial, knowledgeable, and graceful with the preliminaries of my exam, and I was also seen very quickly by Dr. Eric Hammond, who very efficiently determined the proper prescription for my contact lenses, and double checked that the minor scars he could see in my eyes were truly just scars from past infection, and not anything needing treatment. He was very personable and also gave me advice that my pupil size being above average might make me a bad candidate for lasik surgery, if I was ever considering the procedure, and while I had never seriously considered it, that information has never been told to me before although I had already been made aware that my pupils are larger than some. It really made me feel as though Dr. Hammond pays attention to the bigger picture of a patient’s eyes rather than just doing the bare minimum. If in Austin when the time for my next exam rolls around, I will definitely return. They accepted my insurance, and I was pretty pleased with the overall cost and care. If you asked me personally about my experience, I would recommend Lakeline Vision Source without qualms.

reviewText: I dined at your restaurant this afternoon. I won't go into detail about how delicious the food was—though it certainly was—but what I really want to share is something that happened afterward. After finishing my meal, I left in a bit of a rush and accidentally forgot to take my backpack with me. Inside the backpack were my passport and wallet, so when I realized I had left it behind, I was extremely anxious, fearing it might have been taken by someone else. By the time I returned to the restaurant, it had already been two hours since I left. When I asked the staff if anyone had seen my backpack, a young waitress told me that she had found it and had tried to find a way to contact me. Unfortunately, there was no contact information inside, so she decided to keep it safe for me in the meantime. She then kindly returned the backpack to me. I’m incredibly grateful to your restaurant and to that young waitress (I was so relieved and overjoyed to have my bag back that I forgot to ask her name). I would like to express my appreciation for the honesty and kindness shown by your staff.

reviewText: 💕There’s a couple of things that I loved about this place: 1. Customers order at the register instead of the table. 2. You immediately get your dessert or paisley from the bakery as soon as you pay for it. In essence, the baked goods are like appetizers but much FASTER. 3. The kind staff greets you when you come in and when you leave 💚🤍💚🤍 4. The tables and restrooms were clean. Note: The bathroom decals are in French. Just an FYI, Madame means ‘Mrs’ so that you walk into the right restroom. 5. The food was delicious and my entire order was under $38! I ordered a build your own omelette which is originally under $12 with three ingredients. I had tomatoes, spinach, onions, bacon, and cheese. Yes , I know you can order and one te anywhere but this is what I had a taste for 🍳🥚🧀🥓🍅🥬🧅The omelet comes with two slices of tomatoes so you don’t have to add it to the omelet if you wish to save money. Since each ingredient is $1 more , I paid $14, not bad. My daughter ordered a kid’s scrambled egg and bacon with a side of fruit. The kid’s meals are under $6. Each of our meals came with a croissant. In additions, I ordered to vanilla fruit parfaits that were each under $3 and a great proportion. I am very picky about parfaits but the baker did very well with the taste and size ! The fruit didn’t taste watery like some other places. Also, the fruit salad watermelon was cut the perfect bit size. It was sweet and fresh ! If I sound picky, I might be 🤓 6. The atmosphere is very relaxed/ laidback and I saw many different groups of people just as if you were really in 🇫🇷💙 When you walk in, it seems like all the elderly people sit to the right and anyone under 40 seemed to take a left. 7. The baristas/waitresses were wearing cute berets because that’s…. Classic French👌🏽 8. The drinks are self serve. Additional comments: Kind staff and clean bathrooms matter ! ✅💚 This is a snob free environment. There was a rude customer who received judgy eyes for her behavior to kindly let her know to behave 🌝 The croissant was a little dry but still good. I ordered French coffee but the French coffee dispenser was empty. I ended up drinking American which was not any change in price. Four stars total for the great experience and my daughter wants to come back to this family / kid friendly cafe 😊⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

reviewText: I live in the Dallas area, DFW has been my 'go to' airport for many years. I just returned from 1 week vacation, I was horrified and embarrassed by DFW. No problems with my departing flight from terminal B. However, I returned to terminal C. It felt like I was in an impoverished nation that was at war. There is a lot of construction going on, which is necessary I guess to keep it modern, but there was NO SIGNAGE to direct people. I walked around looking for the place to catch a terminal link bus. Doors were locked, closed off, not accessible. I walked half an hour looking for a door that would lead to the buses, and asked 4 different employees where the door is, got 3 different answers, none of them were correct (1 was an AA employee that did not even look at me, she just moaned "mmmm"). I eventually followed another passenger that guessed which door would lead to the terminal link, he guessed correctly, and that's how I got to the bus. It is worth noting that the terminal link driver was working very hard on a hot day, he was very friendly, professional, and very much appreciated. With all the money spent on construction, why can't they spend a few dollars to post signs and arrows to show people where to go?

If you enjoy pastries and casual French café food, this is a great spot, and I definitely recommend stopping by.

reviewText: ⭐⭐⭐ We had our breakfast at la Madeleine, and overall it was a pleasant experience with a few ups and downs. The ordering system is quick and convenient, which makes things easy — but in trying to be fast, some of the quality gets lost. The coffee wasn’t very flavorful, and the hygiene of some serving areas could definitely be improved. That said, the food itself was really good, and the pastries were amazing — probably the best part of the whole experience. The decor also stands out. It feels like you’ve stepped into a cozy countryside house — with brick walls, exposed pipes, and a warm, rustic charm. I really loved the atmosphere. I’ve been to this place multiple times, sometimes for just coffee and other times for meals. It’s always busy and full of people, which shows how popular it is. The staff are friendly and always smiling, which adds to the positive vibe. For me, I wish the quality of coffee and cleanliness matched the great decor and delicious pastries. Still, it’s an acceptable experience overall, especially if you love cozy places with a good pastry selection.

Casa de Julia no es solo un restaurante, es una experiencia. ¡Volveré muy pronto!

name: Lakeline Vision Source
fullAddress: 3419 El Salido Pkwy #100, Cedar Park, TX 78613, United States
reviewText: I received a confirmation email after booking the appointment, and also received reminder text messages as well as online paperwork to fill out prior to checking in the morning of my appointment. When I arrived,I was greeted with 2 smiling faces when I checked in. Both ladies were friendly and pleasant. I only waited a few minutes before I was called into an exam room which was relaxing, neat, clean, and tidy. The tech that helped me was friendly, personable, efficient, And hygienic. After we did the standard eye exams, she led me to a larger more formal exam room, where Dr. Corey entered, just moments later to go over lenses with me. He checked the health of my eyes and addressed any questions and concerns that I had. He then personally walked me over to the final station where the customer service agent pulled a tray of frames for me to try on at her desk that varied in weight and color and design. I told her that I was interested in seeing options and needed help picking one. And she did exactly that! We talked over the pros and cons of the different styles and she let me try on the final choices multiple times until I made my final decision. She was very patient and friendly and professional. My family and I have been coming to this specific location since 2019, and we have always had an amazing experience. 10 out of 10! Highly recommend. Side note: the bathroom and coffee/water stations were organized and clean and well decorated. This painting was so cute I had to take a pic! ❤️

From the reception, the technicians, to my Dr of many years , Susan Shauger,, OD, and Marcus the Optician I could not find better care and and compassion for the patient. I more than highly recommend Lakeline Vision Source - your eyes will very happy!! Paul

reviewText: I can’t recommend Dr. Jennifer Catalasan highly enough. She brings a level of care, empathy, and genuine human connection that’s rare to find in healthcare. What stood out to me the most was how she treated me—not just as a patient, but as a person and an equal. So many times with doctors, especially from older generations, there’s a sense of distance or hierarchy. But with her, it’s the opposite. She truly listens, takes the time to understand what you’re going through, and collaborates with you to find the best path forward. It feels more like you’re talking with a knowledgeable friend who happens to be your eye doctor. She’s a refreshing reminder of what compassionate care should look like.

reviewText: Me encantó la experiencia en esta cafetería (Webster, Texas) por las siguientes razones: ambientación, carta, atención y calidad de los productos. Su oferta de pastelería se inspira en las tradiciones francesas, entre las que destaco variedades locales de pie de limón, tartaleta de frutas y pastel de chocolate. Además de sándwiches, también hay bebestibles y productos envasados como mermeladas. Se puede consumir en la misma cafetería o pedir para llevar. Mención aparte merece el sector de los baños, donde, mientras uno se encuentra haciendo uso de ellos, se escucha una voz femenina en off que da clases de francés (con traducciones al inglés, obviamente), en un acento muy castizo y que convierte a esta experiencia en algo más académico y divertido de lo que pudiera ser en cualquier otra parte. Recomendable ciento por ciento.

reviewText: The food and atmosphere were phenomenal! The young lady at the bakery check out counter was friendly and very customer oriented as was the young man directing people at the tray pickup. reviewText: This place was great. It has a very welcoming feeling to it when you first come in, greeted by a large display of pastries and bread. The ordering process was a little funky, sort of like a buffet. You have your order taken at the front and then move to the register further down the cafe and pay. We didnt have the server there because he was taking a tub of dishes in the back, so the manager stepped up and got us taken care of. I got the croissant french toast and my wife got the chicken salad sandwich. The french toast was so rich and decadent, but light. The chicken salad had an amazing savory flavor with sweet walnuts (I think.) The entire experience was fantastic and I know I will be coming back. I also think i will go get bread from them for my next get together.

reviewText: Their bakery selections are absolutely scrumptious. You can taste the freshness and quality ingredients in every bite. Just looking at them makes your mouth water in anticipation. Their savory choices are fresh, healthy, and you can see everything that is being served. There are choices for everyone no matter what sort of eating regime you follow. I had a personal size quiche florentine and a small fresh fruit salad. The quiche was creamy and delicious. It melted in my mouth. Their mango iced tea was brewed just right. They had a fresh french bread bar across from the drink station that had butter and two kinds of jam to go along with the two kinds of french bread. You can look at their menu online or look at their menu when you get there. The selection is great! This place is worth several visits to sample and enjoy every thing it has to offer. Great place for a meal or just coffee and dessert. Meet friends or go by yourself.

reviewText: While visiting with my Mom she took me for breakfast at La Madeleine's. I'm here on Vacation for 3 weeks from Leavenworth Kansas. It was an absolute wonderful experience. The only issue would be a door that opens automatically or someone to help disabled customers enter more easily. My Mother is oxygen dependent and with her wheel chair & oxygen tank in tow, it was very difficult entering the store. Another customer saw our struggle and opened both doors for us. Other than that it was a wonderful dining experience. The quality cleanliness and service are top notch. The prices are also very reasonable. We give it 9 out of 10 stars ☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆ ( it would have been 10 stars if getting inside would have been easier)

reviewText: Once we enjoyed it here now not. While La Madeleine remains popular, its transformation from a charming, authentic French café to a more generic fast-casual chain is complete. reviewText: La Medline is an absolute gem for anyone who appreciates high-quality European-style cuisine. From the moment you step inside, you’re greeted with a warm, inviting atmosphere that transports you straight to a charming café in Paris or a cozy bistro in Italy. The attention to detail in the decor, the soft background music, and the delightful aroma of freshly baked pastries set the stage for an unforgettable breakfast experience. The menu is a perfect blend of classic European flavors with a modern touch. The croissants are buttery, flaky, and simply melt in your mouth—easily some of the best I’ve had outside of France. Their eggs Benedict, served on a perfectly toasted baguette with a velvety hollandaise sauce, is pure perfection. If you have a sweet tooth, the French toast topped with fresh berries and a drizzle of honey is a must-try.

reviewText: My experience at La Madeleine was incredibly disappointing. My mother had been eager to visit this place during our vacation in Pasadena after hearing about it from a friend. Despite several family members warning us that the restaurant wasn’t great, we decided to give it a try to make my mom happy. At first glance, the restaurant seemed cozy and inviting, but unfortunately, the service left much to be desired. It was, without a doubt, the worst customer service we experienced during our two weeks in Houston. From the moment we walked in, there was zero empathy or willingness to guide us through the process. The menu was outdated and worn, and we were confused about how to order since they offered à la carte options, a buffet, and a bakery. When we asked for help, the instructions were vague at best. When it came time to place our order, we were directed to another staff member who was incredibly rude. She handled our payment, and we asked where we would get our coffee—whether we should wait for it there or if it would be brought to our table. Her response was dismissive, repeating over and over that the coffee "would come to us." I asked again for clarification, and she snapped back with an irritated tone, saying the same thing. Once we sat down with our food, the coffee never arrived. When we asked the person serving the food about it, she said we needed to serve ourselves. The same rude cashier returned and curtly told us that black coffee is self-serve, as though we should have known that. I tried to explain that this was exactly what I had been asking earlier, but she became defensive and acted as if it was my fault for not understanding their process. How could I possibly know how things work in a place I’ve never been before? I came here to give my mother a pleasant experience, not to deal with staff who lacked basic courtesy. The food was mediocre, the place may have been cozy, but the atrocious customer service completely overshadowed everything. I wouldn’t recommend this place to anyone. Save your time and money and go somewhere else.

reviewText: I went in around 8:30 am. I was greeted by Ava. The interaction was fine until I noticed I was wrongly charged for an item. I ordered a French dip sandwich, caramel macchiato, blueberry muffin, crème brûlée, and some mini cookie pack that was at the register. The cookies were priced at $2.99 but I was charged $3.99. When I brought it to Ava’s attention she said they put the wrong stickers on all the mini cookie packs by the register. I said shouldn’t you honor the price that it currently is labeled with. She then started to give me an attitude, rolling her eyes and asking me if I wanted to speak to the manager. I told her I don’t need to speak to a manager; I would just like my $1 refunded as my son was already eating the cookies. She then walked away and came back and was like I have a $1 here do you want it or want it back on her card. She was giving me an attitude but maybe today was not her day. So, I just took the $1 bill and waited for the rest of my food. I took a sip of my hot caramel macchiato at the store and it was cold but didn’t want to interact with her again so I just took it and left. I will start of by saying the blueberry muffin, French dip sandwich, and cookies were good. The caramel macchiato was cold so I just microwaved it and it was good. But the crème brûlée was horrible. I don’t know if it was the prior interaction about the $1 issue was the reason, but I received the most burnt creme brulee I have ever seen from this store. The whole top layer ( sugar part) was not caramelized. It was burnt a layer of black burnt sugar. The taste was horrible even when I tried to scrape it off. It was also so dense and didn’t taste like the usual crème brûlée that I buy when ordering from this store. I’m trying to give Ava the benefit of the doubt because she might be having a bad day, but the interaction over the cookie price was not needed. If it says $2.99 they should honor the price and then remove the rest of the cookies from the front register until they print out the correct price. Btw, She did remove the rest of the cookies but seemed annoyed and threw them at the counter behind her.

Upon pulling the plastic container out of the bag, my mother showed me what appeared to be leftover toast with a thin smearing of avocado on its surface. reviewText: I've always enjoyed my visits to La Madeleine, but this particular one is what made me sit down and write a review. I received news today that a family member passed, so I was a little depressed walking in. I was looking forward to the lemon madeleines, my favorite bakery item there, but they were out. I was understandably bummed out. Well, we get our food and sit down to eat. My husband discovers his eyes were too big for his stomach, and he doesn't have the room to finish his coffee drink. I walked up to the cashier and asked for a to-go cup and expected that to be the end of it. Instead, she offered to pour it into the cup for us, and she warmed it up for him without us asking. Then, as we're standing up to leave, the same gentleman I asked about the lemon madeleines caught me as we were about to walk out and handed me a small plate with a single madeleine on it, fresh from the oven. He said he saw how disappointed I looked when he told me they were out, and had a fresh one brought to me. Those two small gestures really turned my day around. I was really down after getting the news of the death in the family, but their wonderful customer service and their going above and beyond brought a smile to my face. Linda and Ricky were their names, and that restaurant is fortunate to have such great staff that genuinely care about customer service. Thank you both for helping to make my sad day just a little happier. You have a lifelong patron.

reviewText: To the employee with blue hair and bad service. I love La Madeleine. I have been coming to this location for the past 10 years and have always had a wonderful experience with both the food and service. Two nights ago, my boyfriend and I had ordered, had our meal inside, and were about to leave when we decided to stop by the bakery to grab a dessert on our way out. Waiting in line a few minutes to closing behind a customer who was ordering. By the time they finished and received their order, the time was apparently 3 minutes after closing and the person at the front, a lady with blue hair, said "Oh we're closed now." To which we responded in confusion. She then further proceeded to repeat herself saying, "Yeah we closed at 9" and it was 3 minutes after closing and we hadn't realized. We explained to her that we were already waiting behind the customer before us before they were closed and while it didn't seem like she was gonna serve us, someone else said to her, just serve them. She proceeded to roll her eyes and take our order. We were out of there in 3 minutes. You never, never talk to a customer that way. I get people walking in right as you close or even after closing because they see people are still inside, I get the frustration of that, but no matter when they walk in, you serve them. That's customer service. You never let them stand in line and when the clock hits closing, try to turn them away. Terrible service and someone ought to tell this girl otherwise.

reviewText: I have always loved this chain, and had a good mark at this location a few years ago, but, my, how they have fallen down! The young gal who took our order at the register clearly didn’t want to be there — and made us feel like she didn’t want us there. Normally, La Madeleine, in keeping with its French tradition, has fresh breads, jams, and butter out. Here they just had a few leftovers out from the previous day, though they had been open almost an hour, plus no jam or butter. So I asked. I did get a helpful, apologetic man to bring out jam and butter. He noticed the few pieces of bread and said, “Oh, they didn’t bring the bread out? Let me get it!” So, I thought, “All’s well that ends well. At least I will be getting fresh bread now.” Au contraire, mes frères ! He brought out a tray from the fridge under a cellophane wrap, upon which a sticker indicated the bread had been baked the previous day and was to be tossed the next. reviewText: The first time I ate here, with shortly after they opened the restaurant. It was so busy that they couldn't keep up, brought us the wrong food, brought us food that was cooked the wrong way, in a general just botched the whole meal. So, I waited half a year to come back and try it again. Six months later... The food is okay. The folks seem very nice. This time, it wasn't crowded at all. The food was cooked correctly, but they didn't really have what I wanted. Specifically, I prefer my eggs poached, and they either don't know how to do that, or have some sort of Health code issue with cooking them that way. I will say that the first time I was here they did have poached eggs. Of course, they didn't cook them right and I complained about it. So maybe, they just took them off the menu. All in all, the food was okay. The French toast was very crispy and delicious. Parisian eggs were just okay. That said, I everything on my plate, so it can't have been that bad. 12 Months later... All in all, this is an okay place to go. I end up not going to get very often because they don't poach eggs. That's kind of my favorite way to have headaches so, I take that into consideration when I consider going here. Let's forget about the eggs for a while. Here are other good things about this place. The Ambiance is nice. I really like the decor. And, I like other menu items. They have a fried potato side dish that's really very good. They have quiche, which is tricky to pull off. And they have an array of baked items that are just delicious. As I pointed out to someone in answer to their question about the restaurant, they have a pretty good coffee bar. It's self serve, so you fix it the way you like. I think they have a bottomless cup concept here, so you get as much as you want. They also have a fresh baked bread section that's self-serve. On that station are jellies, jams, and butter. That's pretty good too. I enjoy going back to get a variety of combinations of Breads and jams.

reviewText: My friend and I came to this restaurant because he had a craving for the complementary toast and at the time, what I thought included coffee. Now he looked pretty laid back and like he wanted to joking around with us. He ask us, "Now who's got the tab?" Mean while I think this guy is joking. I said "Oh man, guess that's me". He replied, "You guys just sat at the table and didn't order a thing, but have been drinking coffee and tea the whole time." At this point I realize he's no longer joking and is fed up with us for having a great time at what I thought was an great place to start hanging out at... Now don't get me wrong. I would have happily paid for the drinks without anyother thoughts or complaints, but it's the way he treated me at this moment is where I'm really ticked off. He thought I was just another teenager with no morale guidance. He thought I was the scum of the earth and he was absolutely rude beyond belief! In the end, I did pay for the beverages, But I will not forget the confrontation I had with this man and will not recommend this restaurant to any young person looking to have a good time. To the employee who had judged me so blantantly, I kindly ask of you to please correct yourself. Thank you.

reviewText: It seemed like a nice little spot! I didnt really get to experience it though. I was looking for a place to take my new puppy to experience an atmosphere other than my apartment. La Madeleine was listed under BringFido as “dog friendly,” so thats where we went. They were polite about it, but we were kicked out. We were allowed to sit outside, but the uncomfortable outdoor tables on the edge of the parking lot (on all sides) were not fun for me or my two small dogs. So then I have my pom’s leash in one hand, my baby pup in the other, my purse wrapped around my body, and now I have a coffee to carry that I didnt even actually want LOL. Pure chaos. But hey its fine. We’re exploring. We left and embarked on a very unpleasant adventure trying to find a place to sit and enjoy a little time out… failed, and went home. The servers were very nice and polite, which is why I still gave 4 stars! I just think its just worth mentioning for anyone else in the future, that it is NOT really dog friendly unless you want to be a foot from traffic with no barriers.

reviewText: The ordering system is garbage. You feel really pressured to hurry and order rather than being able to take your time to look the menu over. reviewText: During the first week end before they opened food was terrific, the service was very slow and that is to be expected with a new restaurant but after they officially opened food quality was not very good or impressive. Any food that is already sitting on the grill is hard and cold on the top and the bottom is warm and hard. name: la Madeleine
fullAddress: 2110 Louisiana Blvd NE, Albuquerque, NM 87110
reviewText: Not terrible, but we weren't impressed. It felt like we were in line at a Furr's cafeteria, and the food was about the same quality. Everyone stands in a line, often stretching onto the sidewalk, and menus are passed out. Customers are told to choose what they want before they get up to the counter, to ensure that the line moves quickly. A server takes orders towards the front, as customers stand in line, and instructs everyone to keep following the line. Felt like a cattle chute--but it was lunch rush. Servers behind a glass pane hand out soups and sandwiches along the line, if customers ordered them, and you pay and collect your drinks and a number for your table at the end. Like I said, think Furr's/Flying Star. We should have read more about the place before going in--we didn't expect that type of dining environment, and I think that kind of threw everyone in my party off. The menu tempted us with tasty-looking mimosas, but alas--the place doesn't have its liquor license yet. Food was too salty for my taste. Pastries weren't anything special. The tomato basil soup was good! Tart. All in all not my cup of tea, but it is a very popular place, so obviously many other people enjoy it! Give it a try!

name: la Madeleine
fullAddress: 2110 Louisiana Blvd NE, Albuquerque, NM 87110
reviewText: My mom ate at La Madeleine from Maryland long time ago and I learned the other day that there's one in Louisiana and we decided to eat there for Lunch. When we got there, the parking space outside didn't feel right for us because we have to be aware of our surroundings and whatnot and it was very tight and not enough space. That aside, the inside of the restaurant was really nice and bright. It captures the essence of France very well and I like it. The desserts look really yummy and sinfully sweet. The dessert I ate was the "Fruit Tart" or something like that and I really enjoyed it very much because when it comes to eating foods like this, I prefer to take very little bites and savor the moment. My lunch tasted really good, as well. I think it was "Roast Beef Sandwich" with Caesar Salad on the side. Sorry, I'm putting air quotes because I don't have a very good memory of what happened a few days ago. Other than that, my order tasted so good especially with sauce that it came with. It was yummy in my tummy and I was satisfied with it. The employees working at the restaurant in my point of view were doing a good job even though they just opened recently. I'm really glad I gave La Madeleine a try and I would like to come back again in the future. It would be nice to treat my sister and my brother in-law and they would go nuts with the nice, delectable selection of desserts but I wouldn't get my hopes up just yet. All in all, I hope and pray that this restaurant will do fine and get better in the future as time goes on. I'll visit again, later on.

reviewText: Food was okay for ABQ. Americanized French food. Definitely not authentic in any sense of the word. And, they just shouldn't even try to greet you in French. It's embarrassing to any of us who speak the language. reviewText: What a disappointing experience. We ordered our Thanksgiving dinner about a week and a half before Thanksgiving and picked up on Thanksgiving day. Not only did they give us insanely tiny portions, but the lids were not properly placed on the containers, and you can tell it was thrown together. When I brought it to the managers attention, he did not apologize, but proceeded to bring out our correct order. The food quality was terrible and this is the last time I will ever order anything catered or to go from this restaurant. After years of ordering their holiday food, I am sad to see it go down the drain. Never again, lesson learned. Almost $300 thrown away. I had to consistently apologize all night long for the poor food quality, and the fact that the portions were so off. I ended up just leaving the restaurant unhappy because I spent an additional 30 minutes walking them through the correct order. Save yourself the trouble and do not place catering orders at this restaurant. I am not sure what has happened over the last few months but their quality and service has gone down tremendously. The management does not care and should be replaced immediately. What a sad and disappointing experience, sad to say, we will not be back.

reviewText: First off, I hadn’t been to an eye doctor in 2 years because of a horrible experience so I was skeptical about going here, but glad I did. I brought my old glasses which I had not been able to wear, and she looked at them and told me before I had the chance to answer I couldn’t see out of them, which I couldn’t. She built a pair of glasses and had me walk around to make sure they suited what I needed. She actually spent the time to explain things, give a referral for a doctor she would personally use, and told me straight out what to do and not to do. She is very straight to the point and doesn’t sugar coat things, so if you need things sweetened up for you see someone else. If you want a doctor who will listen, evaluate, and create a course of action, then see her! The people up front helping with the glasses were also excellent and helpful. I will definitely go back here next year for my annual checkup!

reviewText: First and last time here. We walk in to order and see a menu with recommendations on certain pizzas to try. We chose two different recommendations and proceeded to tell the person behind the counter. They take down our order and ask for a name on the order and write it on the pizza paper. They then hand is off to 3 other people on the line to fulfill the order. They must all be extremely untrained because they all ask what i want on my pizza and didn't even bother to look on the paper. Why provide recommendations if you won't just make it? I was confused when they asked for me to build my own pizza, granted that's an option, but i didn't want to do that. We then finish telling them what we want and are at the end of the line standing there confused on where to go. Do we get a buzzer to know when it's ready? Do we pay now or later? Why is the register facing away from us in a hallway blocking other traffic to the back tables? Just unorganized and chaotic in my opinion. We get to the register and checkout with a gentleman that couldn't be less friendly. It's like you tried to find someone with the worst customer experience and hired them. If you know there are no buzzers to alert a person on what to to or where to go, why aren't you directing customers to let them know what's going on? When we got to the register, they should know exactly what we ordered without having to repeat our entire order to the cashier which slows the process down. If i wasn't honest, i could have lied, which in the end could hurt your sales. We finally checkout and proceeded to pick and wait at a table. Their method of letting you know your order is ready is to call it out. Not bad, but again i shouldn't have to listen for my order since I'm dining in and trying to have a good experience with my wife. It would be ok if i was dining out. We got our pizza which the wait time wasn't bad. It was fairly quick. However, the pizza itself was rather tasteless and soggy. I've had my fair share of brick oven pizza and that was a sorry excuse of a pizza. I recommend a short, but longer default time of cooking. This is my opinion, but you should possibly poll people on cooking preferences because it tasted like raw dough. Overall, terrible experience. I would go back if it drastically improved. At this moment in time, this pizza business is out of business to me. NOT RECOMMENDED!!!

reviewText: I had to do a business trip to a certain merchant around this area, and decided to go to La Madeleine. I just moved here from Tennessee not too long ago, so I have never tried this place before. I decided to get a sort of chicken pot pie, and sat outside. The first bite was excellent, and then the second bite, I heard a large crunch sound. I pulled out a dime right out of my mouth like some magician. I was terrified on what happened. I did not want to make a big scene, so I nicely went over to one of the workers there, and just explained to them what happened so they can just be aware ... and just take more precaution so it does not happen to someone else. The worker apologized so much, and was saying sorry like no other. She had asked me if I wanted a replacement meal, and I kindly declined, as I did not want to have them make me another meal when they were already busy. As I was about to leave, the lady was so very kind to actually hand me a to go box with a fresh meal, and insisted that I'd take it. I thanked her for what she did, and left. This time, there was no dime in my food. Sadly, I do not think I will be going to La Madeleine, just because I feel like if I see their food, I'm seeing a dime with it too. But over all, that first bite was excellent.

reviewText: DFW was my home airport for most of my life...after retiring and flying even more I fully appreciate DFW Airport. Large enough for just about every airline in the world the airports multiple terminals are connected by a post-TSA, free tram system that runs constantly. With so many airlines the airport is also home to many club lounges. From the Capital One Lounge to the many Admiral's Clubs and so many in between for a respite away from the crowds. Weather and thunderstorm delays are common in spring and summer. Always a good idea to be in and out of DFW earlier in the day rather than late and face cascading issues.

reviewText: We started our morning, not knowing where we were going to end up for brunch, but my boyfriend and I ended up at one of the best restaurants in San Antonio. The exterior of the place does not do justice to the interior. We were greeted by Maria, who is happy to tell us how their ordering system worked. After reviewing the menu we went on to receive our food, which was ,to say the least, exquisite it was cooked too perfection and exploding with flavor. The atmosphere is inviting as well as clean ,we observed the teamwork going on in the kitchen and took notes of all the family style decorations. We sat next to the fireplace, which gave it a very nice touch. The food was so good that we came back for dinner. Here are a few pictures to show the experience. This restaurant is definitely five out of five and is instantly our new favorite. Pricing is economical because my opinion that the food is worth far more. The dessert menu is vast and they even offer housemaid jams and marmalade as well as salad dressing. They even had little gift bags just in time to pick up a last-minute Christmas gift. You won’t be disappointed if you’re in the area Stop on in and if you are a little further it’s worth a drive.

name: la Madeleine
fullAddress: 722 Northwest Loop 410, San Antonio, TX 78216, United States
reviewText: No wonder La Madeleine is going under - my closest location has already closed and this one might as well be next. - Why are servers not taught “Customer Service” any more? - And the words “I am so sorry” when something goes wrong seems to not even be in young people’s vocabulary any more -at least not here! Had ordered meals online - was trying to pickup via their “take out parking spots” - FIRST problem, their phone system instructions didn’t work, however way I dialed in I got into their answering system loop -> so in I have to go (not too much of a deal, I’m elderly but still mobile). - Looking through my order bag, SECONDLY I notice utensils when I clearly stated “no utensils” (not a big deal again - but just “no attention to details”) so off I go. - THIRD: Headed out and started driving in heavy traffic, we noticed items missing from the order, completely: a salad, a soup! -> Now it’s becoming a big deal; I drive back, walk in, talk to same front person, tell them I’m missing items - and what do I get: “oh, what do you need? - what did you order?” - I point to the order strip, show salad, soup - and get “ok”. - And off they go grabbing the stuff! - Coming back, I get “here you go” - THATS IT. Really ??? - So I give them one more chance and state calmly “needless to say, I am not happy having to come back” - and lo-and-behold I get another stare, and a “really”. …. At that point I am becoming speechless myself - and do walk out. Some battles cannot be won; but I *will NOT be back*. - Their food is not what it’s been, and I don’t need to be treated as a nothing! - Now, this all could have been avoided with ONE SIMPLE “I am so sorry we missed that”! (a small extra cookie would have been an extra [Christmas] bonus, but was not expected).

reviewText: This La Madeleine offers a spacious and clean environment, perfect for a relaxed meal. Their menu is extensive, with options for breakfast, lunch, dinner, and pastries. We tried the build-your-own baguette, which was delightful! The ability to choose between hot or cold options with fresh ingredients on delicious bread, paired with a refreshing greens salad, made for a satisfying meal. The French coffee was good, though I wish there were more than just a drip option. The Chicken Friand was a standout – a perfect blend of tender chicken, sautéed mushrooms, and a rich sauce wrapped in a flaky pastry. Each bite was a burst of flavors and textures. The baked potato soup was also fantastic—creamy and flavorful, with onions and leeks adding a nice touch. Overall, a great spot with delicious food and a welcoming atmosphere.

reviewText: First time here, was pretty disappointed as I was looking forward to getting a traditional french breakfast. I really wanted eggs benedict with a true, homemade Hollandaise sauce, and they don't have that. The menu was pretty basic. The pastries, however, looked amazing. Got the croque madame, one of my favorite French meals. It wasn't very good. I wanted sunny side up, they said no, which is weird, not sure why they can't as everyone else in town will. So they gave me an "over easy" egg, but it was way overcooked and nearly over hard. The. Read was way over toasted and very hard. Very little garlic cream sauce. The potato gallery was delicious. They have a bread and jam bar, but the bread was stale. The cook wasn't wearing any hair net or hat! It's counter service as well, which I'm not fond of. It was a $20 breakfast for me, so I expected a delicious and perfectly prepared meal. Not what I was expecting and definitely won't go back unless it's for pastries or dessert.

reviewText: On the way home from work, we visited LA MADELINE FRENCH BAKERY & CAFE for dinner, and had an unimpressive culinary experience. The atmosphere is very nice - especially the big warm flaming fireplace on a cold winter evening - but the food was bland and tasteless. We ordered the French Onion Soup and Original Caesar Salad for appetizers, then the Salad Sampler and the Salmon with Kale & Butternut Squash. The French Onion Soup was tasty, but lacked enough cheese and tasty bread. The Salads were quite good - maybe the best part of our dinners. But my Salmon was overcooked, dry and tastless - like a re-heated frozen dinner. We've been to Paris and other cities in France dozens of times, and this was definitely NOT quality French cuisine! Maybe mediocre Parisian café fast-food. To add insult to injury, they only offer 3 selections of tasteless house wine: White, Red, and Rose. A French Restaurant? Yeah Right. There are several other bonifide French restaurants in Old Town and NorthEast. We are not wasting our money again. La Madeline's is NOT RECOMMENDED.

reviewText: The food here was almost inedibly bad. I ordered the kids chicken, rice, and broccoli for my 4 year old, which comes with a fruit bowl. The rice concoction was swimming in some kind of watery mushroom cream and the rice itself was some wierd pilaf. There were tons of mushrooms and random huge chunks of soggy bell peppers...disgusting for adults but most definitely a kids worst nightmare. Even the fruit was somehow horrifying. The grapes had definitely been frozen then defrosted - their texture was so soft and pliable that I could leave finger indentions in them. The melon, on the other hand, was so hard that I had to spit it out, I couldn't even chew it. My teenage daughter ordered a smoked turkey and brie hot sandwich with sauteed onions and apples on it. It came out looking like school cafeteria food. She ate it but only cause she didn't want to waste it. It was pretty gross. The restaurant looks nice from the outside and who doesn't like French food? Well, I was duped cause as it turns out, la Madeleine is the one who seemingly hates food in general.
