reviewText: 11/12/23: DISAPPOINTED on multiple counts.. It is my son's birthday today & our household has been sick with a flu/cold for a week - altho we are finally starting to recover we are still extremely congested & coughy so conscientiously chose "To Go" online order vs eating inside (which might've gotten employees & other customers sick). I arrived early, called & informed them that I was outside for whenever the food was ready to please bring it out - they said ok. Time elapses & it's now a few minutes before ready time (order said it would be ready 8:12pm) so I asked my sister who is not sick to go inside to check on the order - oddly, the food was all bagged & waiting on the counter for us (me wondering how long the food sat on the counter..). My sister brought the food to the car & I ensured everything was there & spotted the onion soup had no cheese nor croutons/toast so she went back in & she informed them - they said it's supposed to have them (we know, that's why we pointed out they were missing) & gave her a side baggie of those items. 15 minutes later we arrive home with the $90 meal including a whole Sacher Torte (my son's Birthday cake). At least the 4 diff soups were warm & delicious. The Quiche Lorraine was luke warm at best. The Crêpe la Madeleine was cold - yuck (me wondering again how long the food sat on the counter!?). I opened the Strawberry Spinach Bacon Salade & notice no dressing anywhere - I start eating but realize there's tons of bad soggy decaying spinach - gross! Not a happy camper & hope I don't get food sick 🤬 At least the Sacher Torte (we've ordered it most years for my son's birthday) was delicious altho a bit smudged.. altho much better than the year I picked it up & it had cracks all over it due to someone not making/storing it properly. Unfortunately it seems like the quality standards at La Madeleine is going downhill (their salads used to be top notch & hot foods served hot) - I have no doubt they would've fixed these things had I been eating onsite & raised them in person but alas I was sick at my home 15 minutes. By the time our meal ended around 9:15pm La Madeleine was already closed (they close at 9pm) - much too tired from my illness to deal with calling them & having the rectify the issues some how..

reviewText: Was passing through Albuquerque and looking for a place for a nice dinner. Saw this place, looked at the menu online, and decided to try it. Big mistake. When we walked in the girl behind the counter told us to take a menu and look it over and she would take our order. We sat at a table waiting, not knowing we were supposed to order at the counter. Ok, our fault, but I didn't expect that in a "nice" restaurant. We had to go back to the counter to find out that we had to order there, nobody came to tell us. I was ordering the "pick 3" salad/soup, my husband ordered the Crepes Madeleine. I asked about substituting a potato as one of my choices and the counter girl looked confused, (she was so soft spoken we had to ask her to repeat things several times) and said she'd have to charge for it. I just went with the regular pick 3, and tried to order a glass of wine, which any respectable french restaurant should have, asking for a pino grigio, which confused her and she said they only have white wine (lol) I said Chardonnay? and she repeated the "only white wine" statement. In the meantime a gentleman came up and said they only had rose. Ok, a glass of rose it is I guess. Then we apparently had to pay in advance, which felt more like a fast food place, and the machine wanted my husband to put in a tip - I don't know about anyone else but we tip according to service and so far we hadn't gotten any. I got French Onion soup, Caesar's Salad, and fruit salad. The so called fruit salad was a small cup of basic fruit that I could have gotten at Denny's for $1.00. The Caesars salad was adequate but not great, and the french onion was not too bad. My husband's crepe dish came out cold and "muddy" in flavor. The same gentleman that was at the counter and had brought our food came over, and after some discussion took the crepes back and my husband just got a bowl of the F.O. soup. The ONLY reason I gave this place 2 stars is because of the gentleman who did actually give us service, he went above and beyond, I wish I got his name. Everything else about this place was just ..well.. ehhhh.He DID get a good tip, he was the only one that deserved it.

reviewText: Update: Management took my very small complaint ans mishap very seriously. They called me, apologized and asked me how I preferred to make it right. I went to the desk to pay and ordered a caramel macchiato and a blueberry muffin. I picked my muffin and came back to the table to wait for my drink. I was sitting waiting for my guest, she came about 10 minutes later and we talked at least another 10 minutes and I still hadn't gotten my drink. I saw him coming with other drinks and he says did you ever get your hot chocolate? I said no. He gave me a hot chocolate that he had on his tray on the way to the other table, so I didn't get what I paid for. I didn't complain because I was with a guest but I couldn't understand why it took so long or why it was wrong after that. I was the only one ordering at the time and the restaurant was very slow. The muffin was good but I would have liked if it were warm. I'm glad it was something small and sure it was just a mistake so I would go back.

reviewText: A huge airport, mostly beautiful. The terminals are connected by a ground-level metro. However, my experience using this airport included many negative moments. I flew through this airport twice, both times with American Airlines. On my first trip, the flight was canceled due to weather conditions, even though we spent 3 hours sitting on the plane on the runway before being returned to the terminal. None of the other flights took off either. Airport staff advised everyone to stand in line for refunds or rebooking. I stood in line for 3 hours, but eventually gave up because the line seemed endless. I had to spend the night at the airport. In the entire huge airport, there were only two small areas with rooms where people could stay overnight—both were fully booked, and the cost for one night was $200! I had to sleep on hard chairs. Some passengers slept on the cold floor. In the morning, I stood in line for another 3 hours at customer service, where I was told that I would not receive a refund or a rebooked ticket, as the airline is not responsible for weather conditions. I had to buy a new ticket myself. The new flight was delayed by half an hour. And when I arrived at the gate, I found out that the boarding had suddenly been moved to a different terminal, so I had to run to make it.

reviewText: Two stars because the pastries are excellent. La Madeline absolutely ruined my Mother's Day morning. I'm a divorced mom so I don't get showered with gifts and I have to treat myself. I started planning my day the day before and planned to have a mimosa, eat a chocolate croissant, drink some good coffee and relax away my morning. I planned ahead and found that La Madeline has curbside pickup. I order pastries for me and the kids along with a mimosa for curbside pick up. The first thing I noticed was that there were two different telephone numbers on the confirmation email I received. I thought it was obvious that the number with the 201 area code was a typo but when I called the local store number, it sounded as if someone picked up and hung up. I had to get out of my car, defeating the purpose of curbside pickup and walk to to where about 20 delivery drivers were waiting to ask about my order. The lady wrote my name down and said she would check. I went back to my car and finally got through via phone. It was about 11:40 and my order was scheduled to be ready at 11:30. I was told they'd have my order out in a moment. I waited and waited. I spoke to someone next after 12 and was told they ran out of pastries and had to bake more muffins and croissants I reconfirmed where I was parked and the make, model and color of my vehicle. I waited and waited I next called to speak to someone around 1pm after I debated leaving but knew I wouldn't be able to find breakfast anywhere else at that time. Marie, the lady I had spoken to previously asked my name and where I was parked as if I hadn't spoken to her before. Ten minutes later I saw someone waking toward my car. My mimosa wasn't there so I asked for it and it was brought to me minutes later by another lady who looked at my children in the car and wished me a Happy Mother's Day. My morning Mother's Day plans were absolutely ruined as I had spent the morning parked in the La Madeline parking lot waiting for pastries. I had a terrible experience and all I wanted to do was cry. Marie, the lady who answers calla for curbside pickup never gave me a clear time frame for when my order would be ready and in the hour and a half it took for my order to arrive, I watched delivery drivers come and go and saw people drive up, go in and order and leave with their orders. Terrible experience! If my coworkers or the owner of our firm suggest LA Madeleine for weekly lunches or Friday breakfast orders ever again, my answer will be no.

reviewText: Nice space. Excellent location. Sad food. Even if you order from the menu and ask to eat in and you wait for them to deliver to your table, make sure you explicitly told them you want your food heated up! unless you want it notably cold off the shelf. Even heated it will not be hot, you'll get somewhat warm at best. The mushroom soup is good. The croissants are unfortunate, even "toasted". Perhaps their oven was not working properly, the past several visits, spanning ~two months. Nothing has seemed fresh/worth getting excited about. Sad because the menu options look/sound good. Some of the servers are exceptional, thoughtful and responsive; several are just barely fulfilling a job. Remember to ask them to heat your food unless you want the temperature and texture to be sitting-on-a-shelf-for-hours-or-more.

reviewText: I was not impressed during my visit today. Walking in, the atmosphere is nice, if a bit sterile. A sign indicated where to go to dine in -- but it turns out that you don't do that. Rather, you stand at the entrance of the restaurant with other patrons and look at a menu. When you're ready, you tell someone holding a tablet what you want, and then you go to a cafeteria-style line and repeat what you just ordered to them. Then, you reach a register at the end, and you tell the cashier for a third time what your order was. There are several logistical questions I have about this process, but the foremost one is: why do things so inefficiently? Our food came quickly once we sat down, but it was nothing to write home about. Everything was both quite salty and bland, though I do think that the bread my sandwich came on was fantastic and soft. Still, a meal for two with a latte was just under $30, which is absurd for the quality of the food. As an aside, there is a little table where you can get bread slices, butter, and jam, which is a nice touch -- but the butter was in little plastic containers, and every tiny dollop of jam was in another plastic container, which is needlessly wasteful. Pros: Friendly staff, clean restaurant, decent selection, the desserts looked good. Cons: Ordering process built on disorder, mediocre salty food, high prices, lots of wasted plastic.

reviewText: Very inefficient order system which is frustrating to the customer and results in a lot of employees standing around doing nothing. As others have mentioned you wait in a line outside the door to be greeted by an order taker - they only have 1 person in this role. As you can probably imagine, this results in a long line of employees with no customers in front of them as customers are discussing with the order taker how the restaurant works, what they want, etc. This results in the line outside the door getting longer and longer through the lunch rush. In addition, all the employees seem to have been given different instructions as none of them could agree on anything (ie - get your desserts at the cashier but when you get to the cashier she tells you she doesn't do that - you have to go to the "to go" line to order desserts; order taker says you get your salad from the salad person, only to be told by the salad person that since it is a "side" it comes on your plate). Overall, as a customer, I found this whole process confusing and frustrating. The customer in front of me had to go back to the order taker half way through the process because where you order "french toast" is with the order taker, not the "hot grill plate" person. The food came out quickly after the 1/2 hour wait to order and get through the process. It was okay - not great but okay. The dessert was very good though. I think I will wait awhile before going back and will modify this review if things improve. For now, I recommend staying away as they work out the kinks. Advise to the management - reconsider the whole order taking process - maybe put in "ordering stations (multiple)" or consider having a few order takers.

reviewText: Dallas Fort-Worth International Airport (DFW) was one of the most streamlined airports I have ever been in. I got off my flight, the signage to the exit was simple to understand, and what I appreciate the most is the fact that the Ride-Share pickup area was easy to identify. I walked outside. Ordered my ride. The ride app told me to find the nearest pickup location. The location was clearly marked and easy to find. This made my pickup process so easy. Before exiting Dallas Fort-Worth International Airport (DFW) I had to stop by the restroom and this was one of the CLEANEST restrooms I have ever seen at an airport. I'm talking absolutely spotless. Speaking of, that gate area was spotless as well. Shout out to the cleaning crew responsible for Dallas Fort-Worth International Airport (DFW) as their work is amazing and appreciated. I landed at night so I didn't get a chance to appreciate the exterior structure of Dallas Fort-Worth International Airport (DFW), however, from what I did see, the airport has a simple but sleek classic design. As I landed and headed out I didn't get a chance to shop or visit any food spots so I'll make sure to do that on my way out. See you again soon Dallas Fort-Worth International Airport (DFW).

reviewText: My husband and I had a highly unpleasant experience during our visit. From the moment we walked in, it was clear that customer service and cleanliness were not a priority. We stood for a while with no one ready to greet or seat us, and when we were finally told to sit wherever we liked, no one came to take our order. We eventually had to get up and seek someone out ourselves. Most of the tables were dirty and remained unbused throughout our visit, including ours. The table number signs were sticky and unclean, which only added to the discomfort. Despite the restaurant being almost entirely empty, our food took longer than expected and arrived cold. To make matters worse, we were not given any utensils or napkins, nor were we directed to where we could find them. As for the food — the steak bites in my husband’s crepes were tough, stale, and tasted like they came from a can. My crepes, quiche, and chai latte were all extremely underwhelming. We were also surprised by how limited the crepe options were, especially for a place that advertises itself as a creperie. Overall, this was a frustrating and disappointing experience. We won’t be returning anytime soon — if ever.

reviewText: La Madeleine? More like La Misérable My wife and I recently visited the La Madeleine in Gaithersburg, MD, and it was, without question, one of the most disappointing dining experiences we’ve ever had. We walked into a lifeless atmosphere, greeted by a host whose demeanor matched the room — dreary and unwelcoming. Trying to look past first impressions proved to be a mistake. The bakery area looked disheveled, with pastries that appeared stale and no inviting aroma to suggest anything fresh was being made. Service was nearly nonexistent. We had to grab our own menus and seat ourselves, surrounded by dirty, uncleared tables. Even after waiting, no one came to take our order, so we went up to the counter. When our food arrived, the tables around us were still filthy, and we received no utensils or guidance on where to find them. The food itself was no saving grace. My beef crepe stroganoff was bland, with meat that looked and tasted like processed canned beef. The entire dish turned my stomach, and I felt unwell even after returning home. La Madeleine in Gaithersburg is a disorganized, poorly managed, and unappetizing establishment. I’d sooner grab breakfast from a fast food drive-thru than set foot in here again.

reviewText: I’ve got mixed feelings about DFW. On the positive side, the airport itself is genuinely impressive. It’s well organized, very clean, and easy to navigate. The tram system that loops around the terminals is a real convenience and makes getting from one end to the other pretty straightforward. However, the downside and the reason I’m knocking my rating way down is the issue of last minute gate changes. In my case, a sudden gate change came in so late that we ended up missing a connecting flight entirely. That kind of disruption can turn what would have been a five star experience into a pretty frustrating one. In short, DFW has a lot going for it, but if they could manage their gate change notifications more reliably, it’d make a world of difference.

name: Dallas Fort Worth International Airport
fullAddress: 2400 Aviation Dr, DFW Airport, TX 75261, United States
reviewText: Major parts of the airport smell like sewage. Even the water at the bottle filling stations has a slight sulfur smell to it. Maybe that is a temporary problem associated with the renovations? That issue aside, the airport has multiple design issues. The main problem we had was with a luggage setup coming in from an international flight. We got through border control and followed the arrows for a transfer flight. There was a guy shouting to everyone to put their bags on a conveyor. Ok, I figured maybe this was one of those customs scans in some places. Nope, it was a security check for bags for transfer flights, which would be fine if we weren't changing airlines. We were told to wait in one place, which we did for 5 hours since we had time to kill. Our bags never showed and the American Airlines staffer there was completely lost about their job. Eventually we found one of four of them that showed back up at our incoming airline baggage area. Why didn't all of our other bags that went into the same process also get dropped there? Who knows. Meanwhile, We have multiple lost baggage requests out. We know they are at DFW, but no one seems able to figure out what is going on. I'll definitely do what I can to avoid this airport in the future. If you have other options, I suggest perusing those.

reviewText: First of all, the hours state they are OPEN until 10. We arrived at 9:45 coming into town from a long trip looking to make a to go order. The doors were already locked. We went back for lunch today. There were several people working, 3 available to help through the salad line and it seemed no one wanted to. Finally the girl who did help looked like she hated life. My salad was made sloppy and my cup of soup bowl was dirty. Our glasses for our drinks were foggy and wet indicating they had been washed but they were turned upside down which could harbor bacteria if not aired out properly. Once I dried it with a napkin, there were water stains and smudges. as we ate and people left, tables were not bused or cleaned off. A man spilled his drink trying to clean off a table himself to eat at and still no one came to his aid or offered to replace his drink. We then went to the bakery counter to get dessert. There was one person working it although like I said earlier, there was someone standing at the register for an empty salad line and the girl who helped with soups went to the back. One man kept walking back and forth but did not offer to help the individual behind the counter. Because the bakery worker was alone he kept walking away from customers to get boxes for to go desserts as they were speaking. He also had to manage the register. The line was backing up almost out the door so we left. I personally have worked at a la Madeline and I've been to several in different cities. This had to be the most poorly maintained and run location I've ever visited. The customer service was below par and the functionality of workers and roles was non existent. Hopefully changes can be made to ensure a cleaner environment and enhanced overall experience.

reviewText: Bonjour! I typically don't write reviews that include the good and the challenging, BUT in this case and after some thought, I decided to do so. I am a long term patron of la Madeleine locations since high school. The Preston Rd. location in Dallas was actually my very first job (during the time when Patrick was still involved). And during this time of Covid and inability to travel internationally, the Lakeline location in Austin has given me a small "taste" of what I miss, enjoying a coffee and croissant in France. I have always found Melinda to be a wonderful asset to the location (and la Madeleine as a whole) which is why I choose that location vs. others in Austin. She's always been kind, professional, sincere and especially patient during what appeared to be the most challenging times... like yesterday. I am not certain what the end result was, but yesterday one of the cooks was heard arguing with Melinda over what seemed, "bacon". I don't know the prep/cooks , so I don't have a name (and wouldn't share in a public forum like this, anyway). I was surprised and disappointed, especially because Lakeline is always so pleasant to visit for enjoying a bite, a drink, listening to the cafe's music (when not busy) and/or getting some work done. Obviously, I understand that work places, especially those in hospitality and retail, come with a great deal of stress. I sincerely hope that yesterday's lack of professionalism and disrespect (in my opinion) isn't a sign of the future for this otherwise, lovely location. I hope this is read by the Corporate office and that perhaps some conflict management/communication can be done, if not already. And I hope that Melinda is supported as much as she supports her patrons (even the ones who choose to treat her poorly). Until next time, KG

reviewText: It can be a confusing place. Rental vehicles are not directly connected to airport. Look for ground transportation signs or go to ground floors. There is a free shuttle to all rentals. Plus there are individual shuttles at rental drop off to your terminal. Big help. Tsa checks were easy in the 1st plant of morning, but after 545 am, will get long fast. There are more than one. reviewText: We had a connecting flight from Cozumel to Nashville, which had a hour and 50 minutes layover. We weren't to worried about it until we landed. We and Everyone else had to line up about a mile long to go through TSA. People cutting in line, crying and angry! We had 7 minutes until boarding. reviewText: DFW International Airport is mostly clean, well-organized, and presentable. There was some construction going on in Terminal C during my visit, so be prepared for possible delays and expect a good amount of walking—especially if you’re relying on the terminal shuttles. The delays I experienced were due to American Airlines, not the airport itself, so I won’t hold that against DFW. TSA was smooth and efficient, and the agents were not only professional but also had a good sense of humor, which helped make the process feel calm and quick at the same time. One of the best parts of DFW is the food selection. Everything is located past TSA, and the transport between terminals makes it easy to find whatever you’re craving, no matter which gate you’re flying out of. Whether you’ve got time to kill or are just grabbing a quick bite, you’ve got options.

reviewText: Went here with my spouse and a friend after a movie since it was close and we didn't have anything else planned. Atmosphere was nice but a bit on the loud side so had a hard time holding a conversation. The food? Well in my husband's words for his spaghetti, he's had a certain pasta out of a can that tasted better. I thought he was just having an off day but I tried the leftovers I made him bring home(I don't like to waste food) and admittedly it wasn't great at all. My entree which was the pappardelle was not impressive in any form. It was supposed to have sausage which I swear I would have found more of as a topping on a pizza than what was in that entire dish. I have no clue what in the world people are going on about this place food wise. The whole point of going to dinner afterwards was to grab something more decent than the movie theater and apparently our apps there was far better than our dinner. On a last note, please use at least filtered water when serving tap water. The service was decent and friendly and that was pretty much the highlight of our experience here. IMO, the overall experience was utterly forgettable if it weren't for the simple fact movie food outshined this spot and it's the only reason it will continue to be memorable at this point.

name: Cedro Scratch Italian & Wine Bar

reviewText: Wow, what a surprising disappointment 😞. I say surprising because we've eaten here twice before and loved it both times. (Other than the 30 minutes it took to bring my fettuccine alfredo 🤔🤷. My wife shared her plate with me until mine arrived. Anyway, we just went again tonight for my wife's birthday. I could not wait to have my alfredo again! I had talked it up so much to my (alfredo loving) son, that it made the disappointment that much worse. Maybe they have a new chef, maybe new management (which I would suggest looking for another job because I don't think this place can last through the year). Regardless, the alfredo wasn't the same ☹️☹️. Last time there we loved the calamari. This time the portion was so small, I could have counted how many pieces of calamari they served, but the few were hidden under the carrots and pepperoncini! Sad. ☹️ My wife only had mussels and again, they were done differently and portion was less as well. I guess shame on the owner. What a wonderful opportunity to bring a great Italian restaurant to Cedar Park! (I haven't found one yet) I had been spreading the word to everyone I know, but unfortunately I can't do that anymore. My wife and I both agreed this would have to be our last visit. Finally, we decided to sit on the patio for dinner...WOW! I couldn't have imagined what a dumpy area that was! Let's just say they don't need to worry about chaining up their tables and chairs! Beautiful place. Dumpy patio Dump (ish) bathroom Small portions Currently overpriced. EXTREMELY poor ownership/management

reviewText: I went in for breakfast this morning expecting a good experience; I have been to the South location and they are great. I ordered the spinach quiche and potatoe galette out of the display case. The quiche was fine; the galette was cold, but no big problems. My friend ordered strawberry French toast, which has to be made fresh. When the French toast was brought to the table, it was two pieces of dry, unbuttered toast with a few sliced strawberries and a messy drizzle of sweet cream. It looked nothing like any French toast I've ever seen. My friend brought the dish back to the front to ask about it, and the employee at the front counter immediately started yelling at him, loud enough for the whole café to hear. It was pretty clear that he was not willing to refund, replace, or change the order. Another staff member (I'm assuming a manager) came to our table a few minutes later and offered to bring something else (she was much more polite), but honestly, by then we just wanted to finish the food and get out of there. I understand that restaurants have their own "spin" on a lot of dishes, but there is no version of French toast that involves bread that hasn't been soaked, and besides that, the employee's reaction was completely unprofessional and very off-putting. I'm definitely not returning to this location or recommending it to others; if you really want to visit a la Madeleine location, I'd say it's worth it to drive the extra 30 minutes down to Brodie Lane and Ernest Robles.

reviewText: I have been going to Cedro ever since they opened. I know the food will always be good. I prefer going when it is not crowded as the noise level can be very distracting. During this particular visit my friend and I were treated to the most outstanding service. The young man that took care of us, was the only server at that time. And when we told him we were very hungry he did his best to get the food out quickly! There was another gentleman who wasn't waiting on but checking on each table. He had a beautiful Italian accent. Definitely added to our experience. Between the two of them we felt taken care of. Perhaps a bit too taken care of. While we appreciated being checked on, we had trouble getting through our conversations. I cannot complete the service review without mentioning one more thing. Our server would actually come by to wipe away the little puddles that formed underneath our glasses! Yes! He lifted the glasses and wiped the water away. I confessed that no one had ever done that before. That was an "above and beyond effort" if ever I saw one. As for the food, we both chose the Vegetable Conchiglie which, I believe used to be called Vegetable Orecchiette. I have had that many times and it is always good. Always. We ordered the yummy focaccia bread and used it to soak up the wonderful ragu sauce. What prompted us to go there was the coupon Cedro sent me via text. Very smart. They are not inexpensive. The coupon was a nice bonus.

reviewText: I was born and raised in an Italian family...so, OK, I have my biases. Cedro boasts to be a scratch Italian eating establishment. I have to disagree. No Italian meal starts without some form of bread on the table. You have to 'order' it here. When it arrives, it ain't Italian bread. It's some sort of light weight toasted white bread dress up in cheese and toasted. WHAT? That food...I ordered the Bolognese Pasta Dish. OK, the pasta...they didn't put enough salt in the pasta water at the beginning of the process to begin with. So, it was kinda flavorless in my opinion, then add to that, it wasn't exactly al dente....it was sort of undercooked on the inside and overly mushy on the outside. My guess is they crowded the water pot. Grandma would have slapped her forehead and rolled her eyes. Moddonna!! The Bolognese....textually, I would describe less as a meat sauce and more as a soupy mixture of ingredients. I'm assuming there was some meat it there. What was in there I would describe as sparse. Overall, the dish had way too much sauce vs. pasta. Flavorless soupy 'meat' sauce poured over but not clinging to badly cooked pasta. $23 plus $6 for the 'bread'....wow! Forget a side salad, would've been another$7. No thanks. I'll give the place decent stars on atmosphere. It was busy and lively. That's what one would expect in this type of genre. Overall, pricey not so good food in a busy rub elbows lively place. If you're looking for that atmosphere, I recommend to go there. If you're looking for good Italian fare..well, not so much.

reviewText: Poor service. I have been eating at this location over the past year. I like the food, but the service is most often poor. It is a busy establishment and they can't seem to handle the crowds. It has become the most poorest service I have ever seen. When you order for pickup, and follow the directions to send them a text message for pickup, it's often ignored and you have to go inside and wait in a line. They even cut their phones off from time to time so you cannot call them. The sandwich that I got today was not made properly and was very dry. It did not have all of the ingredients on it that it was supposed to have. I don't take "busy" as an excuse. I paid for the food and expect to get what I paid for. I watched a manager today be very rude to a lady who had a mistake on her order and a gentleman who ordered a coconut cake yesterday and paid for it showed up today waited about an hour only to find out they were out of coconut cake. I waited over an hour as well for my pick up order because they did not have directions for pick up communicated to customers. They were not following their normal pick up procedures. At this point absolutely loathe this place. The food is fair, but I've had a lot better. This establishment needs to take a lesson from Spot of Tea in Mobile Alabama. Spot of Tea not only has excellent food similar to the food of this franchise, but the service is impeccable for very large numbers of customers. I watched a lot of people give La Madeline a lot of grace today, but I'm tired of giving them grace. It is a busy restaurant -it's always busy so they need to learn how to handle it and treat people nicely. And they need to communicate to the customers instead of turning off their phones to run from their problems!!

reviewText: I'm giving this clinic a two just because their staff was very professional and really did try to help me. Unfortunately, the technology behind their neurovisual department and prescribing of prism glasses. I recently went to a pediatric opthamologist who specializes in eye misalignment and ocular muscle problems. I found out that I could have just stayed in town to get prism glasses and also that eyeglass prescriptions of eye misalignments of less than 1 diopter probably won't make that much of a difference in your vision. I am disappointed in myself that I didn't do my research and spent so much money and time traveling several times to another city. However, I believe the staff was well-meaning and probably believe that they are truly helping people. I would say, please check with your local pediatric opthamologist first and go from there. There is obviously a lot more and different training that goes on with an opthamologist than an optometrist, and it is probably better to exhaust your local resources first. If you have other symptoms, you probably need to address those before going through the long, expensive, and stressful process of getting prism lenses at a neurovisual clinic.

reviewText: La Madeleine is a good place, however being French, I wouldn't say they are a French Bakery and Café per se. It's good but not very authentic. I would advise to go there if you don't know French food and want to be initiated slowly. It's a very Americanized French food. So beside my disappointment in looking for authentic French food, it's good, not too expensive. The other little malus of that chain is that it is difficult to get something without bacon, but that "issue" is common to lot of places in Texas as far as I know. Advise: just check their menu before going there to be sure they have something you could enjoy. Be aware that's a first step to try French food, but a good one if you are worried to not like French food. On a side note, and because I can't leave a review without talking about the crew working at a place: the team is nice, friendly and you shouldn't worry about bad service (except once in a while, because they are humans that can have a bad day like everybody else ;) )

reviewText: Have been here 3 different times of day and am glad I did! First was for coffee and croissants. Fast service and croissants are 7 out of 10(I am an afficianado) better than most others out side of France. The French baguette not so much. The second time was for dinner. The Madelaine pasta with chicken was fresh and very tasty. The sauce could have benefitted from a tad more cream(okay I am a nitpicker), but was definitely good enough to take leftovers home for lunch. The third time was for Sunday breakfast. Perfectly cooked eggs. I will try their croque Monsieur and pain perdu, on future visits. We will make this a regular stop. P.S. This is order at the desk, get delivered to table service. Pick up utensils at the drinks bar. There is a cozy gas fireplace. The ceilings are too high for an intimate dinner....It is somewhere between an upscale cafeteria(no disrespect meant) and full service restaurant/ coffeebar.

reviewText: After visiting other La Madeleine locations, I wasn't ever overly impressed. Today I visited this location and was blown away. Not only by the tasty food, but by the amazing service. I walked in with my 4 year old and 2 year old. I came I to contact with 4 different employees and they were gracious, polite, and beyond helpful and just genuinely friendly (extremely hard traits to find in employees these days)! They were engaging with my kids and just all around warm! I unknowingly ordered a pesto pasta with cheese (my youngest can't have dairy) and tried to order one without cheese and willingly pay for it, because obviously it was my mistake. The chef insisted that he would make it again, without dairy, at no charge. I tried to give back the pasta with cheese bc we hadn't touched it, yet. He smiled and told me to feed someone else with and wished my a good day. I was blown away! La Madeleine can be on the pricey side when feeding 4 peop, but I will most definitely be back to this location!

reviewText: This is the most insane, terrible, unorganized airport I've ever been seen in my life. I travel a lot and I've been to many airports. And each time you have to take the skylink train to go to the other terminals. I swear I walked like 12 miles over the course of 7 HOURS just trying to get a flight home that wasn't delayed or canceled or changed for literally no reason. DO NOT schedule a flight with a layover at this airport. And if you absolutely have to. Bring lots of snacks. Don't spend a dime at this airport. reviewText: Not sure how this place has 4 stars. Had a horrible experience here which killed my anniversary night. We did not enjoy our food. The only thing we liked (not loved) was the Carbonara pasta we had. What made the night worst was the service, OH GOD!! Our waitress was so bad. At one point I saw what it seemed the manager or owner grab our waitress arm and scolded her about something in the middle of the restaurant. This was very awkward and not professional. I felt uncomfortable. Not once did our waitress refill our driks, gave us our pasta and didn't even ask us if we wanted parmesan cheese, and took forever to look for her to ask for our checks. When we finally asked for the check she literally went to the bar instead to dry wet wine glasses and flirt with a man sitting in front of her. After 20 minutes waiting in awe we waived her over and she comes over and was like "Oh right! Your check! I forgot about that!" Really, you don't say? When we finished our "Carpaccio" and the server comes with the main entres... he didn't even ASK if he could grab the empty plates we were finished with. Just left all the used dirty plates there. We didn't even have room for everything in the table. This was incredible. This place is not cheap, and looks pretty "fancy", however the food and terrible service made it one of the worst restaurant experiences I've had.

reviewText: I've tried to enjoy this restaurant on multiple occasions. At first, I gave them the benefit of doubt due to them recently opening the Louisiana location. Now that it's been almost a year and the quality of service had only gotten worse and more inconsistent. Pros: The recipes offered are tasty. It's also nice to see a company calling themselves a bakery that actually makes loaves of bread. Good salads are hard to find in Albuquerque. They offer a couple interesting selections. Cons: Inconsistent. Occasionally I'm greeted with a smile right away, most of the time I wait without acknowledgement while several people stand with their backs to me even when there is no line. The quantity of food is different every time. Out of the last ten visits, I was satisfied with the serving size four of them. Paying 12+ dollars a salad is fine but sometimes it's only about one cup of greens. When I order to go, the container it's served in is always different even though I ordered the same exact meal. Once, when I got home, there was a big mess in the bag. Pasta sauce leaked everywhere. After I ate most of it, I noticed a hole was cut out of the bottom! The quality is usually good, but several times I had to throw away half the salad due to rot and what looks like freezer burn. I've also had my delicate pastries served on its side several times. Now I sit feeling like I've eaten week old fried carnival food when I should feel great and refreshed from my Caesar salad. These problems should have been remedied by now. I have given them a dozen or so chances and it's time for me to realize the hype of a 'French' bakery with prices high enough to compete in San Francisco is not what it claims.

reviewText: I have come here tons for their desserts. They're amazing! That's the only reason I'm giving two stars. I decided to eat in for the first time today. Nope. I was expected to pour the au jus into teeny tiny containers. It would have taken quite a few to be able to take enough home for my sandwich. I was extremely disappointed. The only reason I will ever come back here is for the dessert.

reviewText: The food is great and the prices are better than other fast-casual chains. They face one major flaw...service. reviewText: I would give it no stars if I could! Terrible service! I placed a "to-go" order over the phone - had to wait at least 5 minutes on the phone for them to answer my call and take the order. When I arrived at the "to-go" counter, 3 other people were ahead of me who had not placed to go orders on the phone - I had to wait for them to place their order AND wait while the one person at the counter ((at 1pm, their prime lunch time) filled the order then waited on the next person in line. At one point, when she took the order of the person in front of me, she checked the one bag waiting on the counter (mine) but did not bother to ask my name and proceeded to fill the order she had just taken. Ten minutes later- they finally got to me and gave me my order (a now cold rotisserie chicken and wilted salad from being next to the hot chicken). The manager walked up at that point (don't know where she was before) and I asked her what was the point of bothering to call in an order if I had to wait in the phone line to give the order and wait in another order fulfillment line when I got to the store? She shrugged her shoulders and said it saved me from waiting for my own order. Too bad I had to wait for everyone else's order. When I left, there were at least 8 people waiting behind me for service. Good luck to them! Bottom line, be prepared to wait 20+ minutes to pick up an order and don't bother trying to call in an order at this store! The wilted salad was terrible and the chicken was cold. Just threw $12 out the window and wasted my time. They need to take a lesson from the much more efficient Rice Village store - they process phone orders FAST!!

reviewText: This place is so allergen UNfriendly. We specifically asked for no bread because of a gluten allergy. Food came out with bread. When we told the person, she didn't speak enough English to understand. Ok fine understandable. But then she tried to force me to take the food. Then more people came up to us with the food telling us to take it. When I pointed out that their receipt and ours both said no bread and that the order was wrong, they still insisted we take the food. I had to explain probably over 5 times that there is a food allergy before they understood and took the food back. The food came back out a minute later just rearranged without the bread. Wow. This place is the WORST at accommodating allergies. It's a lawsuit waiting to happen. Be extra careful if you have any allergies!!

reviewText: I like to go to coffee shops to write and even though this isn't really a coffee shop, I enjoy going here during the week. In the middle of the day, you'll find people working remotely on their laptops or having business meetings. There's an abundance of wall outlets, and it's well set up so that you can usually find a corner of false corner area that isn't loud. The food is good but I wouldn't come here if you're starving or a big meat eater because its mostly pasta, soup, salad, sandwiches. The coffee is good, and when the restaurant isn't busy, sometimes the bussers will come over and offer to get refills on the java or tea I'm drinking.

reviewText: We went in this place this morning at about 10 and promptly walked out. There was a woman that was running the front ordering machine and she apparently was in a hurry. reviewText: Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW) is truly one of the best airports in the world. From luxury boutiques to local Texas-themed shops, there's something for every traveler. Whether you're looking for last-minute gifts, high-end fashion, or a quick snack, the variety is impressive. The transportation options within the airport are also top-notch. The Skylink train system makes navigating between terminals effortless, with frequent and fast connections. No matter where your next gate is, getting there is seamless. If you’re renting a car or using ride-share services, the process is efficient, ensuring minimal hassle for travelers. Beyond convenience, the airport is also clean, modern, and well-maintained. There are plenty of comfortable seating areas, charging stations, and even great dining options that go beyond the typical airport food. If you're traveling through DFW, you’re in for an excellent experience. The combination of amazing stores, efficient transportation, and top-tier amenities makes it a standout airport, whether you’re here for a short layover or an extended stay. Highly recommended!

reviewText: I am beyond disappointed with our experience at La Madeleine at The Forum. What we encountered was not just poor service, it was unacceptable and embarrassing for a brand that presents itself as a French-inspired-bakery-café with an upscale, boutique image. The restaurant was clearly and dangerously understaffed. The line to order moved at a crawl because the hostess was forced to juggle multiple roles. Once we finally placed our order, the wait for food was excessive, and when it arrived, the quality was inexcusable. One member of our family, someone who never complains, immediately notified the waiter that his two scrambled eggs were cold. In a shocking and unprofessional response, the waiter put his finger into the eggs to confirm they were cold and then removed the plate. That moment alone demonstrated a complete lack of food-handling standards and training. It also left us questioning whether the food was properly remade or simply reheated and returned. My daughter’s bacon was raw and completely inedible. The French toast was burned on the side that was intentionally not visible, which felt deceptive. My own French toast was served lukewarm, not hot. When customers order freshly prepared food, they reasonably expect it to be served at the proper temperature. This is a basic standard, not a luxury. The operational failures did not stop there. The restaurant did not have spoons available, and when my daughter asked at the counter, she was told they were all in the dishwasher. The same excuse was given when we requested knives. The raw sugar container had only two packets left, and there was no staff member available to replenish it or assist us. To make matters worse, the hallway leading to the restrooms had several trash cans lined up with towels underneath, actively catching water from a roof leak. This was alarming from both a cleanliness and safety standpoint and should never be visible to customers. Overall, this experience was worse than dining at a budget breakfast chain. For La Madeleine to deliver a dining experience that falls below the standards of IHOP is frankly astonishing. Whether this location is cutting costs by refusing to staff properly, suffering from constant employee turnover, or experiencing severe management failure, the result is the same: customers are paying for a brand promise that is not being delivered. I hate that the lemon creme cake is only offered as a seasonal dessert but I will continue my search for another location in my home town of San Antonio n hope to find at least 1 location that measures up to this 1 as I wait patiently for the lemon cake to return. reviewText: I have been a loyal Visionworks customer for years. However, my experience both last year and this year at the San Tan Village location has been very disappointing. So much so, that it has prompted me to re-evaluate where I will seek future optical services. Last year, I ordered contacts as well as purchased a pair of reading glasses that were approx. $300 out of pocket. Unfortunately, I never received a call notifying me that my glasses were ready. After multiple unsuccessful attempts to reach someone by phone, I visited the store in person, where my file couldn't be located initially. It was only after some persistence that the staff was able to locate my order. Additionally, there was not a fitting provided for my glasses, which due to their strength, I’ve not been unable to use. This year, they again could not find my file and treated me as a new patient (I had to fill out all new forms) and after seeing the eye doctor, (who by the way, didn’t listen to a thing I told him) he suggested I try a couple different types of contact lenses, both of which had to be ordered. When checking out, I asked if I could pre-pay for my contacts and was told someone would call me the next day to take the payment - that never happened. Two weeks later (I was told it would be two days) I did receive a call saying that the sample contacts were in, when I again asked about pre-paying for my contacts, I was told someone would get back to me that day - again, didn’t happen. I finally called and told them I would come over to get the trial contacts. When I arrived to pick them up, I encountered an employee whose behavior was extremely rude and very unprofessional. The doctor had ordered 2-pair of contacts for me to try, and one of the employees went to hand me the order, but this woman grabbed the bag away from her and only gave me one pair. Further, she fought with me the entire time saying they had attempted to call, and I never answered. I told her there were no messages, which escalated her discourteous behavior. I let her know she was making the entire experience unpleasant and therefore, I wouldn't be purchasing my contacts or any glasses for that matter, from Visionworks. She continued yelling at me as I walking out, that I wasn't going to get my RX, for which I paid the deductible, and my insurance had covered a couple weeks prior. Given these repeated issues, I will no longer be using Visionworks. While I’ve appreciated the service at other locations in the past, I feel there are many other vision options available in the San Tan Village area, ones that will hopefully provide a better overall customer experience. Therefore, I'm sharing this feedback to let Visionworks know they’re not the only game in town, and therefore they may want to “do better” in the future.

reviewText: Oh...I don't know. Perhaps only giving it 3 stars is a bit harsh, but there are some details being missed here which I think are worth reviewing. First, the food. Fundamentally, it is good. Tasty and relatively well put together. That said, I get the sense that they use their microwave extensively for re-heating...and their quiche usually tastes like it has been sitting under heat lamps for an extensive amount of time. This isn't make or break, but it's a detail that might be something to look at if I were management. It shouldn't take that much to keep food fresh and hot without the use of microwaves or long heat lamp durations. The salads are great. Deserts are good. Overall, is eat there again for sure...but I'll lean towards items that aren't obviously pre-made. Tip: after the drink station, don't forget to pick up some bread and jam that they put out.

reviewText: The service here is deplorable! Couldn't order the Crêpes bc according to the manager, they had run out by 1 p.m. No problem. Went to grab a coffee mug, & every single one was filthy, with brown coffee rings & specs of food on the inside. Fine. Ordered oatmeal for my 6 yr old & was charged full price, bc the cashier informs me that even though the actual menu lists oatmeal on the kids menu, there's no such thing. I asked another staff mbr where I could find the plastic forks, & he tells me "by the door". I ask again bc I couldn't hear him, & he very rudely says, "I JUST TOLD YOU BY THE DOOR!" My mother was actually frightened by his tone. The same man comes to our table later & stared us down. I ask him if there's a problem, & he says he was looking to see if the honey was on our table-very disturbing. We ordered potato hash browns & when the waitress brought them to the table, one order was missing. When we asked for it, she tells us, she'll bring it later, "when the kitchen is done cooking it", slams the plate down & walks off. 20 mins later, still missing, so my mother had to go ask for it at the counter. Everyone else at our table had already finished their food. My family and I have patronized this location since it opened, but due horrible, somewhat aggressive attitudes of the staff, bad customer service & the dirty dishes & tables, we will never return. We recently visited the Memorial location & we were met with a smiling staff & a clean restaurant. It's sad to see what the Sugar land location has been reduced to. Never again! Note: Several other customers were complaining as well.

reviewText: Terrible! Terrible! I drove 20 miles very excited to visit La Madeline as it is one of my favorites in Texas. I talked my daughter into driving 20 miles as well and assured her it was worth it. How embarrassing for this company. My first contact was at the register where it says line starts here and the waitress or a bus person said this isn’t open go down to the other register with no smile no apology. I noticed there was no food along the service area in the glass window at all, which is strange because there is always delicious looking food to view.OK maybe she was having an off day. I enthusiastically approached the second register and when I explained where we came from and how excited we were to be there, she asked “why would you do that? There is one in Santan Valley”. I explained to her I was from the opposite direction that is why I chose her restaurant. She seemed baffled but now I know why. I’ll shorten the story up. They were out of half-and-half so I asked for heavy cream and the manager just looked at the waitress and asked three times why. I chimed in and said because “you’re out of half-and-half”, so he gave me heavy cream in a coffee mug and just said “here” with no smile no apology. My quiche came five minutes after my daughters plate. The crust was hard as a rock. My potato galette was definitely one to two days old and cold on the plate. I flagged down the waitress and asked for the side of béarnaise sauce that I ordered and she said what is béarnaise sauce? I advised her it’s a French restaurant and béarnaise sauce is common and she didn’t know what I was talking about. I pointed to someone else’s béarnaise sauce and she just walked away and came back with a cup of Béarnaise sauce that was cold. I ordered crisp bacon and clearly they microwaved it and burned it. I had to apologize to my daughter for making her drive 20 miles for the worse breakfast I’ve had all year. This store needs quality control from corporate in the worst way. Please get this store in shape so you can be represented correctly. The French coffee was great and the fireplace was nice and that’s the only positive thing I can say for my visit.

reviewText: I have come to this restaurant quite often and I always get the chicken friand. The puff pastry is usually nice and soft and fresh looking. Usually the inside has a good amount of chicken mushrooms. The sauce on top is very very good. I went at 3:00 with someone else. I was never so surprised when I sat down and I probably should have taken it back but the pastry was hard. Very hard to cut. Whatever was inside was brown ground up .heaven's knows what that was. I do know that this is usually made with the little pieces of chicken and mushrooms and onions. That was not the case. The man that served it was very nice but he only put a tablespoon of sauce on the top of it so I tried hard to cut it and eat it but it actually made me sick. I left a note on plate to say that I was not pleased with it at all and I will not be back. There were only two left. My friend and I got those two, but in retrospect those two should have been thrown out because they were dark looking and they were hard.

reviewText: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ La Madeleine offers a charming slice of France with its delightful ambience and tasty cuisine. The Croque Monsieur was a highlight, perfectly toasted with just the right balance of cheese and ham. The French Onion Soup had a rich, savory broth, though it could have used a bit more cheese. The patisserie section was a treat, with an array of fresh, delicious pastries. The Lemon Tart was particularly noteworthy. Service was generally good, though there were moments when it felt a bit slow. The restaurant maintained a clean and inviting atmosphere, making it a nice spot for a casual lunch or a relaxed dinner. While there's room for improvement in service speed, the overall experience was very pleasant. La Madeleine is definitely worth a visit for those looking for a taste of France.

reviewText: My experience at Dallas airport was not entirely good. In terms of immigration, it was a good experience because the employee who helped me was objective and efficient. However, in the sector where your luggage is scanned, I felt a lack of efficiency. The girl who was supposed to tell us what to take out of the backpack spoke very quickly and left because she was alone serving a lot of people. I didn't know I should take the tablet out of my backpack because I never needed to do that. The problem was that the other employee decided to punish me for this and passed my luggage through twice more. The first time she took out my tablet and the second time she looked at the details of what was in my backpack. I spent 40 minutes barefoot and without a coat, freezing to death and super anxious because I couldn't check the time and know if I was missing my flight or not. The girl who was supposed to tell us what to take out of the backpack spoke very quickly and left because she was alone serving a lot of people. I didn't know I should take the tablet out of my backpack because I never needed to do that. The problem was that the other employee decided to punish me for this and passed my luggage through twice more. The first time she took out my tablet and the second time she looked at the details of what was in my backpack. I spent 40 minutes barefoot and without a coat, freezing to death and super anxious because I couldn't check the time and know if I was missing my flight or not. Meanwhile, people who had to have their luggage searched were piling up there. But other people at the airport improved my first impression, like a pilot who helped me with information and a girl who cleaned the bathrooms while singing a very beautiful song!

reviewText: This location is gross. I’ve eaten at other locations before and they were great. Everything from the food covered front patio furniture, giant chunk of crispy oven gunk that was left in the wife’s pizza. One of the guys behind the counter had a disgusting tattered shirt that fit in with the cleanliness level I only noticed while waiting for my pizza. It’s a level of dirty that can only happen with neglect over time. The kitchen looked very messy and unorganized compared to other locations, but the pizza still tasted good. The wife’s salad was completely overlooked by the staff and came out when we were ready to leave, but only after we asked. To their credit, Jacob refunded us the whole meal without us asking. So, I don’t know what to say. They are going through a rough patch but there are still enough good folks working there that I’ll come back and give it another try in a few months. A year later update: when we walked in there was a very loud noise coming from the soda machine/icemaker. Loud enough I didn’t realize there was music on until it finally turned off. They clearly hire some staff with disabilities, which is awesome. Everyone seemed super nice. However, there is still an issue with cleanliness. They just opened on a Monday morning and there was old food on the ground and pizza sauce on the walls of our booth. Not super inspiring for a restaurant. I’ll try an again in a few months, but it’s kinda a last chance try. It’s a bummer because I like the chain in other locations.

reviewText: I went to this location on the request of my wife. There is a saying about pizza, “even when pizza is kind of bad, it’s pretty good”. The pizza was average at best and that is being generous. Mod Pizza has lost our business because of this visit. MOD Pizza: your staff sets the tone and impressions for your customers, perhaps ensure that your staff is capable of basic customer service or teach them to fake it until they make it. Being polite costs nothing but being impolite costs you customers as it has in this instance.

reviewText: This ramen place was over-hyped for us. Everyone had really positive things to say about it. We liked the ramen, but still preferred the ramen at Misaki ramen in Round Rock. On the bright side, this was was a little cheaper. Misaki ramen has bulgogi ramen and veggie ramen we like a lot. Ramen tatsuya was a little loud and we had to sit a little crowded in the central table. We could hear the date going on next to us, which was entertaining but I don't want to hear that so well! We both got OG ramen and he gave me his egg cause I like them and he doesn't. I gave him half my pork piece because it was on the fatty side. He said his was not as fatty. It was tender and tasty, though! I had the corn bomb for some fiber and it was delicious.

name: Ramen Tatsu-Ya
fullAddress: 14028 US-183 Bldg G, Suite 310, Austin, TX 78717
reviewText: The staff were really nice and respectful. The place got really busy as it got darker out and there was a giant line of people, buuuut I totally understood why when I had my food. I'm not a huge fan of ramen anymore, but it was quite tasty! They also have outdoor seating, which is what I wanted, but my girlfriend wanted to sit inside because it was cold. We found out leaving the restaurant that the outdoor seating has heaters above! It's super pretty and will definitely come back!

reviewText: Atmosphere is overall great and it is constantly busy. I am well ventured and traveled, I would say, and this location fell short for me in authentic Japanese ramen cuisine. I did interfere with some rude male staff, but was treated my a nice hostess that pointed me with the menu as it was my first time at the location. I wouldn’t say I’d return due to the fact that I found it a tad overpriced for lack of authenticity, friendliness of overall staff and long wait time until I was attended given I was a party of one. The only thing that made up was that they had proper authentic Japanese sake. My visit was 3/21/2023 as a local restauranteur in Houston, San Antonio, Austin, & Boulder.

reviewText: La Madeleine has been an established cafe for over a decade within Austin. launching with high appraisal it seemed clear this cafe had a lot of potential for a prosperous and delicious legacy. sadly, I am not here to give praise to this establishment today; walking in on this Monday afternoon I was excited to have a wonderful French inspired brunch experience. it came to a shock to me that a place with 4 stars overall would be so empty. Stained floors, clear signs of water damage, and an empty restaurant set the tone for what I was getting into quickly. I ordered the French breakfast, a $12 meal with eggs, sausage, croissant, and a potato galette. Looking at my late it was clear not a single one of these items listed were made from scratch. the flavorless eggs were clearly powdered eggs, the bland paper-thin sausage patty reheated from a frozen bag, and the croissant was the equivalent of one you would have at Sams club. I was given complementary "bread" that had the distinct taste of plastic. So far this has been one of the worst meals I have had, you are truly better off eating dinning somewhere else. overall, it was clear La Madeleine is well past its golden years and is yet another failing cafe to be closed in a few years if no changes are made.

reviewText: My husband and I went today in the lunch hour, we saw there was only 1 cashier (at the take out line) and everyone had lined up there. So we waited about 20 minutes, when our turn came, the young cashier asked “is this dine in, or take out?” We answered “ dine in” she said “dine in is over there” and promptly walked away and served another customer even though we were next in line. There was no dine in cashier, but she walked to the dine in register and served another customer!!! Leaving us standing there with no explanation. We have enjoyed our previous visits to La Madeleine, however, to be treated so rudely on this visit, we will never go back. We are happy to give other establishments our money, yes we understand staff shortages, COVID etc…but please train the staff you do hire to be polite and efficient. Update on this experience: I decided to give La Madeleine another chance, and it was good! Good service, delicious food, the cashier was helpful and attentive and polite. You have won me back! Before COVID it was one of our favorite restaurants in this area. Today was our first visit after Covid, we ordered chicken Parisian with tomato basil soup, and Basalmic salmon with steam/boiled broccoli on the side. The food came over, it was different to my expectation. The salmon cooked well, but the broccoli was giant like trees 😅and there was standing water on the plate…. the salmon and broccoli staying in the standing water on the plate…. The basil soup was used very good, but until toward the end of the meal and reminding them the soup, the waitress brought the soup, but she held the plate close to her face and also talking to us ,actually she spoke to the soup—- her saliva probably on the surface of the soup….We didn’t have the soup…She brought coffee, and she held coffee close to her face as well… and she was talking, mouth to the coffee… During the time when we were eating, several fruit flies was flying around in the restaurant, one of those on my plate… Also this place asked us to pay tips before we got any service! Hopefully this place returns to how good they were.

reviewText: I’m updating and changing my review for this location. The eggs in the quiches are still raw, the dough in some of pastries aren’t cooked through. I came to eat with my family and the food we got wasn’t cooked. We returned it to have the person helping us roll her eyes then sigh and ask what we wanted to do. We asked for cooked pastries and when we received the freshly “cooked” pastries, they were still raw in the middle and the person responded “well that’s how we cook them so if they’re not to your satisfaction then I can’t help you”. I’m sorry, that’s not an acceptable response. Am I supposed to be ok eating raw dough? (The picture is of the raw pastry dough, that’s not melted cheese). La Madeleine, I am very disappointed and I will not be coming back to any location again.

The staff will bring your food to your table. The drink selection did include fresh unsweetened tea and mango tea (unsweetened), select coffee choices, and a soda fountain. The mango tea was quite good! I normally prefer sugar but I love a strong fruit tea so it worked for me. After eating my chicken salad croissant I ended my dinner with a fruit cheesecake, so good! The berries on top were fresh and the the actual cheesecake was the perfect size to savor and not be stuffed. The staff were all pleasant and even turned down the ac for us when we requested it, the party room got pretty stuffy! The tables were clean and drink station sanitary. Good experience!

Last but not least the Dessert like I said at the beginning the cost to portion ratio was not even close to being worth buying. I’ve never seen dessert if you call it that in a small (dixie cup) size. I will NOT buy from La Madeline ever again in the future. I will not be disappointed if they close the store. reviewText: Made an order for pick up online a couple of weeks ago. I followed the steps online to order and after paying I got a confirmation email and pick up time. Showed up to pick up and they had nothing and they claimed I had order somewhere else even though we showed them the email with their address and time for pick up. By the way, the place had no customers. My husband then heard one of the girls tell another one that of course she did not have any online orders, the machine was turned off. As I walked to the restroom I could hear them laughing, maybe it was at something else but made me feel that they were laughing at the situation. Still, the manager insisted that I must have placed the order for another day or a different location instead of apologizing. Of course I argued that that was incorrect but she kept making excuses. Ended up waiting an additional 25 minutes for my food, it was somehow still my fault even though she would said sorry but there was a "you must have" followed by it. It was my first time eating La Madeline. Food was delicious and exactly what I was looking for since I was in recovery from surgery. But the situation made it a very bad experience. Damn, she could had at least thrown in a crossiant or cookie for my troubles. I was not looking for free stuff or a free meal. We all make mistakes , but a simple sincere apology after learning of their mistake and we'll get cooking would had made a big difference instead of blaming me for their problem. Also, you have to order through grub hub in order to make an online order, this made it hard to get a refund. We were at a loss since we couldn't just get our money back and cancel the order.

The food was good and they offer gluten free alternatives which was appreciated. The pizza was pretty good, but I’m sure the dough on the gluten free pizzas isn’t made on-site which is understandable. The waitress offered us sparkling water but was going to serve the room temp bottle that was on the table over ice cubes. That was strange to me, mineral water over tap water ice cubes?? I’m not sure that I would return purposely, the menu could be fantastic with just a little push, I feel. Something has to bring people back, like a little spark of something that I felt was missing.

reviewText: Cedro is one of the best spots in Greater Austin. They have great wine list with phenomenal wine specials on the regular. Their food, from appetizers to salads to entrees are all delicious. The pasta made in house is top notch and I can’t use enough positive adjectives to explain the Seafood Risotto. We also really enjoy the dining room and patio vibe as well. Coupled with great service, my wife and I frequently have business meals, special celebration meals, and of course (more than) occasional “it’s Thursday night we should probably go unofficially start the weekend” meals here. If you are looking for a really nice dining experience. Do yourself a favor and check out Cedro.

reviewText: Took a group of 10 people to Cedro’s last week and we had a wonderful time. It’s one of my favorite restaurants that never disappoints. Cedro’s is tucked away in the HEB shopping center off of Lakeline so I don’t have to fight central Austin traffic and there is always plenty of parking. It’s not loud and it has a calm ambiance. Add to that the food is always fresh and tastes wonderful and there is lots of variety on the menu and Cedro’s is top on my list for Cedar Park. The only negative was that Cedro’s, like most of the restaurants in Austin right now, could use more waitstaff. The waiters that were there did their very best to juggle the tables. And for a group of 10, they did a very good job. Other than that they would deserve 5 stars.

reviewText: I rarely post negative reviews and I’m not “one of those negative people” but today I went in to relax, work, and enjoy a pastry. I’ve never had a major issue with La Madeleine’s but this particular location has lost my business until they get new employees and possibly new management. That was just odd, off, and wrong.

reviewText: I mostly travel internationally through DFW's Gate D, and it has consistently been a smooth and pleasant experience. The terminal is large, clean, and well-organized, with plenty of stores, restaurants, and restrooms. Basically, everything you need while waiting for a long-haul flight. What really stands out to me is how courteous and respectful the TSA staff have been, especially when assisting with me with my wheelchair and in recognizing and respecting my religious attire (niqab). That level of professionalism and sensitivity makes a big difference in the travel experience. Arrival and baggage claim are also very efficient. I’ve never had an issue finding my luggage or navigating the terminal. Overall, Gate D is a great hub for international travel, and I’m always happy to fly through it!

reviewText: Dr. Catalasan is absolutely amazing! I came into the office after seeing twelve other doctors about a sudden onset of vertigo and sever migraines. I had been to several different specialties including my regular doctor, 3 different neurologist and ENT. Not to mention the countless eastern methods I tried, acupuncture and message. Finally, my neurologist mentioned getting a check up from an eye doctor. I researched headache eye doctor on google and out popped Dr. Catalasan. My first appointment was all the normal stuff leading to Dr. Catalasan saying, “Well, you have perfect 20/20 vision, what brings you in?” I explained everything I had been through over the last 3-4 months and was just searching for help and a answer. She said, “Hmm- I have one more test to do.” Sure enough- My eyes see perfectly by themselves, but together not so much. “Binocular Vision Disfunction” Dr. Catalasan read off a list of symptoms of this issue and I was just shocked! They were all me- (cannot read in the car, car sickness, sleeping problems, needing complete darkness, just to name a few. I came back in for a complete neuro exam and ended up with prism glasses. I’ll be honest, I was not hopeful this would even help me. I had gone through so much at this point. Day 1 with the glasses- my migraine went away and I was not dizzy. I couldn’t even take them off to shower! I had to wear the glasses sun-up to sun-down. When my children would wake in the middle of the night- I would be falling over down the halls without my glasses. I was just in shock and so greatful. I share my story to help others out there like myself who are also suffering from these symptoms. Dr. Catalasan listened me and my concerns. She helped me through the process and then again in a few months when I was ready for an adjustment. Thank you for giving me my life back.

reviewText: I used to work at la Madeline's (Sundance Square) many years ago. I had nothing but the fondest memories of those times. Saute and Prep, I learned a lot about cooking and restaurants. The pastries and bread items were incredible and nicely portioned. I still love the place, but I think the portions on the pastries have gotten significantly smaller. Food is a bit more expensive (sign of the times) The new fruit tart seems smaller for the same price. The French coffee is amazing still, almond croissants are fire! Croissants are still soft and buttery. The parking situation at this store is fugly, tiny lot (shared with Starbucks and it's drive through) in a VERY busy shopping center near Costco. I still love coming here, just not as often as I used to. I hit that Camp Bowie location all the time when I lived over there. I think you would enjoy: Breakfast - French Country Breakfast, strawberries Romanoff, Quiche Lorraine, or potato galette. Lunch - Chicken Friand w/mushroom sauce, tomato basil soup, potato soup, French onion soup, croque monsior, chicken Parisian sandwich, or French dip. Dinner - chicken la Madeline or Pesto Pasta.

reviewText: From the time I arrived I felt like I was about to be ripped off. I wanted a general eye exam for glasses, they tried to prompt me into a more expensive exam instead. They have that eye scan they charge for and they tell you in advance, fine. But how does insurance not cover that? Then the optometrist did the exam for glasses. That went ok. Then she goes on to tell me that even though my glasses prescription has changed my contacts has remained the same. How would you know that without doing a separate exam for contact lenses? Finally when I selected my glasses frame the optician immediately tacked on the most expensive option of the lenses. I had to keep at her to bring down the price. And my insurance apparently didn't cover the entire cost of the glasses, which normally anywhere else it will. How is it that it doesn't happen here? These guys will do anything for a buck, but hey that's America right? Don't get ripped off. You may be better off buying glasses frame elsewhere , and if you do come here tread carefully as they will try to steer you in the most expensive direction. Look out for your interests over their's because they're definitely looking out for their interests over yours.

reviewText: Firstly, I was having a difficult time finding Maui Jim glasses at a location that had samples to try on. You were the 14th place I called. reviewText: Nice location and I love being able to schedule my own eye appointment online. I was able to get a last minute appointment on a Saturday. Check in was easy, medical staff was friendly. My only negative is the cost of ordering glasses in store is a total racket. Ultimately you're paying double what you would to order glasses yourself online, so think of it as a convenience fee really of having someone plug all the numbers in for you. I'm not going to blame Visionworks, because they're a business and I get it. But - if you're at all willing and able then your best bet is to try on all the frames in store to get an idea of what you're looking for as far as style and fit and then just use that information once you get home. In store - during a "buy one get one free" deal for glasses they quoted me $500 for 2 compelte pairs with progressive lenses. I came home and ordered two pairs from an online competitor for under $250. Again, I totally understand WHY it costs more in store, but there are more affordable options out there if you need it.

reviewText: They took my number for an account, but I never received any calls or texts with updates about my contact lens trial.
