They communicated poorly about when my glasses’ lenses would come in: it takes two weeks, but I don’t have to choose the frame somehow. It didn’t make sense exactly but I thought it was a “trust the process” thing. They actually did need a frame chosen first, which makes more sense, but the associate didn’t try to explain much when I asked questions. They may have been having a bad day, but they seemed pretty depressed. (I’ve worked in a similar position for a major corporation before myself so it would be sadly unsurprising tbh.) When choosing a frame, I felt pressured and almost shamed to spend more for thinner lenses. I know my nearsightedness is horrible and my glasses are gonna be thick, it’s not my first time getting glasses. The associate was pretty rude and said, “okay, we just won’t wear the glasses out of the house!” At least they worked with my insurance and the glasses are cute. I won’t come back unless it’s my only choice.

reviewText: WHAT HAPPENED?? I have eaten at this location many times and entertained family and friends here. My experience tonight was off putting to say the least. Initially I ordered a Chicken Friand, I was told they didn't have any made and it would take about 15 minutes. Then I was asked if I wanted something else. I almost understand that, almost. Prior to paying I was asked for a tip... just seems a little gauche. The ice machine was out of Ice. Which was refilled. Then the water dispenser quit working so I was charged for a soda. When I asked for bread I was told that the store didn't have any...the French roast coffee was empty as well. The 15 minute wait for my Friand turned into 40... However, when our food arrived it was piping hot and delicious! If the reviews improve, and I hope they do, We will be back.

The tomato and basil soup contained and ambundance of flavors without a salty base. I hope to go back and try again for a better experience and most of it was delicious.

reviewText: I’ve been here many times and never leave dissatisfied. This location has been here for at least 15+ years and is still popular in NW Austin. I love tomato soup and their tomato basil soup is one of the best I have ever tried. So much better than many famous chain cafe restaurants. It is so creamy and the basil and tomato are perfectly balanced. We ordered a lemon tart, French Dip and Chicken Parisien. We had both sandwiches with caesar salad, and a bowl of tomato basil soup. Their sandwiches and salad are freshly made with a big portion. The bread is amazing. Pastries and coffees from previous experiences were always great. The Interior is cozy, clean and the staff is very friendly. Locals will come here to work or study and not be bothered. A perfect place for brunch and lunch, or even just an easy and quick dinner! Highly recommend this place if you love a cafe-type restaurant.

The food is good, their chicken parisien hot sandwich is to die for. Unfortunately the service has its ups and downs, it seems the staff rotates a lot so it is not consistent. It also would be nice if they had more options for beverages, their fountain drink is quite limited. Last night they were out of ice, dark cherry yougurt danish and the cashier forgot to serve us a cup of soup and did not catch the chips as side for the sandwich. But we love this place so much that we will insist coming back, we know already what to expect.

My partner thought that his Croque Monsieur (Forgive me if I misspelled that) was just ok, and expected it to be creamier. I did love the coffee, and my hard boiled eggs were done very well. The plating and presentation was nice as well. Other than that we really weren't too impressed by the food and aren't too inclined to go back soon. We also did not know that we had to go right up to order, rather than wait to be seated, which confused us initially as there was no indication of what to do. Overall, my first impression is that it's a restaurant with lovely atmosphere and average food. It's not a bad place to go at all, but probably could make more improvements and little changes to be even better than it is currently.

reviewText: When it comes to French cafes in Houston, you can't go wrong with Le Madeleine. Been coming to this location for over five years now. Breakfast croissant is killer and the quiche is on point. Eggs Benedict is perfect if you really want to indulge. Plus don't forget to try the madeleines from the bakery! Plenty of seating indoors and out, plus plenty of cute treats if you need a present in a pinch. Although it's pretty much self service ordering at the buffet line, the waitstaff is always happy to help out, clearing plates and getting condiments. Highly recommend for singles, couples, families, and groups.

reviewText: Absolute worst airport experience ever. Went to terminal D to pick up a friend arriving there. Only found the right baggage carousel by accident due to poor signage inside the terminal. Then when exiting the parking area, again due to a lack of signs directing you where to go to exit the massive parking garage, it wasn't clear where to go to exit the garage. We finally found our way out only to come to a Y in the road where yet again, there was no sign telling which way to go for the north or the south exit, so we took the lane going right. All of a sudden, a big arm comes down and hits the top of our car! The arm wasn't visible when we started down the lane so it came as a complete shock. Fortunately, our car wasn't damaged but what the hell? Why in hell did it come down in the first place? On top of all we'd gone through at this point, the right lane we'd chosen was the wrong one to take, sending us south instead of north where we wanted to go. We finally found a crossover intersection to turn around and go north but then there was no on-ramp to get on the main road going out of the airport. We ended up staying on the access road all the way to the airport exit which then made it difficult to get out of the airport due to vehicles coming at high speed exiting on the main road. On top of all of this, the toll tag on our car didn't register with the toll tag system so we'll probably get a bill for the time we were in this horrible, awful, confusing airport. I'd visited this airport several times in past years and it wasn't like this back then. It is now a nightmare to try find your way in and out of! Hope I never have to go back again!!!

name: Dallas Fort Worth International Airport
fullAddress: 2400 Aviation Dr, DFW Airport, TX 75261, United States
reviewText: I’d imagine many years ago the design of this airport was revolutionary. Those years have gone by and time has not been kind to this poorly crafted structure. The bubble concourse system all herded together via a looping train makes for long concourses that the train system does honestly make any smaller. Tools such as moving sidewalk would help passengers maneuvers through this extremely large airport (not as bad as Dulles). With constant gate changes prior departure it becomes a marathon to keep pace in this airport. Other issues are the following: the rental car center is too far removed from the airport (slightly better than BWI). With such a crafty concourse design it is obvious the rental car building was a thought long down the road from useful. When riding from the rental car center make certain to pay attention to the concourse the bus is traveling to, as there’s a bus for each of them. Restrooms are next on the list. There aren’t enough restrooms on any concourse. A restroom line is pretty common. Someone dropped the ball on that one. One plus. The food choices here are better than most airport. All and all for Texas sized city this Texas sized airport under performs in more way than I have listed here. I try to avoid this place.

reviewText: My husband went to the Chandler La Madeleine for breakfast this morning. The young man who took our order was surly. He never smiled. He seemed as if he really did not want to be there. I asked for "crisp bacon" with my order. I asked him, "can your cook do crisp bacon?". He answered "Yes." When I got my order, the bacon was limp and fatty. The woman who brought us our food was nice and helpful. I asked her to cook my bacon some more, to make it crisp, and she said she would get me a new order of bacon. When I got the new bacon, it was crisp because it was black (burned). Apparently no one in the kitchen this morning knew how to cook bacon. While our meal in general tasted good, my husband's plate gave the impression of being slapped together with no care taken about how it looked. I had a latte with my meal and my husband had an espresso. Both coffees were great. To sum up, the food tasted good, but the surly youth's attitude, the bacon issue and the lack of attention given to presentation caused us to conclude that eating breakfast there just wasn't worth what it cost. I should add that I have eaten lunch multiple times at the La Madeleine in downtown Phoenix, and it was great every time, in every respect. Perhaps the problem is just with the Chandler branch, and some (but not all) members of the breakfast-shift crew.

reviewText: I was really looking forward to going to Cedro. This restaurant is not cheap and they claim that they do everything from scratch so I was expecting the food to be delicious. The pizza I ordered tasted like the lean cuisine frozen pizza. I told one of the employees to please take the pizza because I didn’t like it and the table we were sitting at was small. He asked me if I wanted to speak to the manager and I said no. However the manager came out and I explained to him the pizza tasted bad. He apologized and said he would make this right for me and for me to pick another item from the menu. I told him that was not necessary but he was insisting and insisting. So I ordered the seafood risotto and it was alright. I was disappointed when they charged me the full price of the seafood risotto which was $28 when the pizza, I originally ordered was $17. Keep in mind, the least expensive thing on the menu was the pizza.I don’t understand how that is making it right for the customer!? I didn’t want to order another dish in the first place. I was just giving them honest feedback. I am not saying I wanted a free meal but they should have just charged me the price of the pizza since that’s the dish I wanted and it tasted bad and the manager insisted on me ordering another dish, even though I didn’t want too! I would not recommend this place because the food does not taste good and it’s pricey. However, my waiters were great, so no complaints there!! Reply to management: It’s ok, that’s your view of “making it right for the customer” and that’s fine, it’s your business. Just please next time don’t insist for someone to order something else if they tell you No. Just be respectful and take the No. Also I didn’t enjoy the risotto as you mentioned. I had a few bites and took most of it in a to go box because I wanted to be polite. When I like food, I finish it, so please don’t write as if I ate the whole dish because that’s not true.

reviewText: I was really looking forward to going to Cedro. This restaurant is not cheap and they claim that they do everything from scratch so I was expecting the food to be delicious. The pizza I ordered tasted like the lean cuisine frozen pizza. I told one of the employees to please take the pizza because I didn’t like it and the table we were sitting at was small. He asked me if I wanted to speak to the manager and I said no. However the manager came out and I explained to him the pizza tasted bad. He apologized and said he would make this right for me and for me to pick another item from the menu. I told him that was not necessary but he was insisting and insisting. So I ordered the seafood risotto and it was alright. I was disappointed when they charged me the full price of the seafood risotto which was $28 when the pizza, I originally ordered was $17. Keep in mind, the least expensive thing on the menu was the pizza.I don’t understand how that is making it right for the customer!? I didn’t want to order another dish in the first place. I was just giving them honest feedback. I am not saying I wanted a free meal but they should have just charged me the price of the pizza since that’s the dish I wanted and it tasted bad and the manager insisted on me ordering another dish, even though I didn’t want too! I would not recommend this place because the food does not taste good and it’s pricey. However, my waiters were great, so no complaints there!! Reply to management: It’s ok, that’s your view of “making it right for the customer” and that’s fine, it’s your business. Just please next time don’t insist for someone to order something else if they tell you No. Just be respectful and take the No. Also I didn’t enjoy the risotto as you mentioned. I had a few bites and took most of it in a to go box because I wanted to be polite. When I like food, I finish it, so please don’t write as if I ate the whole dish because that’s not true.

reviewText: I love La Madeleine togo and eat there so much I have a rewards account. Today the Northwood's location changed that. It was horrendous and dissapointing. I ordered the cafe sampler; the lorraine quiche was cold and weirdly textured, the spinach salad special this month is strawberry, bacon and spinach salad which was actually delicious the last time i had it. If you look at the attached photo this time it was terrible. The bacon was a grease ball with some bacon bits. Like so much bacon grease I couldn't separate it from the bacon bits and it stunk. I'm not sure how hard draining the bacon after its cooked is for the workers but if you can't do it right just leave it out. After industrially taking out the grease ball and bits, I had a strawberry and spinach salad. My daughter ordered the salad sampler. Her salmon ceasar was also terrible. The salmon was barely heated with so much water in the container it looked like they boiled the salmon then threw it into a container without draining it first. The taste was bland and the texture terrible. The workers need retraining on what's an acceptable product to give a customer and maybe some time off. It was a huge waste of money. The only decent item from my $25 order was a cup of potatoe soup that was watered down and really thin but the taste was fine. We couldn't add the cheese or the bacon because the bacon for the soup was also cocooned in grease and was in the same baggy as the cheese so the cheese was buried in bacon grease, too. La Madeliene Northwoods, your togo food sucks.

reviewText: A huge airport, mostly beautiful. The terminals are connected by a ground-level metro. However, my experience using this airport included many negative moments. I flew through this airport twice, both times with American Airlines. On my first trip, the flight was canceled due to weather conditions, even though we spent 3 hours sitting on the plane on the runway before being returned to the terminal. None of the other flights took off either. Airport staff advised everyone to stand in line for refunds or rebooking. I stood in line for 3 hours, but eventually gave up because the line seemed endless. I had to spend the night at the airport. In the entire huge airport, there were only two small areas with rooms where people could stay overnight—both were fully booked, and the cost for one night was $200! I had to sleep on hard chairs. Some passengers slept on the cold floor. In the morning, I stood in line for another 3 hours at customer service, where I was told that I would not receive a refund or a rebooked ticket, as the airline is not responsible for weather conditions. I had to buy a new ticket myself. The new flight was delayed by half an hour. And when I arrived at the gate, I found out that the boarding had suddenly been moved to a different terminal, so I had to run to make it.

reviewText: This is a very well organized airport! Kudos to all the staff operating this place - airline checkin staff, maintenance folks, CBP, TSA, and so many others - all working in harmony. The place is neat and clean, passenger friendly with well placed signs and directions. Parking is easy and accessible. Good connectivity to most places, domestic and international. Since quirks though: 1. For some reason this is the first time in a row we have had to wait on tarmac after landing because the gate wasn't available! This time it was for an international flight that flew for 15 hrs. It's interesting why the gate unavailability situation is discovered only after landing. The flight just doesn't appear at DFW - as a layman I feel there is ample opportunity to either prepare an alternate gate or announce to the passengers about the impending delay. Must be some valid reason behind this. 2. No cops or traffic directors on terminal d ride share pickup. That could help prevent ghost jams 3. TSA pre is often slower than regular lines!

Clear and well-placed signage throughout the terminals significantly enhances the ease of navigation, ensuring that passengers can reach their destinations without confusion. The electric train system is an outstanding addition, providing quick and smooth transportation between terminals. Overall, I consider this airport to be C among the finest I have visited globally. It truly sets a benchmark for what a modern international airport should offer in terms of efficiency, comfort, and service excellence.

reviewText: La mad has a special place in my heart. You can never miss with the creamy pesto pasta. I don’t get chicken with my pasta but when I do it’s always juicy and full of flavor. My other go to is, of course, the chicken friand. You must get extra mushroom sauce, that’s what makes the dish. I could literally just eat a cup of that. reviewText: Rather than making sure the order was correct, the person taking orders seemed more worried about making sure everyone in our party of 6 understood that she would let us know if we needed a tray after 3 of us already had trays with glasses on them. There didn't appear to be a shortage of trays! The soup server started with the last person in our group, so the ones who ordered first had to wait for their soups, causing the line to back up. She also mentioned that we could combine our glasses and soups so we didn't all need a tray! We were down to 3 trays already! More time spent trying to reduce tray usage! Still plenty of trays available. All soups were barely warm enough to melt the cheese. My Croque Monsieur was soggy from too much uncooked cheese on the outside rather than the toasted cheese it should have had. Same thing on my daughter-in-law's Croque Madame. All and all a very sad experience for our granddaughters 16th birthday lunch...it used to be her favorite place for our special outings. There is too much commercialization of this small chain restaurant... I'll be going back to our locally owned bakery cafés and scratch la Madeleine off my go-to list.

reviewText: I've been a fan of la Madeleine for a while, and most of the time I enjoy the food, atmosphere, and service. This past time however, I was completely disappointed. My husband and I placed our order, paid, and waited for our meal. 15 minutes in, we still hadn't seen our food. Just before we were going to ask, the server brings one sandwich to us. Takes our number and says nothing. We are missing my meal, and my husband's salad. We ask the server where the rest of our food is and she has no idea what we are talking about. I explained half our order is missing. She goes back and they said they hadnt made my food. At this point I'm irriated as I already been 20 minutes since we ordered and now we will have to wait even longer for my meal. I'm usually an understanding person, but the fact that we didn't even get an apology is absurd to me. Like I'm not asking for a comped meal, but to not even apologize or offer anything at all is just ridiculous to me. I paid $42.00 and had to wait 38 minutes for a sandwich. And the sandwich wasn't even good. It was dry, flavorless, which isn't not how it usually is. I will never return to a la Madeleine's again after that. Like seriously, where is the customer service? Zero stars. Awful. Just plain awful.

reviewText: I hope this complaint gets to the right staff who will take these issues seriously. 1/8/25 I was attempting to check in for my flight with Frontier on the app. Running into issues, I contacted their customer service number. I called several times unable to speak with anyone. For spending hundreds of dollars this is unacceptable. My flight for 1/9 was cancelled due to the weather. Since I was unable to contact support, I had to drive to the airport with my newborn son, 10 month old niece, and six year old niece to get customer service to assist. I arrived at DFW airport around 6:30pm today (1/8/25) and was assisted by two Latina women. The first was younger and had an attitude the entire time. I explained to her that I needed a new flight because mine was cancelled. She was not trying to assist me she was telling me to “just get my refund”. She informed me that she was not able to book a new flight with no charges. She said “that’s not a thing”. I told her that my husband is a member and that he has done this before. She was going back and forth with me. I asked for a supervisor or someone else to help her. An older Latina lady with glasses came to help and told her that they do book flights no charge due to the inconvenience. Feeling embarrassed she was wrong, the girl began to ignore me when I asked to be booked for Sunday. Since I was being ignored, I asked the older lady to just help me instead. They then turned to each other and began speaking Spanish and scoffing. It was obvious they were talking about me in front of me. I waited. The older lady said that she could get me another flight but it wouldn’t be for the same date. I understood that and wanted the Sunday flight since there was no layover. I’d be traveling with my newborn and I wouldn’t be able to make layovers work. She acted as if the only flights were connecting flights with 12 hour times etc. I had to tell her I already looked online and found the Sunday flight with no layovers to please book that one. She continued to give me attitude and asked me to check my email. I didn’t get any confirmation at that time and she didn’t care. I asked for their names before I left and they laughed and said “Mary” which were fake names they gave. They both said their names are Mary. I hope the time and date can have you identify who it was who helped me and get rid of those employees. They are foul. You have miserable disrespectful staff working for Frontier. I flew Delta and recovered the complete opposite treatment at the other airport in Dallas.

reviewText: This was the airport I stopped at as a layover to Ohio. International arrivals needed to head through customs, grab your luggage and come back into the airport through security. Following the signs for re-check in just to drop your bags off after customs before going back through security. When transiting from America, the luggage went straight to the final destination and you don't need to exit the airport area, just head to the next gate. The airport has free Wifi which was convenient, parituclarly when waiting in line for customs. I took me about an hour to get through. Once through the gate, look out for the information kiosks as scanning your ticket into it will give the information about your flight. the airport itself is quite large, almost like a circle. There are four terminal areas, A, B, C and D, which is walkable by following the signs. There is also a train available for faster movement between the terminals. Each terminal has food, drink and shopping options and they were quite different. I quite liked the walk but did take two four-hour layovers to walk through the entire airport.

reviewText: They have several locations around town. It is an up-and-down sometimes in terms of service but the food is always good. As you go through the line, you can pick from their wide selections of soup, pastries, and other goodies. We chose a creme brulee cheesecake and a quiche. We also went with their shrimp pesto pasta with a side of bread. You are given a number card and they will bring the food over to you. This place is more self-served. Silverware are off to the side and you can help yourself to their complimentary bread. I remember coming here a while ago with a party in one of their private room. It wasn't the best service but the place has since improved. Not bad for some quick pasta fix.

reviewText: I LOVE Mod pizza and would usually give it 5 stars ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐. Service has always been great, this time, not so much ⭐. My husband and I went there last night (Oct 20th about 730ish pm. She gave me the other pizza in the box, just took off the lid. I asked her if it was cut (which I knew it wasn't) and she said yes. So I took my pizza un-cut and still in the box. When I got to my table and confirmed that my pizza was NOT cut, I went back up to the counter. Had to wait till someone would help me. Finally got it cut and abruptly pulled out of the box onto a plate. All pizzas were cut was wonky but that's the least of my problems. The staff was awful. I hope my next visit to Mod pizza is much better than this.

reviewText: I travel a lot these days through DFW Airport and I hope someone pays attention about the condition of Terminal E. You have to go spinning in circles to find a parking unlike some of the other Terminals that display a Number/Green light serving as a visual indicator of an open parking spot. God forbidden you didn’t know about this and if you’re in a rush to park at Terminal E then you are totally screwed up. The other thing is the lack of elevators. I always have a checked-in bag and a roll on and I have to climb down or climb up the stairs to get to the Terminal entrance or the parking lot. It looks like nobody really cares in doing any upgrades to Terminal E. It’s like one of those dark/Stone age buildings. If you are a heart patient and if you are flying international with your family with four 50 Lb suitcases, four roll on’s, and with all your backpacks and your strollers, climbing all these stairs with all these bags doesn’t absolutely seem to be a good idea. On one side everyone is talking about all the AI, Aerospace & Tech Companies coming into the State of Texas, and on the other side we’re painfully living in the dark ages sort of with Terminals like these. I am sure that with all the daily passenger traffic, and with all the major Airlines operating every single day and flying in almost every minute, and with all the per passenger PFC’s, and with all the per passenger Federal Flight Segment Taxes and with all the per passenger September 11th Security Fees being collected through Passenger Airline Ticket purchases, this isn’t about DFW Airport NOT making profits and I believe this is just about being conveniently ignorant and negligent. Statistics show that an average of 150, 000 Passengers travel from/to DFW Airport so it’s NOT about lack of passenger traffic either. If passengers were late to book a long term parking, you might get stuck with parking at Terminal E because the other Terminals get filled up fast, and if you have a family and small kids, Remote Parking isn’t a viable option after 12 AM. I hope someone who is responsible will pay attention to this cause and I hope a change will happen soon.

Today I ordered lunch online and arrived 10 minutes after the scheduled pickup time. I followed the instructions for curb pickup, by dialing the provided number when I arrived and the designated location and keyed in the number to be asked for my identifying vehicle, etc. The phone rang without being picked up for 30 minutes. Irritated that I had to then find a non curbside pickup location, I re-parked my car and went inside to find my order. At the indoor register where two employees and maybe a half-dozen seated customers, spread the safety distance within the restaurant area. I eyed my order on the counter and waited for the employee nearest me to acknowledge my presence. When she did I asked was there a problem with the phone service, due to the fact that no one picked up the curbside line? She said to her knowledge it was working. I then told her that I had been waiting thirty minutes in the pickup zone, with no one answering the line. I even showed her the number, when questioned about whether I dialed correctly! Well, the number was from the email reply, I showed her what it was and she then believed me. I informed her my cold food order had at that time been sitting at room temperature for nearly and hour, judging from the time stamp on the bag receipt, and she offered to have it remade, and have the manager come out to address my situation. Five minutes after this brief discussion, the manager (or what appeared to be the manager) walks out behind the counter and towards the end I was located, over to the pickup shelf, retrieves an order for a deliver service, and goes out the door, without evening stopping to acknowledge my presence. WOW! Talk about discourteous service. The counter clerk glanced at me quickly, before disappearing. I don't think I will be patronizing this location again, and please be warned, don't attempt to use curbside pickup here, unless you want to be totally ignored.

reviewText: Personally I enjoy eating at la Madeleine the food is very good we have eaten at three other locations on a few occasions always a great experience but today we tried the location at the forum and boy what a mistake it was we arrived at 10:05 a:m on a Sunday Morning not very busy at the time that we arrived.We placed our order and was given a wood block with a letter L on it and was told to find a table and they will bring our order to us when it was ready ...We went and sat down everything good drinking coffee having conversation after 45 min I started questioning about how long it was taking to receive our food so I approached the gentleman behind the counter and asked him about our order he asked me what did I order I told him what I ordered (what was the wooden block I was given for ?) I asked the gentleman to check on the food he then asked the cook who seemed to be lost about our order ..I then seen gentle reach bellow the serving counter and grab our plates he then added a potatoe patty to the plates and handed them to me ...I took to the table in which of course discovered the food was cold ..My partner asked the server if she could take her plate back and warm it up ..Mistake !!!!! 20 min went by then 30 she then went up to the counter and asked about her food they couldn't find her plate ..I asked for the Manager and told her about what happened she replied I got you ?? I got you what does that mean ? She proceeded to my table and gave me two $10.00 gift cards ..I wasn't looking for that actually it was insulting to me ..Me and my partner left and left the gift cards on the table as a tip ..Not too the Server but to the Manager that you cannot just buy your way out of poor service but to learn how to deal with a person's bad experience and maybe just be truly apologetic..We will never come back to this location again ..Will drive the extra distance to the 281 & 1604 location for a better experience...Lesson learned for me just because it's the same name doesn't mean same pleasant experience!!!

reviewText: I have been enjoying coffee and eating while finishing work at La Madeline for nearly a decade now as I get closer to wrapping up my schooling in its entirety. As I slide my tray to the cash register there is a gentleman wearing a red shirt with a full beard at the register. He never makes eye contact, he fumbles with some money, and after a long while waiting to pay he looks to an employee and request they pay me out. Never said a word to me. Of course, she comes over and struggles because the cash drawer is under him, which was confirmed when he said, "You can only log in with sliding the card if the drawer is under you," then slides his card. I can only assume he is management which is why it was so disappointing. Get the points where they are handed to you this way there is room for some error coming from true mistakes. This note is mostly for La Madeline to ensure continued growth and happy guest.

The lady at Memphis said her device said my bag was loaded and then unloaded at Dallas. I have been traveling for 36 hours now. Find my own way back home just for my bag not to be in Memphis. Worst experience of my life at an airport.

reviewText: I always order the Chicken Pesto Pasta and over the past year, I have seen the quality of the food suffer. What used to be a fresh, made to order dish with bow-tie pasta, pesto, sliced moist chicken and creamy sauce has now become a dish that looks and tastes like it is pre-made and just placed in the oven to heat it up before serving. Now what you receive is penne pasta with barely enough sauce, tough dried out chicken (from baking it in the oven again) topped with clumps of melted cheese. And now if you are lucky they serve it with a croissant instead of the previous baguette bread which was perfect for the dish, in my opinion. Will I order it again? - likely not for a while or at least until I start to crave the original version and forget how much it differs from what this dish once was.

reviewText: Update: looks like they upped their temperature for the au jus and enjoying it very much! name: la Madeleine
fullAddress: 3615 W Chandler Blvd Suite 7 Ste 7, Chandler, AZ 85226, United States
reviewText: On day 2 of their official opening, La Madeleine has some of the usual issues any new business would have. Service hiccups and incorrect orders, I am able to sympathize with and not judge too harshly. What really helped me overlook past these problems was the creamy wild mushroom sauce and coconut cream cake! After being kindly greeted in french, we placed our order, paid and took the food pager with us to the table of our choice. Complimentary slices of their sourdough and whole wheat bread were offered with mini cups of jam and butter to accompany you while you wait for your food. I picked "Chicken La Madeleine," one of their signature dishes . This entree arrived composted of a balsamic marinated chicken breast with a delicious wild mushroom cream sauce, nicely done broccoli and rice provincal that was a tad on the soggy side. "Pasta La Madeleine's" shrimp missed the boat, for the sauce was thin, runny and flat on the taste buds. Showing what they do best, La Madeleine shined at dessert time! The coconut cream cake was superb! I couldn't stop eating this wonderfully moist, layer cake that came stacked with flavor and endless sweetened, shredded coconut! I did appreciate the fireplaces, french accented decor and clean layout of this cafe. It makes for an inviting environment. In fact, I think I will be inviting myself back really soon........

reviewText: Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport opened on January 14, 1974. The airport expansion project began in 1981, and the Trade Center opened in 1995. There are 26 airlines that serve 182 cities domestically and internationally. It is a very large airport with the second largest destinations and the third largest number of passengers in the world. It is the largest airport in the United States and the second largest in the world. It is located at a transportation hub connecting North America and Texas, and has easy access to major international markets, so the Trade Center was opened and performs major functions such as the Labor Office and Customs Center. It is an airport that has a great impact on the economy of the northern Texas region. If you have time while transferring at this airport, I recommend taking the Sky Link to look around the planes and the airport. It has an enormous scale that cannot be compared to other airports.

reviewText: We had a horrible experience at the Dallas Airport. My husband’s wheel chair was not at the gate, though it was prearranged. We then had to wait for over an hour for a wheelchair. We watched 30 people come in after us and get wheelchairs. They had a room full of wheelchairs locked. Each porter was pushing 2 wheelchairs. Then had to go through customs, find our now lost baggage and wait another hour to get through TSA. TSA was horrendous. They refused to let the wheel chairs in until the Priority passengers went through . We missed our flight completely even though we had a 2 and 1/2 hour layover. The American Airline’s representative was ridiculously rude. She put us on the last flight of the night. We now won’t get to our hometown until after 11pm, five hours after we were supposed to arrive. I will never fly through Dallas again. (And we fly through Denver yearly.)

reviewText: Revised Review: Coming back to this airport after 6 years, I still find DFW to be the best airport to make a connecting flight on American Airlines or fly into DFW as a final destination. Facilities, mainly the B and C concourses, are starting to show their age. Seating and navigating the concourse can be challenging, but with constant construction going on, especially the High C Gates, I can tell that this airport is going in the right direction. The Skylink train makes connections easy and makes for a great opportunity for plane spotting. The A and D concourses are my favorite as it has a good amount of seating and dining options, as well as plenty of space to roam around the airport. The only downside to this airport is the WiFi isn't that good, so if you get it to work, consider yourself lucky. As for Texas Airports, even though Dallas Love Field is much simpler in size, which some may prefer, I still take DFW as the better airport to fly out of due to the number of destinations and things to do. The pickup and drop-off is easier than with DAL, but with the C concourse, pickup/drop-off can be challenging when there's traffic. Being the 2nd busiest airport in the U.S., I still prefer this airport as an American Airlines hub for connections instead of ORD because you don't need to leave security to get around the airport (ex., from domestic to international flights). Plus, most of the gate layout is curved instead of splitting into different sections. For the typical air traveler, I highly recommend this airport for travels within the U.S. and beyond.

reviewText: As a whole, the aiport seemed pretty nice. My issue was with reentry after being out of the country. Immigration was fine, they scanned and confirmed who I was and then we went to area where all the luggage was located. I didn't check a bag, so headed to the where the overhead sign stated the exit was. A security guard started screaming at the top of his lungs at us that there was a line and we had to go get at the end of it. I had assumed the people all around the luggage area were waiting for their bags. The line wrapped twice around then entire outside area and then in between each luggage belt terminal. No corrals, just one ticked off guard screaming at people. I'm guessing 700 people or more. People kept cutting in line, arugments and shouting, people going to miss connecting flights. All this to get to the single person checking the passport who didn't even look at it, just to see if you had one. Remember, we had all just come through customs where they scan your face or examine your passport. There is no where to merge with other people. A friend tried to complain about the people cutting line, and the security guard grabbed him and screamed for him to go to the end of the line. I tried to explain and was told to shut my mouth or he would stop the whole line. So I responded with go ahead and get upper managment down here now. There's cameras to show what was going on and how he was mistreating people. I understand my friend was upset, but also know complaing would do nothing, people cutting in line no one really cares. The way the airport handled the situation was horrible. I'm sure the guard was stressed, but he let it get to him and was taking it out on people, some coming to the US for the first time. It was so unpleasant. Several people around us stood up and confirmed we had been in line with them, but I just turned and continued up the line and he didn't bother us. I've heard from other people this has happened to them also on different days. The airport needs to address this fail in the system, put up corrales and have better signs so the foreign people can figure out wha'ts going on.

reviewText: My girlfriend and I came here yesterday, we ordered a soup, a sandwich, an iced latte, a pre-packaged cookie and a croissant. The tomato basil soup was quite literally the worst tomato soup I have ever tasted. It tasted old and microwaved, and was sour beyond belief. How do you make a tomato basil soup so sour? We had ordered a baguette on the side, they forgot it. My girlfriend and I both agreed their croissant was noticeably lower quality than the one we bought at Starbuck's earlier in the week. (Pitiful...) The sandwich I bought was a Large, it was called "Chicken Riviera". It was okay, but the bread was very hard almost to the point it hurt my mouth. It was also put together veryy sloppily, (avocado drenching the top-side of the sandwich bread) and they didn't even cut the large sandwich in half! What kind of bistro doesn't cut your large sandwich in half for you? It was put together so sloppily, I had to cut it in half myself before I could even attempt to eat it! The pre-packaged cookie was nice, but they don't make those in store. My iced latte was delicious, I will say. However, virtually everything else about the visit was extremely disappointing. We decided to give La Madeleine another try because I was tired of how often I find myself at Starbuck's for similar products. After this last time, I will never make that mistake again and I urge you to save your money as well, and probably more importantly; your time. The first time my girlfriend and I ate here a couple of months ago, we ordered two coffees and two pastries and it took 45 minutes for them to arrive at our table. Their laughable service is a running joke around Cedar Park honestly, a lot of people have heard about how miserably slow and unattentive they are. Of course we should show some sympathy for these restaurants who lost a lot of staff during Covid, but at the same time if a business simply does not possess the means to deliver to their customers the quality that they advertise, they should close down. La Madeleine may not care about customer satisfaction quite as much as they claim to.

reviewText: The restaurant itself was a lot smaller than I anticipated so I was glad that I made a reservation. It took a little bit to be seated but once we were our food came out quickly. We ordered the full gauntlet of drinks, appetizers, entrees and desserts. The highlights were the calamari, chicken Marsala, carbonara and mussels. For dessert we got the mousse, crème brûlée, fig cheesecake and tiramisu. The mousse was a bit soft but the most delicious and the crème brûlée was a bit soft but the sugar top was perfect. The other two were fine and would order them again. Our server was very nice and understood our needs though she was quite busy. This was a big bill but it was well worth it and we will be back.

fullAddress: 14028 US-183 Suite 210 Ste 210, Austin, TX 78717
reviewText: As simulations go of regional cuisine, La Madeline ain't half bad, although they certainly get some stuff much better than others. OMG, I love the soups, especially the Tomato Basil, which they're well aware of the popularity of, as they sell it to-go by the door. The deserts from the pasty bar are all quite delectable as well. It's the meals proper that have a variable quality, or, at least, don't feel very French farm house. I've never had anything I outright didn't like, but certainly have felt inspired to go try something a bit more regionally accurate for my next French craving after a so-so meal. But really, I'm being nitpicky for a place that does so much more good than bad, and quite a bit really great. reviewText: I am a huge La Medeleine fan, but this particular location needs some serious help. We walked in and a younger lady was in front of asking for an application to work at the restaurant, the cashier had no idea where the applications were so she went and got the manager who also had no idea. The manager made the salad and put no dressing on which I asked her as soon as she bagged it to make it again and she looked at me rudely. She said I didn't ask for dressing to be mixed, and I said check the receipt and she looked and just put her head down and started making a new one. She then begin to make my wife's salad which has bacon on it. She bagged it up and I checked and noticed there wasn't any bacon, she took another 2-3 minutes to go find where the bacon was and returned with it in a container. As I was leaving out the door I overheard another patron say "The soda machine isn't working" Maybe it was just a bad day for this location, but having worked in retail you have to put up with it and show some urgency. If I saw her running around and going as fast as I thought she could, I would have been a little more patient and not written this review. reviewText: If I could give negative stars I would! Atrocious customer service! Myhusband and I went in for lunch yesterday and it wasn't busy at all. When we explained what happened he asked for my receipt and then began to chastise my husband and I for not checking our receipt as it was rung up the way it was delivered. I explained that the young lady repeated my order correctly before I paid, so I didn't feel I needed to read my receipt. He continued to tell my husband and I that it was our fault and never uttered an apology. The unnerving part is that we ate at this location a few weeks ago and had bad service and decided to try again. That time our order was taken and after my food was delivered the manager (same one as above) told my husband his order could not be made. reviewText: My lunch was very good, no issues. The staff was very friendly as well. The only issue I had was when it came time to order from the dessert case. Creme bruleé is a favorite of mine and I was excited about getting one. I have had bruleé at La Madeleine before and I remember it being very good. Weeks ago I was in and ordered a bruleé cheesecake and was disappointed to find that the bruleé had been done before they were put in the refrigerated case and was, predictably, soggy. I asked today if they creme bruleé was bruleéd at service and was told no, they are not. So, that would not be creme bruleé. Maybe creme au flan or caramel, but not bruleé. I've enjoyed la Madeleine over the years but this just seems like laziness and poor quality control.

reviewText: The food La Madeleine offers is absolutely delicious. On quality of food alone I would rate La Madeleine as one of the top chains in San Antonio if not the United states far outstripping comparators (e.g. Panera). It may surprise you then that I rank - at least this location - so low. Please understand it takes a lot to earn such a low rating from me - not just a single bad experience but evidence of serious issues related to cleanliness, health, safety, or service. My negative experience started on Mother's day last year. I waited for two hours to receive my order and never got it. I called the phone number at curbside pickup pproximately every five minutes and got through maybe one time in ten. I went in multiple times (masked, socially distant, the whole nine yards) and each time was told another few minutes. After two hours, and missing the brunch I was supposed to host for my wife in the first place, I left. I was never reimbursed. Even after this infuriating experience, I gave them another shot. There were some mitigating circumstances, after all: many had the same idea as me for mother's day during the pandemic and their online ordering had obviously been overwhelmed. It was also early on in the pandemic and so I recognized that as much as it was frustrating, all businesses were struggling to adapt to the new way of doing business. So this morning, I gave them another try. I figure the morning of the superbowl would be an off day and not terribly busy. I pull up to curbside, call the number, and again no response. I wait a few minutes, call again; no response. I mask up and go inside. When i explain the situation, i get little sympathy. But here was the kicker: the man working the register, turns around, puts his gloved hand into his trousers from behind - not sure if he had an itch, was readjusting himself, or what - and then without changing gloves proceeds to transfer the fresh tray of croissants onto a dish. I don't care how good the food is, that is unsanitary and frankly disgusts me. Too many strikes. I'll never go back.

reviewText: We landed at C terminal and transferred to C terminal. We had requested wheelchair assistance to and from gates to include inability to climb steps. We ended up waiting for a wheelchair and had only one so my mother who had surgery on both legs take it. They only took us to the beginning of the gate. From there we were transferred to a motorized cart that went very slowly to a location to switch carts to the D Terminal and switched again to another one to go down the right corridor to our gate. Each time we would have to load up and unload at each section. It was all run very haphazardly and we missed our connecting flight. We were rebooked over 6 hours ahead and all the American customer service rep said was “we are not responsible for the airport transportation” so all she could was rebook us on an evening flight. Not acceptable at all. My mother should not have gone through all of that. We were told it was only 20 min from C to B terminal. Didn’t even know about the skytram until we were waiting around for 8 hours or we would have taken that. Never again will I go through Dallas/Ft Worth. I only have a 2 because the people were friendly.

reviewText: I'm sure there are people who won't agree with my rating, however, I feel they deserve it. Aug 30th...a day of chaos. The storm blew in and stopped all flights in and out. This is beyond the airports control and yet every employee I saw dealing with the aftermath of delayed and canceled flights were nice, as helpful as they could be depending on the circumstances, and worked as fast as they could. It's a huge airport with the sky train and a gazillion flights a day. Changing flights for a gazillion people. Frustrated people who had to additional stops or wait overnight, sit on the planes for an extra hour, be diverted to other airports....chaos and many tired and unhappy people. In a well oiled machine, or even one that runs good thr majority of the time, one cog out of place will throw everything off. I was affected by all of it with my flights and was tired, as were all employees at every level. So, thank you to every employee who did your very best under trying circumstances, keeping people informed by text, and my luggage was at my final destination.

reviewText: Dallas Forth Worth Airport (DFW) has been named the best airport in North America for large airports. It's BIG! Its BUSY! It's WELL-MAINTAINED. Let's jump right into this review. Pros 1. Skylink tain is fast, convenient and connects you to all/everything in the airport. It's a 15-20 minute transfer process for the entire route. The average Skylink ride is only five minutes, and trains arrive every two minutes, so you can connect to your next flight's gate efficiently while staying within the secured area of the airport. 2. Variety of food options, including some nice sit down options - Pappadeaux, Maggiano's, Chili's, Chick-fil-A, McDonald's, Pinkberry, Baskin Robbins, & Dukin Donuts are a few options I saw in Terminal C. I had Pappadeaux Shrimp (grilled - 6 pieces) and Cat Fish (fried - 2 large pieces) w/ French Fries $37. No drink included. Food is on the high side. The food was delicious! Shrimp and cat fish were seasoned well. The fries were OK. 3. Airport is relatively clean and maintained given the foot traffic. DFW is booked and busy, B-A-B-Y! 4. I saw some bathrooms had an electric sign at the entrance that kept track of the # of vacant lavatories. That's some high-tech stuff (lol). 5. Staff inside Terminal C was friendly and professional. Cons 1. I was in Terminal C, and between gates 15-35; I saw two bathrooms. A bit shocked given the size of the airport and the distance those gates covered on foot. 2. Limited charging stations in Terminal C that are safe to charge. Sumthin' 2 Note: To charge your phone safely in an airport, avoid public USB ports to prevent juice jacking, a form of cyberattack where hackers install malware. Instead, use a portable power bank or your own charger plugged directly into a wall. I had a positive experience at DFW. My connection had a 2.5 hour layover. By the time I deplaned, used the lavatory, and did an order pick-up from Pappadeaux; I had 30 minutes before my plane started to board. Wear walking/running shoes. Read the signs. Know where you are going for connection flights. Avoid a short layover, if and when possible. Be prepared for crowds and long wait times. Overall, DFW is one of the US better airports to fly in and out of. Happy travels!

reviewText: If I could give this place 0 stars, I would. Here was my first and last experience at this location: The location closes at 10, and I live less than 1.5 mi from where it is. I placed an order and finalized it online at 8:20pm, and it stated that it would be ready at 8:40pm. Great. I ordered the Roasted Salmon with Dill Sauce, which was described to come with rice provençal, and "fresh roasted" asparagus. I added a side of broccoli and a cup of the bean soup and was set to go. Wonderful. I left my home a short while later and and arrived at 8:38pm. The lady at the register brought up my order and asked about the side of broccoli, saying that it came up as a replacement side for the asparagus. I told her that I wanted it in addition to the asparagus, and she okayed that and told my total. A young gentleman who was getting my other together asked me if I wanted rice with it since he asserted that I got broccoli instead, and I answered yeah, mentioning that I was under the impression that it came with the dish, and that I ordered a side of broccoli. He mentioned the extra charge on the register screen, of which I could not see myself, and said that he'd get the rice together for me, that they'd have to heat it up. I said alright, thanked him, and waited patiently after paying my $17, thinking it wouldn't be that long of a wait. Well, he came back and said that they were out of dill sauce... at this point, I'm a little annoyed, mind you, I'm a fairly patient person, but I couldn't help but consider how ridiculous this situation is becoming. I asked what other sauces they have, and he said there was a pesto sauce.. that again, he'd have to heat up. I didn't want a dry filet of salmon, so I said ok, having paid and everything, and sat down to wait even longer. A little after 9, my food comes, and I head out the door. Before getting in my car to go home, I checked my bag only to find that---yep, you guessed it, my asparagus was missing. I go back in and wait for another 10 min for them to get it, or rather, I find out later, microwave zap it along with the rest of my god-awful food--after sorting through the confusion that they were under the impression that I subbed it out for broccoli (which was 100% overcooked with ZERO seasoning). The salmon was overcooked and tough, warmed with a microwave, and the asparagus which was BROWN was wrapped in a foil pack with a little "Sat" sticker on it, referencing two days prior (today is Monday!!) Fresh vegetables my ass! On top of that, it carried a rancid odor that spoke to how old it really was. Long story short: BAD communication, SLOW service, HORRIFICALLY AWFUL food. I don't know how this place got 4 stars, but this will absolutely be the last time I go here, or at least to this location. Should've gone to Chick-fil-A for dinner instead. Ugh.

reviewText: Let me touch down on this review by saying: DFW is less of an airport and more of a sprawling aviation-themed escape room designed by someone who once got lost in a corn maze and said, “Hold my carry-on.” This place is so big, it has its own gravitational pull. I entered Terminal A and by the time I reached Terminal D, I had aged five years and achieved platinum frequent walker status. There were sherpas. I’m pretty sure I passed a small village and a guy selling maps like it was the Oregon Trail. The Skylink train system is like a roller coaster with commitment issues—it ascends your hopes and then descends them into mild panic every time it delays. I think I accidentally circled the globe twice while trying to reach Gate C37. Honestly, I’ve seen less complicated aeronautics diagrams. Security was a breeze, if that breeze were a Category 5 headwind. I got patted down so thoroughly I feel like I owe TSA dinner and a callback. One guy looked into my bag like he was trying to read my flight plan for life. Food-wise, the options are sky-high—and I mean in price. A turkey sandwich cost $18 and came with a side of existential dread. But hey, they accept all major credit cards and minor regrets. The bathrooms? Spacious, clean, and more navigable than the terminal itself. Honestly, if I had found a vending machine and a cot in there, I might’ve just taxied into retirement. In conclusion, DFW isn’t just an airport. It’s an adventure. A journey. A saga of confusion, cardio, and Cinnabon. If you ever find yourself flying through here—bring a compass, a water bottle, and a Sherpa named Dave. And remember: it’s not about the destination, it’s about surviving the layover.

reviewText: I recently visited Lakeline Vision Source for my yearly optometry checkup and I must say, their customer service and communication exceeded my expectations. Even without health insurance, they were incredibly informative and transparent about all expenses. From the moment I walked in, the staff was welcoming and attentive. They took the time to explain each step of the process, making me feel at ease. They were not only professional but also genuinely caring. What truly stood out was their commitment to ensuring I understood the costs involved. They provided a clear breakdown of expenses and even discussed alternative options to help me make informed decisions about my eye care. They offered a variety of samples to insure my new contacts met all of my needs. One of the contact samples in the prescription I needed was not in stock. They ordered them right away and within a few days I received a call and text. After picking up my contacts, I called Brenda to inform her that my contact case at spilled in one of the monthly contacts was completely dried out. She was so understanding and kind and within minutes had another pair for me to pick up. Brenda, Angie and An went over and above in customer service and that seldom happens nowadays. Thankyou for having these 3 on your team. Overall, my experience at Lakeline Vision Source was excellent, and I highly recommend them for their outstanding customer service, communication, and affordability.

reviewText: So my review has 2 parts. It's long, sorry. 1st part for the doctors, 2nd part for the rest of the staff. My 5 stars are for the DOCTORS (and their staff at the back desk that leads into the Drs offices, they're great too!). I've seen 2 of the doctors, and they are both absolutely wonderful. Dr Basset who I've been seeing for years, and Dr Patel who helped me for the first time today. Dr Basset is always so kind and quite funny. We always have a few good laughs during my appointments, it really helps me enjoy my visits, and not dread going to the eye doc. He's such a good conversationalist and great at explaining what he's doing and why, which I appreciate greatly as the curious person I am. I just like to know what's going on, and he always takes the time to tell me and does so patiently and thoroughly. He's never in a rush, and is just so genuine and ready to help you. Dr Patel helped me for the first time today and he's fantastic too. SOOO patient. I got a new prescription a few months ago and somethings been off with my glasses ever since. He took so much time today to help me troubleshoot what could possibly be wrong. We tried everything, and he was very reassuring that he was there to help me and we weren't in a rush. He tried any silly little thing I wanted to try and I'm so grateful. In the end my prescription did change a little, but we think the problem is mostly dry eyes! I know customers like me and weird situations like mine can be exhausting, but he took everything in stride and helped me find a solution and I am eternally grateful for his patience and his efforts. Especially while my usual doctor, Dr Basset, was away. The front office staff definitely could use some customer service training. About half of them are lovely, truly. But the other half are curt, and don't own up to their mistakes. Some time ago I got an email with an appointment reminder. When I showed up for my appointment they said I didn't have one. I showed them the email that I had that said I had an appointment that day at that time, and they said there was some error with their email system and they just sent me away. I tried to argue a few times that I definitely had an appointment that day, I'd gotten several emails and texts about it, as I always do. But they just kept cutting me off and making excuses. They didn't even try and fit me in, they just told me to leave and reschedule. They're lucky I love these doctors that I just spoke so highly of otherwise I never would have come back here. It's a miracle I come here at all. I drive 40 minutes from Scottsdale just to see these fantastic doctors. More than worth it for the docs, but some of the front office should really be talked to about their attitudes.

reviewText: Since I moved to Houston nearly 3 years ago, I have been told to try this delicious bakery. I am addicted and it has absolutely moved up to one of my all-time favorites- without a doubt. The cordon Bleu pasta with the croissant, amazing. The loaded baked potato soup, a delicacy with crispy bacon. Their new prime rib sandwich, to die for. name: MOD Pizza
fullAddress: 8134 Agora Pkwy Suite 250, Live Oak, TX 78154, United States
reviewText: I have been eating at Mod Pizzas in several states for several years. I live in Selma now and have eaten at this location numerous times. I love the pizza but have noticed a real decline in the employees ability and willingness to work hard at what they do. Last night for my birthday I told my wife let’s just go get pizza. We get to the restaurant and there were six or eight people in front of us in line. Giving me ample time to watch the employees that were working. There was one guy that was supposed to be pressing the dough into the 11 inch size. At all the other stores that I have eaten at they take a two layers if you what a thick crust. But he was squeezing two dough balls together and then pressing them out. His technique wasn’t the big problem but watching him play around with the dough knife all over the machine and the surrounding area. Then the fact that he was not doing anything but playing with the dough and only pressed about three pieces in the 20 minutes that we were in line. The other guy that was making the pizzas had his hat over his eyes and appeared to be on something. It took him over five minutes to put the toppings on my pizza and half of the containers were empty or low of toppings and instead of getting more from the refrigerator behind him, he would walk over and grab some from the next prep area. It was so obvious that he was worthless that after making my pizza a different employee working the register offer us a discount and then told him to clean tables. This was also very difficult to watch someone spraying cleaner everywhere except on the tables he was supposed to be cleaning with a dirty paper napkin. It was hard to watch two employees doing nothing and with no sense of responsibility or drive to do things right for which you are getting paid. These two apparently do not appreciate having a job and drag the entire restaurant down.

reviewText: If I could give this place a negative number, I would. I went there for the first and last time today at this Montfort location. I wanted quiche and almond croissants. I walked in - all the almond croissants were burnt. Asked if they had more, they didn't have any. I've been baking since I was 9 years old. My mother would've never allowed me to serve anything like this to family or guests. So I got the quiche lorraine and got muffins from Tom Thumb. Got home - warmed the quiche up. It was not fresh...tasted like it had been frozen and thawed out. Absolutely no seasoning of any kind. I've had better out of the box at the grocery store or Sam's from frozen food aisle. The owners of La Madeleine have completely destroyed not only the French bistro concept and charm that this restaurant once had before, but now they have absolutely insulted anyone's understanding of edible food. AWFUL - never again..

My dog had a hard time chewing the bread so I know my 3 yr old niece (who it was ordered for) would not have had a chance. HIGHLY disappointed with la Madeleine and very sad about it. The change is not for the better. I see this is a new concept location. I will have to order from the main restaurant in the future and see if it's any better. I still stand by the lack of quality vs original store.

fullAddress: 2400 Aviation Dr, DFW Airport, TX 75261, United States
reviewText: Major Disappointment for a Major Hub For one of the busiest airports in the world, Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW) is shockingly underwhelming. You’d think that with the amount of traffic and money flowing through here, it would be a polished, well-run operation. Unfortunately, it’s quite the opposite. Once you're inside, the experience doesn’t improve much. The terminal itself looks like a relic from the early 1990s. The rugs are old, stained, and visibly worn out. Tape is peeling up from the floors in random spots, and seating areas are dirty and uncomfortable. It’s the kind of environment that makes you want to stay standing — not because you want to, but because you don’t trust the chairs. Want to eat something while you wait? Good luck. The food areas are often messy and neglected. Tables are sticky, floors are littered, and there’s very little effort put into keeping things clean. For such a high-traffic airport, it’s honestly unacceptable. And don’t even think about getting online easily. The internet is painfully slow, and if you're flying with American Airlines — which basically owns this airport — guest Wi-Fi access is a maze of red tape. They make it incredibly difficult to just log in and check your email without jumping through hoops. It’s a ridiculous barrier for something that should be a basic amenity. All in all, DFW is a huge letdown. This airport should be world-class, but instead it feels neglected, outdated, and mismanaged. With the amount of money and passengers coming through here, it deserves — and desperately needs — serious improvement.

reviewText: This restaurant was quite bad and I'm dismayed at the many positive reviews (although some of the photos and reviews come across as advertisements to me). My wife and I stopped in and noticed the restaurant had very few patrons, all on the patio. We sat inside a neat looking but quite noisy indoor dining area with concrete floors and extremely flimsy chairs that sagged backwards uncomfortably. There appeared to only be a single waiter working despite it being dinnertime. We ordered calamari for an appetizer. The size was very small, particularly for the price, and the calamari wasn't drained well, so each piece dripped of oil. They were served on a bed of soggy bell peppers. Nothing wrong with the concept, but it looked like filler to make the dish less expensive to make. We ordered a pizza and a pasta, and were told both were homemade. I'm not sure what that means, as the bread of the pizza and the noodles to the pasta didn't seem fresh. Both came out on extremely hot dishes (suggesting they sat under a heatlamp for a long time before being served). The carbonara sauce was separated, with soggy, limp bacon, and was an extremely oily mess. The pasta was overcooked. I was unable to finish this. The pizza was worse. It was larger than the plate it was served on, and it wasn't actually pizza. It was just thin but not crispy bread, covered in cheese (no sauce), and with an extraordinary amount of uncooked arugala thrown on top. Cheese bread with a salad on top. The bread had dark grill lines all over it, but was completely limp and without texture. My wife was unable to eat it. My theory about this is that the something went wrong with the pizza, and they made the one we were served on the fly while my pasta sat under a heat lamp, giving us undercooked pizza and ruined pasta. But whatever the issue was, the food sucked, it looked bad, and a good restaurant would not have served it. The pasta was $15, and the pizza was also overpriced. For 4 star prices, I was surprised that the people bringing this food to the table were wearing t-shirts and jeans and looked like they had been working in the yard all day. I suspect this couple were actually the owners pulling double duty. That is admirable, but please dress like you're working in a professional restaurant if you charge such high prices. Despite the restaurant being completely empty when we arrived, a family with young kids were sat right next to our table. I like kids, but the concrete floors and the screaming child were not a winning combo. For desert we ordered the tiramisu, which was excellent. Still, for a three course meal we were starving when we left. So my advice to the owners: dress appropriately, seat tables separated, and fix the food. Wal-Mart has a more comfortable atmosphere, better dressed staff, and frankly better pizza.

reviewText: My wife & I went here for our 3rd wedding anniversary last night, and we loved it! I picked it because they make their pasta fresh, and I love handmade pasta. The owner, James, was very nice & friendly, came out and introduced himself and checked to make sure everything was going well. Our waitress, Michelina, was great, super friendly and personable, and very attentive to our needs. We sat on their covered patio (it was raining super hard) and sipped our wine and had a delicious dinner. We had the aricini, then the roasted beets with gorgonzola cream, then the mushroom grilled pizza, then the gnochi (we just shared everything) and finished with tiramisu for me & chocolate mousse for my wife. Everything was fresh, and delicious. Pricing is middle of the road, not cheap, but definitely not expensive. The decor is modern and clean, but not very upscale. Overall, I give it a 5 star although some may give it 4 because of it's not "fine dining" but we loved the food and the staff, and will definitely go back, and recommend to anyone looking for a good Italian menu.

reviewText: Where do I begin? Great food, horrid service. We went to Cedro's for Mother's Day Brunch. The dining room is very attractive and modern looking. We ordered our food and the waitress confirmed the adjustments we'd made to the orders (my grandmother is 92 and only wanted 2 eggs instead of 3 for example). The first issue came with the entree delivery. My French Toast was brought out and we waited for the other entrees but they never came. We asked the waitress how much longer it would be and she sort of smiled and nodded (English was not her first language). After 15 minutes my mother suggested I start eating my food before it got cold and nasty. Finally my father and mother's food came out, but still nothing for my 92 year old grandmother. She had the most basic meal of us all - 2 scrambled eggs, sausage and toast. I feel like hers should have come out with mine or at least with my parents' food, yet nothing. We couldn't find the waitress so I stopped one of the hostesses and she immediately came back with eggs and sausage. Sadly, the eggs were sunny side over and not scrambled and my grandmother hates runny eggs. We tell our waitress about the error and a manager comes out shortly with scrambled eggs, but still no toast. At this point she's upset and doesn't want anything to eat and I couldn't blame her. The oldest person at the table had to sit and watch people eat even though she ordered the easiest thing to prepare; it basically ruined our mother's day brunch. As I said in the first sentence, everything tastes GREAT! There is something going on with the communication between the waitstaff and the kitchen that ruins the dining experience at this place. I can't suggest that anyone go there given what happened to us even though the chef is obviously good.

name: Cedro Scratch Italian & Wine Bar
fullAddress: 14028 US-183 Suite 210, Austin, TX 78717, United States
reviewText: I came here for lunch this afternoon, and to say that I was disappointed, is an understatement. When my companion and I first entered the restaurant, there was no one to greet us nor show us the way to our table. We waited a couple of minutes assuming that we would be assisted after a moment, but when both gentlemen came from the kitchen, one went to the bar and began to look at his cell phone while the waiter went to check on his tables before seating us. I understand that you need to ensure that your customers are satisfied with their service, but no one had even acknowledged our arrival. When we were greeted, we were told to choose any table and were given our menus. We were then ignored for another 10 minutes. We had reviewed the menu before arriving at the establishment and had an idea of what we wanted to try (this being our first and last experience with Cedro). After the ten minutes, we decided that if our waiter walked past us without taking our order, we were going to leave before trying the food. Unfortunately, our waiter arrived to take our order. I'll explain the 'unfortunately' part of that sentence in a moment. Our food arrived quickly and we liked the salads that we ordered. My companion's salad was the green salad and the roasted red pepper was prevalent, but not overwhelming. I had the Caesar salad which I found intriguing because it came with freshly grilled bread which was surprising, but it was quite good. Our issues came with the main course. I ordered the Fettuccine Carbonara with smoked bacon and a poached egg. The egg was perfectly poached from my perspective, but my issues came when I went to eat. The carbonara sauce was extremely thin and the bacon was limp. When you order a meal with bacon, you expect it crisp to add a nice textural element. No. In all honesty, I couldn't finish my meal. My companion ordered Orecchiette (which our waiter corrected her pronunciation of, we came for a quick meal, not an Italian grammar lesson), and she stated that the pasta didn't taste handmade and there was a mushroom that she couldn't even chew. Our food arrived quickly, but not quickly enough to make up for the atrocious service and substandard food. I enjoy food and I think if a few changes were made, this could be a decent little place. Maybe change the bacon in the Carbonara to crispy pancetta, thicken the sauce and using a different poaching liquid for the egg (it seemed a little sweet to me). Also, please teach your waitstaff some common courtesies.... simply put, a smile would be nice and an apology for the wait without any service.

reviewText: Something has happened at LaMadeleine, over past year or so. There are several different locations where I have eaten for many years. One of the my favorite meals is the Country French breakfast, they scrambled eggs were always so fluffy & cooked to perfection Probably the last 3 or 4 times I have ordered this eggs have been scorched. I can do that at home. Also the portion is significantly smaller while the price almost doubled since 2022. (Of course, I am aware of change in prices of eggs) Today, I ate at Preston / Forest location & ordered French toast eggs & bacon. I was sitting outside because it was still lovely before noon.. When my food was delivered, bacon looked very greasy, eggs were not scorched this time.Thank goodness. French toast was cold. I went back in and told cashier. She told me I had to bring it back in.So I grabbed it to go box to put my eggs and bacon in. Then I dutifully brought plate back in. I waited 10 minutes or more, was eating other 2 food items, however , they were also not hot. I went back in and asked to speak with manager. She brought me a card for a free meal. I said "thank you, but I want my french toast" She told me they were remaking it. I did tell her, at that time, that rest of my breakfast was not hot either. However I ate it. In a few more minutes, she brought me a new plate of all food ordered. Guess what? Still not hot. I related this to her and said , I was taking eggs and bacon home, was not going to waste it!! I would reheat them there... I already had my go box. Probably more than an hour later, after I had run another errand in Center, dirty dishes were still on table outside as well as to other tables where patrons had been. Regards, Barbara

reviewText: Ahh man, hell yeah. They're good. I eat here multiple times a month with zero regret. The noodles are always cooked just right for slurping, amazing flavors, and great staff. Saying that, the flavors can be strong so be prepared, these are not wimpy flavor profiles, but they're well balanced and nothing becomes super overwhelming in any of the bowls. They obviously take pride in their dishes, they'll fix anything they get wrong, and the ramen is always satisfying. My two personal favorites are the Sho-yu with the yuzu bomb and marinated tofu or the now recently re-added (happy to have it back!) Tsukemen dipping ramen. Don't get me wrong, I love the OG, but the extra umami that the Sho-yu and Tsukemen give me, just edges them a touch higher for me. If it's your first time though I strongly recommend the OG with the corn bomb or the Ol' Skool as is, which is chicken broth ramen (and makes for a great cold remedy!). Also, if you manage to eat a whole bowl and somehow still have room for a bit of something, they've brought in dipdipdip ice cream for a burnt orange or matcha ice cream sandwich. My personal preference is the burnt orange as it's got a nice almost chocolate covered orange flavor, the matcha one though is the favorite of everyone else I've brought here. I can't recommend coming here enough. It's delicious, filling, relaxed, and falls squarely in the best of "keep austin weird" traditions.
