reviewText: Made the hour drive to come and eat at my favorite ramen joint! Haven't been since the pandemic. As always, the staff is wonderful and super friendly. For a Saturday, it wasn't especially busy so there wasn't a long wait to order and get seated. I ordered the Miso Hot (spicy miso ramen) with an extra Ajitama (marinated soft boiled egg) and a Hibi-Gibi (hibiscus and lemongrass iced tea). It was absolutely delicious! The Miso Hot wasn't as spicy as it usually is, but it was flavorful and hit the spot. The Hibi-Gibi was a wonderful fusion of flavors and really complimented the ramen, really balancing the savory with a light sweetness. With a closer location, I'll definitely be back.

reviewText: I went to this location for lunch yesterday after having gone to the other in Austin. The first and most noticeable thing was the fact that the food quality and taste was the exact same. That’s a rare thing when a restaurant grows. This is where the trouble started. After ordering our food we sat for more than 30 minutes without our food. I politely asked a gentleman if he could check on it. A young lady approached us a few moments later and verified our order. She apologized and said it would be straight out. The good. I thanked her politely again and she went to the back. She came back with our food moments later and apologized again for the delay. I told her it was no big deal while again being as nice as I could. The great. When we were almost done with our meal that same young lady appeared and told me she had refunded our money in full. I insisted this was not necessary as we enjoyed our meal but she refused and insisted we get our money back. The food and willingness to take care of the customer is the reason I will frequent this place in the future. Thank you to everyone who worked there yesterday.

name: Ramen Tatsu-Ya
fullAddress: 14028 US-183 Bldg G, Suite 310, Austin, TX 78717
reviewText: It finally happened! Ramen Tatsu-Ya up north in the burbs, Lakeline meets Cedar park and my foodie self from my younger 20's living in the arboretum/domain is thrilled. I have eaten at Tatsu-Ya numerous times since its inception days of stomping its way into Austin bringing into the foodie world, the obsession of what is their tonkatsu broth, yum. Heavy, rich, divine and extra sodium heavy like ramen does, it's just as tasty as I remembered. The interior in this one is the same vibe and style as the OG off Payton gin, very kitschy, artsy and super beautiful with the natural lighting. Service is just the same, a line awaits you, you get a number, and then once you order, the staff will seat you at an appropriate opening. The perk, the communal table is much smaller and there are smaller tables for small parties! No bar seating here boo like the OG, but that's ok! I ordered the #9 Curry Nu Skool which is vegetarian broth and added an extra ajitama, yum! Missing their dipping ramen on the menu which I didn't see, but all the sides = yum. The outside space has heaters for a chilly day, and it's perfect with your hot piping ramen! Welcome Tatsu-Ya and can't wait to dine here again and again! Slurps up!

name: Dallas Fort Worth International Airport
fullAddress: 2400 Aviation Dr, DFW Airport, TX 75261, United States
reviewText: I have had to fly out of DFW on 2 separate occasions and both were awful due to the personnel working at this airport. First occasion, the people were rude and unhelpful. Unfortunately that can happen just about anywhere so I tried to look past it. The second occasion though is just incredibly unbelievable. I was in the TSA line and was waiting behind a gentleman who had to take somethings out of his bag (probably electronics) and was taking quite a bit of time doing so. There was a TSA agent who was getting bins ready for people to place their belongings in. (Or that’s what I thought) once again the man in front of me was taking sometime to get of his belongings and so I went around him so I would not hold up the already long ling behind me. I start to place my items in said bins that TSA agent had placed, and I very politely asked her if I had to take my laptop out. She replies in such a disrespectful demeanor saying, “these are not for you.” I realized that she must have only put those bins for the man. I apologized and took out my belongings and went back and waited behind the man. A couple minutes later the same attendant says to me in the same disrespectful tone, “get your own bins.” I do so and start placing my own belongings in the bins I chose. While being baffled that the woman was just being so incredibly rude I was unable to hear exactly what she said next, but she started saying comments about me to another person who was waiting behind me. I did hear him go, “are you talking about me?” And she goes, “nah her” while pointing at me. Unfortunately I was already in an emotional state of mind because I had to say goodbye to a loved one and was leaving, and then I had just experienced blatant disrespect/ racism. All I was able to do in that moment was tell the another TSA agent how rude the other agent was. The Forth Worth/ Dallas area is a lovely place and the people OUTSIDE the airport are some of the nicest people I have ever met, and I’ve loved coming to visit here. But after these last two experiences, I would NOT recommend flying in this airport if you’re not okay with the complete disrespect you’ll receive for most workers.

reviewText: This review is solely based on my experience on today. Suggested by my wife we went to dine. So to make a long story short....upon paying for our meal I was handed a dirty glass. Water spots I can handle but stuck on food residue I won't do. I gave the glass back and requested to use a togo cup instead. Fixed my water, wanted to add lemon, however the lemon container had not been replenished. The few in there looked as though they were in there from the day before. Also no straws available, they didn't put any more out until we were leaving. Taking our seat I sipped my water and it had a funny taste as if the drink/ice machine hadn't been cleaned in a while. I order the potato cake which I got in the line, and the provolone chicken rice bowl that I had to wait to be prepared and brought to me. My wife had to replace her utensil because the first one was still dirty with food particles. As I waited for my food I had eaten my potato cake but my additional dish had not come out. I noticed several customers after us receive their orders but I hadn't yet received mine. We had to check the receipt just to make sure they added the dish on our order. Well I sat and watched my wife eat her food alone. We did not have the pleasure of enjoying our meals together. Finally when we where getting ready to go, I'm guessing she was the manager, noticed we still had our letter tag on our table so she went to the back to check on what we were waiting on. We went to the counter to ask about the dish and finally it came out which I had to tell them I'll just get it to go. So they put it in a togo container handed it to me without a bag, without any utensils, and without an apology for the wait and inconvenience of having to take my meal to go because someone dropped the ball. It was not busy at all, numerous employees, but much disorganization. Needless to say this was my first experience visiting La Madeleine and will be my last time visiting La Madeleine. Additionally the food is subpar based on other restaurants in the area. Coconut cream cake taste store bought or brought in from off site not homemade. Customer service non existent beyond ordering and paying for your meal. Dishes not cleaned very well. No hello's or thank you's for coming. I hope others do not have the same experience I just had because this left a sour taste in my mouth.

reviewText: Was in La Madeleine for breakfast. I found the manager, Lester, to be apathetic and discourteous. My husband and I waited to place our order as Lester chatted with a worker. He did not ask us to excuse him while he handled whatvever non-emergency issue that was at hand nor did he acknowledge our presence. When I mentioned it to him, he gave me a blank stare. I suggested that he should have acknowledged that we were standing there. He said flatly "I spoke to you when you came in". I don't know if he did or didn't. I don't think he did. Whether he did or not, it had no relevance to our waiting for his little chat to end. He said nothing but just stood there waiting for us to place our order. We did. I ordered the potato galette and an order of bacon. I was told that the galette would take 10 minutes. I was okay with that. After several minutes, my husband received his order and I received 3 bacon slices. I suppose I could have stated I wanted to receive the potato galette and bacon at the same time. I did not realize that it was necessary to state the obvious. I returned the bacon order to the counter. A young woman at the counter told me the galette would be ready in few minutes. I told her that was fine but my bacon would be cold by then. I asked that the galette be served with bacon. She seemed personally offended. She took the plate and walked away without a word to me. Based on the prior poor customer-oriented response from the manager, her atttitude was not surprising. The galette and bacon was brought to me by the manager, Lester. Not a word was said about the delay, the inconvenience, nor the fact that my husband and I had come to have breakfast together, but were served several minutes apart. The food was fair, a little salty. The service is below par. We chose La Madeleines because is near our home in Champion Forest. Next time we will opt to go to our favorite breakfast spot, Le Peep's. It's worth the extra time and travel to the Westchase area for good food and much better service.

reviewText: Where to begin on this? Next to cover the food, first I will say their deserts and bakery items are perfection each that my wife and I tried were incredibly delicious. We were there for lunch so I ordered the french dip sandwich with the tomato basil soup both of which I found to be flavored wonderfully without any one flavor overpowering the dish. My wife ordered the French Onion soup which was also absolutely delicious and the mimosa she ordered came out as a small champaign bottle and small carafe of orange juice (roughly 3 glasses worth of mimosa). Over all the price, quality of food, and service were outstanding and I highly look forward to many more meals here.

reviewText: I've been an avid La Madeline customer since the 1990s. When I first discovered La Madeline, I lived in Irving; however, Arlington's closest location, and I gladly drove for my favorite items. So, one can imagine my excitement when I learned that this location would open just minutes from my office. The excitement was short-lived; this new concept is nothing short of a fast-food chain that serves pre-packaged meals, a limited menu, and inflated prices. My lunch was served to me in a plastic sack (not even branded), no silverware, and stickers on my salad as if I had purchased it from 7-11. This review is not a reflection of the employees at this location but the corporation. Over the years, I've seen subtle changes to the brand but have accepted it, but this change has surpassed the limitations I'm willing to accept. Sadly, I won't return to this location.

I called the store the next day to explain what happened. The manager told me that if I wanted a refund, I would have to bring the receipt and come back to the location in person. I found that response unhelpful and disappointing. Instead of offering a sincere apology or even a small store credit for the inconvenience, I was asked to make another trip just to get my money back for something that should never have been sold in the first place. It’s very frustrating to buy a dessert at the end of the day and realize they are selling items that should have been thrown away. I hope the management improves their quality control and shows more respect for their customers’ time and experience.

reviewText: I hadn’t had La Madeleine in a while and was craving their Caesar salad and tomato soup, so I placed a takeout order, even though it’s a 20-minute drive each way (40 minutes total). When we got home and sat down to eat, I realized the Caesar salad was missing its dressing. I called the restaurant, and their only solution was for me to drive all the way back, another 40 minutes roundtrip, for a completely new salad. I ended up eating the original salad with ranch from my fridge, not what I wanted. Since we were hungry and did not want to wait another 40 minutes. Husband went back for the replacement. I told him it was pointless. Mistakes happen, but it only takes a few seconds to double-check an order before handing it off. People are spending their time, gas, and money to support a business, and it’s frustrating when the burden to fix errors falls entirely on the customer. So now I have a soggy replacement salad sitting in my fridge, and I had to eat the original one with ranch from home, not what I paid for or wanted. No offer for a refund, no accountability, just a shrug and more wasted time on my part. It’s not just about a missing dressing, it’s the complete disregard for the customer’s time, gas, and experience. If restaurants want people to keep coming back, they need to treat accuracy and service as a priority, not an afterthought.

reviewText: Unfortunately, today's review won't be good. I've been to La Madeleine before, and my previous visits have been very good. I found out from a friend that they had remodeled it, and I decided to come for breakfast. I was served by the manager, Jackie, who took my order at the register, and I truly felt humiliated. She assumed I didn't know why I didn't speak English. Maybe because I look Latina, she shouldn't assume anything. I speak perfect English, so I told her. She continued trying to say a few words in Spanish. What I felt wasn't pleasant. Aside from that bad experience, I ordered my breakfast, and it was cold inside. Of course, I returned it and asked for a refund because I was no longer hungry. As a manager, she should have refunded the entire ticket, but she only returned my food. As a food service worker, I was trained differently. Aside from the apology I received, she should have refunded the entire bill. Based on my experience today, I'm giving it less than one star. That doesn't mean it's always like this, but they should review some things in management.

reviewText: *GO TO A DIFFERENT LOCATION. THIS PLACE IS A BAIT AND SWITCH SCAM* I have never left a review of a place before but my two experiences at this location compelled me. First time I get my usual order, a croque monsieur and a cup of potato soup. The soup was great as always but wow, the croque monsieur was the worst one I’ve ever gotten. It looked like the middle school knock off version the lunch lady tried to make. It looked and tasted like it was only half way prepared, it was cold and you could tell it was not prepared at all the way it needed to. Not even the cheese on the outside of the sandwich was melted. I said I wouldn’t go back for awhile after that but today, I found myself not feeling that well today and a bowl of potato soup from La Madeline is my go to when feeling sick. I pull up to the window and ask for bread or some crackers for my soup, as they offer these things for free in their locations. I was absolutely shocked when the women told me that this location is a “boutique” location and the bread costs money and they don’t have anything for the soup. What other things are they going to charge for because it’s a “boutique” location? Here’s my problem, there are zero signs, advertising, or any indication that this place is different than your average La Madeline. It feels pretty scammy to me to advertise your store as a regular one but then tell people when asking for something provided at the normal store for free, you charge them for it. You need to add some kind of sign within two weeks or I will get the BBB, the city, or whoever needs to know because this is false advertising, it’s a pure bait and switch. Not even the Google listing for this place mentions it’s a boutique. Something is not right and I will happily make sure this is corrected.

reviewText: Hey :) I’m in a season of learning about how we must try and include others in our appointments, yet maintain relational purity, presence of mind, and arriving on time. An important lesson I’ve learned is that, “There is a way that seems right to a man, but the end thereof is the way of death” (scripture). I looked this up online, and it explains that to avoid this reality, we must be willing to follow the Lord’s direction according to Proverbs 3:5, 6 and not rely on our own understanding. reviewText: I rather much like La Madeiline. Food, great. Atmosphere, great. But ,unfortunately for this La Madeline, service was mediocre, employees maintaining conversation even when noticing there is a customer waiting to give them there order, time wait for food was longer than it should have been, and I do not appreciate it when I see an employee carry food from the kitchen, in her palms( she did wear gloves) to an order sitting on the counter of the to go station in front of the customers, for me that was a bit unsafe carrying food around like that. You could notice that employees were taking their time with orders which is a bit annoying because customer want their food out as quick as possible. I ordered a chicken parisian duet with pasta and side salad. The pasta and salad were the first things out of course but the sandwich took approximately 15 to bring out even then when I checked the sandwich the chicken was cold on the outside but warm on the inside the placement of the chicken and cheese on top look as If they took scrapes from another sandwich and put it in the sandwich. And the toast was really dry and too toasted. Pasta... well not good but not bad either. This establishment should try to push there employees to move a bit quicker especially if the cafe is more than half full and to go orders are piling up. I'm sure the employees all have wonderful attitudes, but their time management from the orders to the customers should be a lot quicker. Personally, I will not be returning to that unit, but others if who are willing to wait a while and chat with friends, enjoy!

reviewText: It is a Friday afternoon and I placed an online order as a request from my husband who had been at home ill for the day. Once the order was placed I received a call that they did not have the product available to full the complete order. I made a substitute. When I got the the restaurant NONE of the order was ready - not even the two sandwiches I had ordered. But there were several workers standing around doing nothing, THEN when I received my order it did not include one of the items I had ordered online. I called the store and received numerous apologies and then the manager hung up on me. A few minutes later she called back once again apologizing saying she "dropped the phone". I am frustrated and angry at the service but there is something else corporate needs to address. The place was DIRTY. the floors both behind the counter and at the entrance were dirty, there was an trash can in the entrance that was overflowing and there were gnats flying around the bread - which was open, and also in the checkout counter area. This place has taken a nosedive downhill. I have been eating here over ten years and I have never seen it like this. This was just before the dinner rush and I experienced an unfilled order, dirty public areas, and employees standing around talking. No since of urgency in a location where if you stand in the street count at least 20 food establishments. I put my crepe down my garbage disposal and I will not be returning.

reviewText: We went to Cedro Scratch Italian without much expectation beyond having a solid dinner. No special occasion, no hype cycle — just a normal night out. That matters, because it became clear very quickly that this is a place that doesn’t rely on momentum or novelty to be great. What stood out first wasn’t any single dish, but the consistency. Every plate felt composed, intentional, and confident. Nothing was rushed. Nothing felt like filler. This is a kitchen that understands fundamentals and executes them quietly, which is harder than it looks and rarer than it should be. The lamb shanks were exceptional — slow-cooked to the point where the meat separated effortlessly while still retaining depth and structure. Rich, deeply flavored, but never heavy. It’s the kind of dish that reflects patience more than technique. The NY steak was equally impressive in a different way. Perfectly cooked, cleanly seasoned, and left alone to be what it is. No distractions, no unnecessary embellishment — just excellent beef handled with restraint. The pasta was one of the highlights of the night. Light, fresh, and clearly scratch-made. The sauces were balanced and bright, allowing the ingredients to speak instead of being buried. Italian food that satisfies without weighing you down. Even the pizza, which at many restaurants feels like a separate lane, was executed at the same high level. Great crust, proper balance, and clearly treated with the same care as everything else. The wine selection was thoughtful and well-curated, clearly chosen to complement the food rather than simply fill out a list. Everything worked together naturally. Then came dessert, which pushed the experience into a different tier. These were some of the best desserts we’ve had, period. The only place that even enters the conversation is a standout dessert spot in Georgetown, and Cedro absolutely holds its own. We would return just for dessert alone. Our server, Michaela, was outstanding — calm, attentive, and perfectly paced. She elevated the evening without inserting herself into it and clearly understood how to support the flow of the meal. At one point, I wanted to speak with the owner simply to say thank you for building something this thoughtful. They weren’t there, but that absence was telling in a positive way. The standards here are embedded. The restaurant runs on culture, not oversight. By the end of the meal, the only real question was how this hadn’t already become a regular stop for us. Cedro Scratch Italian isn’t flashy or loud. It doesn’t need to be. It’s just consistently excellent in the ways that matter most. We’ll be back — often — and we’ll be rethinking what we thought great Italian food meant for a while.

reviewText: Scratch?? Maybe … but certainly not FRESH. 1st the wait staff definitely didn’t think we were worth their time. Almost no balsamic, but it did taste fresh and was the best thing. But come on… three tiny pieces??? The photo on here even shows four, how do you share an appetizer of three?? Ok moving on. We shared (went with my grown daughter) an espresso martini… heavy on the vodka- just wasn’t good. Yes… one alcoholic drink and our bill was still over $100. Next we got the Braised lamb orecchiette (to which the waitress tried correcting me on the pronunciation … I’m an Italian from Brooklyn…) and the pappardelle ragu e pesto. The pasta was over cooked. In both. Mushy. Almost no pesto in the e pesto. One TINY dab. The sausage was just crumbled so really it was just a red sauce with a bit of sausage. My lamb was dry even in the red sauce. Hard to do… but they managed. Neither plate was even warm. We waited for over forty minutes BETWEEN COURSES and we didn’t even get warm food?? Both dishes were just pasta and red sauce with a bit of different meats. And the red sauce was horrifically acidic. My god worse sauce I’ve ever had- jar sauce would have been better. So unbalanced- felt sick for the rest of the night… even a ten year old knows how to cut acid, who is the chef here??? Not impressed. And no bread. No cheese. Just a plate of room temperature, over cooked pasta with dry meat from maybe a few days ago. No idea why, but we went with sharing a crème brûlée for desert. Right out of the fridge. Dead COLD and about 1.5 centimeters thick in the shallowest ramekins I’ve ever seen in my life. The top clearly hadn’t even just been browned but done previously and then refrigerated. Who does that?? Such a horrible experience. And back to the wait staff- assign tables so they aren’t tripping over each other saying over and over has anyone helped you… honestly, it’s like restaurant 101. If the wait staff is in blue jeans I shouldn’t be paying over $50 a person. Save your money, nothing about this place was good. *edit after horrific response from owner(?)* oh… we can play. Nice edit for your ‘supposed’ timeline. You can try to say anything you like… I had a watch on. The martini was ordered WELL after the app so how did it arrive in four min??? And the chick that delivered it took at least a min to get to me because I WATCHED her navigate the busiest side and wondered exactly how stupid do you have to be to walk down THAT side?? And your waitress and host in blue jeans??? Yeah. Upscale. The 1.5 cm crème brûlée? I didn’t say it was BAD… it was DEAD COLD. And itty bitty tiny. The top WAS NOT just fired. Nice try. And the tree pieces of bruschetta??? Any comment on that???? For $16????? lol And nope… pasta was over cooked and room temp. You don’t think we’ve ever eaten cold bad pasta before??? We were HUNGRY you little bitty… of course we ATE IT. Note I didn’t ask for a mother flipping REFUND… I just want to warn others. But get on with your bad self… this makes you look ridiculous. *chefs kiss*

name: Cedro Scratch Italian & Wine Bar
fullAddress: 14028 US-183 Suite 210, Austin, TX 78717, United States
reviewText: If you’re craving some good pasta, this is your spot. Granted, I’ve only tried the bolognese so far. It was delicious and makes me want to try the others pastas as well. I had also requested some extra parmesan and the kind waitress brought a heaping side of it which was nice. The grilled focaccia was also delightful - warm, soft on the inside and perfectly crisp on the outside, served with an olive oil and balsamic dip. My fiancé had the steak, eggs and potatoes from the Sunday brunch menu which was good. We were there around 11am and upon walking in, we were greeted by the friendly staff. But my first impression was that it was quite dark in there. Most of the window shades were still pulled down. As it was an overcast day I think it would be nice to open the shades and brighten the space a bit more.

name: Cedro Scratch Italian & Wine Bar
fullAddress: 14028 US-183 Suite 210, Austin, TX 78717, United States
reviewText: Visited Cedro Scratch Italian & Wine Bar with a friend and had a mixed experience. The restaurant definitely has a nice Italian vibe, and the atmosphere is warm and inviting. Our server was really friendly and attentive, which made the visit pleasant. We ordered a chicken pizza with mushrooms, pasta, garlic bread, and focaccia. While everything was well-presented, the food itself felt average from our perspective. The flavors didn’t quite stand out and came across as a bit bland, especially compared to other Italian restaurants in Austin that offer bolder and more memorable flavors. I also tried a cocktail, which was decent but nothing exceptional — I’d rate it around 3/5. Overall, this place earns points for its ambience and service, but the food has room for improvement to really shine. With more depth in flavors, it could become a much stronger dining option.

name: Cedro Scratch Italian & Wine Bar
fullAddress: 14028 US-183 Suite 210, Austin, TX 78717, United States
reviewText: First time ever eating from here so I tried something simple which was the spaghetti and meatballs and let me tell you it was MID ladies and gentlemen. Maybe it’s because I’m from New York City so I’m very spoiled with Italian food but this is one of the easiest dishes to get right and they failed. The marinara is lacking, the noodles were way too mushy and the meatballs can knock out your grandmothers dentures. The people inside were very nice at least. Definitely won’t be ordering here again.

reviewText: Cedro Scratch Italian & Wine Bar offers a nice italian dining experience, We started with the bruschetta, which was fresh but slightly sweet. The lamb orecchiette was rich, well cooked, and full of depth. The NY strip steak was tender and cooked just right, and the chocolate mousse was a decadent, smooth finish to the meal. Great ambience, attentive service, and lovely Italian flavours.

name: Cedro Scratch Italian & Wine Bar
fullAddress: 14028 US-183 Suite 210, Austin, TX 78717, United States
reviewText: Small mom and pop restaurant in a strip mall. Food is good but not great. Clientel is very nice. Downfalls are No specials and menu rarely changes. Little to no marketing done tl get people in the door. Cheesecake best thing on the menu and the caprese salad. I noticed dishes are often cold or undercooked and sent back. There's only a few tables in the restaurant with rickety tables and chairs, minimal decor. You can tell they didn't have much money to start this restaurant or spruce it up. Management runs around yelling at staff, especially the big girl, instead of helping and supporting them during busy times. This leads to constant staff turnover. Bread is only available by request or with purchase. Pizza tastes bland. I wouldn't recommend this place unless you want carry out. This is coming from a NY Sicilain Italian person with almost 30 yrs. In the Restaurant industry.
